News.title: Twisted paedo ex-cop, 31, to be chemically castrated for raping young children
News.content:
EVIL COP Twisted paedo ex-cop, 31, to be chemically castrated for raping young children







Next

A TWISTED ex-police officer who raped three young children is set to be chemically castrated.

Kedreyon Williams, 31, was found guilty of first-degree rape of a juvenile – and will become the second person in US history to be handed such a punishment.

The paedophile was also found guilty of two other charges, including indecent behaviour with a juvenile and possession of child pornography, WAFB reported.

Prosecutors said on Friday: “If a man takes sexual advantage of a child, then we will take his manhood!





“We hope the families know that justice was served here and have some comfort in knowing he will never be able to prey on any children again.”

Williams was given three life sentences and is due to be castrated.

The rapist abused several minors aged between eight and 11.

Prosecutors said the sexual assaults took place at New Roads fire stations – where he served as a volunteer – as well as at his workplace and at home.



He also recorded videos of the rapes.

The jury deliberated for just 39 minutes before reaching its verdict.

A rape conviction in Louisiana comes with a mandatory life sentence – but prosecutors sought to give him a more permanent punishment.

They eventually settled on chemical castration.



Prosecutors also said: “He performed disgusting acts on children who could not defend themselves.

“He is a child predator, and he deserves exactly what he is getting and more.

“The castration is another layer of punishment for these horrendous crimes.”

The first person to receive such a punishment in the US was believed to be a sex offender from Assumption Parish.

Carrol Ray Clark, 51, pleaded guilty to possession of child pornography and indecent acts with a juvenile in August.



He was handed a 35-year prison sentence on top of the life-changing punishment.

Under Louisiana’s castration code, a person convicted of a severe sex crime for the first time can be ordered to undergo chemical or surgical castration.

An amendment to the law in 2024 allows judges to order surgical castration for aggravated sex offenses against victims under the age of 13.

News.title: PM leaves door open to age of consent law change after Russell Brand conviction
News.content:
SERIOUS CONCERNS PM leaves door open to age of consent law change after Russell Brand conviction







Next

ANDY Burnham has opened the door to tougher age of consent laws in the wake of Russell Brand’s rape conviction.

The PM suggested a crackdown on adults having sex with 16 and 17-year-olds could be considered.

When the allegations against Russell Brand first emerged, one of his alleged victims called for a law change.



Asked if he was considering it, the Prime Minister said: “I’m not going to say at this stage that things are off the table.



“Obviously, we want to have a very, very, detailed consideration of all the issues involved.”

Mr Burnham said a whole series of “important issues” need to be “unpacked” as a result of the revelations at Brand’s criminal trial.

He also praised the “bravery” of Brand’s victims while he was in Dublin for a European summit.



A justice minister had dismissed the idea of staggering consent just a day earlier.

And Downing Street has insisted there are no plans to change the law.

Calls to stagger the age of consent have also ramped up amid allegations that David Walliams preyed on young women. He denies any wrongdoing.

Victims Commissioner Claire Waxman said there needed to be “serious conversations” about changing the law to protect teenagers when there was a big age gap in a sexual relationship.

News.title: Ruthless contract killer, 59, dubbed Russia’s ‘sexiest hitman’ marries Putin’s ex-civil servant, 48, behind bars
News.content:
Next

RUSSIA’S so-called “sexiest hitman” has married for the fourth time, wedding an ex-civil servant who worked for tyrant Vladimir Putin.

Alexei Sherstobitov, 59, has attracted a string of female admirers despite serving a 23-year jail sentence for his brutal gangland murders.



And he has recently found love for the second time while locked up, making Yulia Gvozdetskaya, 48, his fourth wife.

The cold-blooded contract killer was once the most notorious murderer of Moscow‘s underworld gang members.



But the “handsome assassin” appears to have focused on finding love in his time behind bars.

Sherstobitov married his new bride just three years before his planned release.

Former civil servant Yulia once worked as a senior specialist for Russia‘s state pension system.

The mum-of-two is now employed by a major Moscow construction company.



A woman of the same name as the former civil servant was fined for owning an illegally modified air rifle.

Ruthless killer Sherstobitov once worked for the notorious Orekhovo-Medvedkovo mafia empire as a so-called “in-house assassin”.



He was commissioned to take out the gang’s enemy’s after the fall of the Soviet Union.

His most famous kill was powerful underworld king Otari Kvantrishvili, 46, who he gunned down in Moscow in April 1994.

Another of Sherstobitov’s confirmed kills was ex-KGB spy turned gang kingpin Grigory Gusyatinsky, who was murdered in 1995.

The allegedly attractive assassin was reportedly once ordered to kill billionaire Boris Berezovsky with a Tigr sniper rifle.



But at the last minute his higher ups commanded him to abort the execution mission.

Sworn Putin enemy Berezovsky later died in still-unexplained circumstances while living in exile in England.

Sherstobitov was said to be a master of disguise, owning an incredible array of wigs, fake moustaches and beards.

He is also said to have owned an arsenal of umbrellas with needle-like bladed tips designed to stab or poison victims.

The hitman threw authorities so many false leads that cops thought Lyosha the Soldier, as he was known, did not exist, believing instead that killings attributed to him must have been the work of several hitmen.



But it was Sherstobitov’s romantic pursuits that led to his eventual capture.

Another gangster reported driven mad with jealousy after Sherstobitov “stole” his fiancée, leaked the killer’s identity to police.

The assassin was convicted of 12 murders and attempted murders, but still managed to court female attraction while imprisoned.

He had already been married twice when he was jailed, and he wed glamorous Marina Sosnenko, then 31, behind bars in 2016.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The pair divorced in 2020 before he met his new Russian bride.



Russian reports say his new bride wiped her social media accounts before the jailhouse wedding.

News.title: Man in his 20s dies after trying to cross English Channel in small boat as body found on beach
News.content:
BOAT TRAGEDY Man in his 20s dies after trying to cross English Channel in small boat as body found on beach







Next

A MAN in his 20s has died after attempting a small boat crossing on the English Channel, French coastguards have reported.

A body was found on Sainte-Cecile beach near the coastal town of Le Touquet on Saturday morning, authorities said.

A French rescue patrol had been monitoring migrants boarding a “makeshift vessel” at the beach.



The vessel was reportedly stopped by French authorities, who concluded that no one was in the water following a “thorough sweep”.



A small craft had been sent out to check the waters, as land-based units surveyed the coastline.

The coastguard reported that the boarding had been “chaotic”, with five men treated for hypothermia by firefighters.

Tragically, the young man’s body was located this morning.



“Following the operation, at approximately 08:00 (09:00 GMT) the body of a man in his twenties was discovered on the beach,” the coastguard reported.

It added that an investigation will be opened to determine the “circumstances surrounding the incident”.

The latest records show that 903 migrants have arrived in the UK by small boat in the past week.

An additional 624 migrants were prevented from making the crossing, data shows.



It comes as Belgian police claimed migrants are using a 325-mile stretch of the Channel coast spanning Belgian and French shorelines to launch smalls boats to the UK.

The warning in late October came a day after a video emerged, showing migrants using a “custom” craft – sporting the Kurdish flag – to put themselves out to sea in Belgium as cops stood by.

News.title: Four-month old baby dies in Glasgow home as cops launch probe into tragedy
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

BABY TRAGEDY Four-month old baby dies in Glasgow home as cops launch probe into tragedy







Next

A FOUR-month-old baby has died in an unexplained tragedy in a home in Glasgow, sparking an investigation by police.

Emergency services were called to the home in Milton, north Glasgow, after the alarm was raised on Wednesday, November 11.

A “significant presence” of police officers and forensic teams have remained at the site of the tragedy since then.

A source said: “A baby has passed away. It’s tragic, very sad.





“Police and forensics have been there for a number of days now. They’ve been taking photographs of the garden and outside on the street.

“There was a very, very significant presence of forensics in white suits. They there from morning to night.

“Officers have also carried out door to door enquiries. So, it’s been a big operation.

“The police have not been saying much. Obviously it’s something very sensitive.”



A Police Scotland spokesperson said: “On Wednesday, 11 November, 2026, we received a report of the death of a four-month-old baby within a property in Milton, Glasgow.

“Enquiries are ongoing to establish the circumstances.”

More to follow.

News.title: Nurse, 65, who spent 13 years in Italian jail after being wrongly convicted of neighbour’s murder is finally FREED
News.content:
MISCARRIAGE OF JUSTICE Nurse, 65, who spent 13 years in Italian jail after being wrongly convicted of neighbour’s murder is finally FREED







Next

A NURSE who spent 13 years behind bars after a wrongful conviction for her neighbour’s gruesome murder has finally been freed.

Monica Busetto, 65, had been sentenced to 25 years in jail for the killing of Taffi Pamio, 87, at her flat in Mestre, Italy.



The pensioner was found strangled and stabbed 40 times with four kitchen knives on December 20, 2012.

Such was the violence of the attack that cops found two of the blades still embedded in her body when they arrived.



Monica, who lived across the corridor, was arrested in January 2014 and denied the crime from the outset.

Nonetheless, she was sentenced to a quarter-century behind bars on a flimsy piece of evidence that eventually helped overturn her conviction.

Investigators seized a necklace from Monica’s apartment and a forensic lab in Rome found minuscule bits of Taffi’s DNA on it.

An initial geneticist, Luciana Caenazzo, had found nothing on that same item.

But the case should’ve been blown open when another woman, 81-year-old Francesca Vianello, was later found murdered in a similar manner in 2016.

The perpetrator, Susanna Milly Lazzarini, confessed to killing Taffi a few weeks later.



But despite claiming she acted alone during the first three interviews with police, she implicated Monica on the fourth.

She was deemed an unreliable witness due to the change in her story, and appeal judges upheld Monica’s conviction.

Lazzarini, meanwhile, was acquitted of Taffi’s murder.

Monica’s lawyers sought a review of this discrepancy two years ago, but the Court of Appeal in Trento refused.

The breakthrough would eventually come in the form of a family photo album.



Journalists Max Andreetta and Nicola Remisceg obtained photographs from the victim’s relatives that showed Taffi wearing her necklace in the 1980s.

It was revealed to be a longer piece of jewellery – around 28 inches – than the one found in Monica’s flat, which measured just 23 inches.

Not only was it significantly shorter, the chain was also a completely different design.

This was the very point that Monica’s lawyers, Alessandro Doglioni and Stefano Busetto, had argued from the outset.

The trace of Taffi’s DNA was also revealed to be from contamination with other blood-stained pieces of evidence.



The Trento Prosecutor General’s Office insisted that protocols had been followed correctly.

However, Monica’s conviction and 25-year sentence were overturned, and she was released from Montorio prison, near Verona, on Friday.

After her release, she told Rai: “I didn’t expect it, but I never gave up hope because I knew that one day – sooner or later – the truth would come to light.

Speaking about her newfound freedom, she said: “Today is an extremely happy day for me.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“To see my family again, the people who love me and have always stood by me… It feels like a dream to look around, breathe the air and see my Venice again.”



Her lawyer Busetto said: “Now, we need to say to this woman: sorry for the delay.”

News.title: M62 closed after horror crash as police chase suspected stolen car – as man, 18, arrested
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

HORROR CRASH M62 closed after horror crash as police chase suspected stolen car – as man, 18, arrested







Next

A MAJOR motorway has shut after a suspected stolen car crashed during a high-speed police chase.

Traffic has ground to a halt along the M62 between J26 near Cleckheaton and J27 for Birstall in the eastbound direction.

Cops were called to Wilson Avenue in Swinton at around 10.30am today, following reports of a vehicle theft.

A police helicopter tracked down the vehicle on the M60 but it failed to stop.





Cops then pursued it onto the M62, where it collided with Greater Manchester Police’s tacticial unit cars, the force said.

Photos show the car overturned as emergency vehicles surround the site.

No serious injuries were reported.

An 18-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of theft of a motor vehicle, cops said.



Motorists are reporting lengthy delays in the area, with queues stretching back miles past J25 for Brighouse.

Several players heading to a match between FC Farsley and Berry Brow have been stuck in the tailbacks.

FC Farsley posted: “Not quite the matchday start we had planned! A number of Berry Brow’s players and their manager appear to have taken an unexpected detour and are currently stuck in standstill traffic on the M62!”

The force said: “Officers pursued the vehicle on to the M62 working alongside officers from West Yorkshire Police.



“The offending vehicle then collided with GMP TAU vehicles, between Junction 26 and Junction 27 on the M62, causing damage to them.”

News.title: Female university lecturer, 30, arrested after ‘sexually abusing’ schoolboy, 15, at her apartment
News.content:
TWISTED MISS Female university lecturer, 30, arrested after ‘sexually abusing’ schoolboy, 15, at her apartment







Next

A LECTURER has been arrested on suspicion of sexually abusing a 15-year-old school boy at her flat.

Award-winning Russian teacher Daria Khurda, 30, allegedly engaged in “sexual acts” with a teen student.



The teacher has been detained on suspicion of carrying out a relationship with a child for more than a year.

Khurda is a senior lecturer at St Petersburg’s prestigious National Research University Higher School of Economics.





She also teaches English and Spanish at leading high schools in the area.

Police said the boy was just 15 when they first got together.

Her alleged victim’s mum reportedly filed the complaint.

Investigators claimed Khurda met with the teen between March 2024 to December 2025 in her apartment on Svetlanovsky Prospekt.



Law enforcement sources told 112: “A criminal case has been opened on suspicion of indecent acts involving a minor.

“Police are investigating other potential incidents.”

Baza reported that authorities are “determining whether there are any other victims”.



Khurda teaches in her elite university’s public administration department.

She was recently handed an award recognising her as “one of the best” teachers in St Petersburg.

It comes after a disgraced drama teacher who confessed to having a sick relationship with her teen student was jailed in Sydney this week.

Ella Clements, 25, collapsed in shock when she was cuffed on school grounds after abusing her 15-year-old male student last year.

And another disgraced Sydney teacher was jailed last month for having sex with a 17-year-old and assaulting a 16-year-old.



Tayla Lee Brailey, 32, admitted to having sex with a 17-year-old student in his car during a school day and sexually touching the younger student in a classroom.

The twisted former PE teacher bawled her eyes out and hugged her parents as she was taken into custody at Parramatta District Court.

She was sentenced to 15 months in prison after pleading guilty to five offences, including sexual intercourse with a 17-year-old and sexually touching a 16-year-old.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Both of the children were in her care at a school in southwest Sydney at the time of the offences.

News.title: Tenerife boss claims ban for keeper involved in fatal Jesus de Miguel clash is 'too light'
News.content:
Tenerife boss claims ban for keeper involved in fatal Jesus de Miguel clash is 'too light'

Jesus Owono, the goalkeeper involved in the collision which led to the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel, has been banned for 12 matches by a disciplinary committee

View 2 Images Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games (Image: Getty)

The manager of Tenerife says the 12-game ban given to goalkeeper Jesus Owono following the collision that led to Jesus de Miguel's death seems "a bit light".

‌



Owono collided heavily with De Miguel in mid-air during the Spanish Segunda Division match between Tenerife and FC Andorra at the start of this month. The forward, 30, tragically died the following day, sending Spanish football into mourning.

Owono was sent off as a result of the collision and was banned for 12 games by a disciplinary committee on Friday.

Alvaro Cervera, the head coach of Tenerife, has commented on the length of Owono's ban, which was the maximum penalty available to the disciplinary committee given they could only consider the offence on the pitch rather than the tragic consequences of the collision.

While he feels the ban is light, he also acknowledged that the regulations do not "specifically account for what happened". "I think that, just as in other areas of life, there are rules or laws that must be followed," said Cervera, whose team will play for the first time since De Miguel's death on Sunday against Ceuta.

"Since the current regulations don't specifically account for what happened, I believe they have simply adhered to the rules and imposed the number of matches permitted by the regulations.

"Anything else I might say would just be my own personal opinion, which I'll keep to myself. It might seem a bit light when compared to other cases, but in reality, I don't think the rules allow for anything else."

View 2 Images Jesus de Miguel died aged 30 following a collision with the goalkeeper during a game earlier this month (Image: CD TENERIFE/AFP via Getty Images)

The disciplinary committee shared that the referee's report said Owono was sent off for "violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play".

The 25-year-old released a statement following De Miguel's death, which read: "These are the most difficult days of my life. I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to process what has happened.

"I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many questions to address.

"I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the ⁠pain we are experiencing. Rest in ⁠peace, Jesus."

News.title: Man, 21, arrested after Met Police officer stabbed in neck in Romford
News.content:
Man, 21, arrested after Met Police officer stabbed in neck in Romford

The incident took place as emergency services were called to welfare concerns at an address on Mawney Road in Romford, east London

View Image Police at the scene in the Mawney Road area of Romford (Image: Facebook/Imma DaLleshi)

A Metropolitan Police officer has been stabbed in the neck, with a man arrested on suspicion of attempted murder.

The incident took place as emergency services were called to welfare concerns at an address on Mawney Road in Romford, east London, shortly after 4.15pm yesterday. On arrival, officers were met by a man aged 21 threatening them with a "sharp object".

One of the officers was then attacked and taken to hospital as a result. The Met said his condition is not life-threatening or life-changing and he has since been discharged.

A male suspect was arrested at the scene and remains in custody. A crime scene was in place last night, with footage seen by MyLondon showing a number of police cars and ambulances blocking Mawney Road near the junction with Olive Street.

The suspect male was arrested at the scene and remains in custody.

A crime scene remained in place last night as investigators work to gather evidence. Footage seen by MyLondon shows a number of police cars and ambulances blocking Mawney Road near the junction with Olive Street.

A statement from the Metropolitan Police reads: "At around 16:16hrs on Friday, 13 November, police were called to an address in Mawney Road, Romford following concerns for the welfare of a man. On arrival, the 21-year-old man threatened police with a sharp object before assaulting an officer.

"The officer was taken to hospital with a stab wound to their neck. His injuries have since been assessed as non life-threatening or life-changing and he has been discharged.

"The man was arrested at the scene on suspicion of attempted murder and remains in police custody. A crime scene remains in place."

News.title: Man, 21, stabbed to death by Tottenham park pictured and murder probe launched
News.content:
Man, 21, stabbed to death by Tottenham park pictured and murder probe launched

Emergency services were called to reports of the attack on Lordship Lane in Tottenham, north London, with a police cordon still in place today

View 2 Images A tent and police cordon on Lordship Lane this morning (Image: Twitter/X/@ediz1975)

A murder investigation has been launched after a 21-year-old man was stabbed to death outside a park in London.

‌



‌



Emergency services were called to reports of the attack on Lordship Lane, near Lordship Recreation Ground, in Tottenham, north London, at around 6pm yesterday. The victim was treated by paramedics at the scene but died from his injuries.

‌



The victim has been named by the Metropolitan Police as Thomas Oduro from Tottenham and his family are being supported by officers. No arrests have yet been made, as detectives continue to carry out enquiries.

‌



MyLondon reports a team of forensic officers were spotted at the scene overnight, with a large cordon still in place near the park's entrance earlier today. A police tent was also seen on the road, just metres from the park gates.

View 2 Images Thomas Oduro

‌



Officers have now urged anyone holding any information about the incident to contact them. Detective Chief Inspector Phil Clarke said this afternoon: "Thomas’s family have suffered a devastating loss. Our thoughts are with them, and they continue to be supported by specialist officers.

"Enquiries continue at the scene and there will be an increased police presence in the area over the coming days. As part of our investigation, I’m urging anyone who was in the area of Lordship Recreation Ground around 18:00hrs on Friday, or who has information which may be relevant, to speak to officers or get in touch as soon as possible."

Article continues below

Anyone with information is urged to contact police via 101, quoting CAD 5439/13NOV26. Alternatively, call Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Horror crash on M62 shuts motorway after police chase with heavy delays
News.content:
Horror crash on M62 shuts motorway after police chase with heavy delays

Police were called to Wilson Avenue, Swinton following reports of a vehicle theft - the car overturned after it was pursued by police and then collided with Greater Manchester Police’s tactical unit car

View Image The M62 has been shut down

A major UK motorway was closed after a crash involving multiple vehicles. The M62 was shut following a crash after a high speed police chase.

Police attended Wilson Avenue, Swinton, at around 10.30am following reports of a vehicle theft. The car overturned after it was pursued by police and then collided with Greater Manchester Police’s tactical unit cars.

Emergency services vehicles quickly surrounded the site with traffic halted along the M62 between J26 near Cleckheaton and J27 for Birstall in the eastbound direction, reports The Express.

Greater Manchester Police said in a statement: "Officers pursued the vehicle on to the M62 working alongside officers from West Yorkshire Police.

"The offending vehicle then collided with GMP TAU vehicles between Junction 26 and Junction 27 on the M62, causing damage to them."

The vehicle was pursued by a helicopter but failed to stop. An 18-year-old man has been arrested.

National Highways said as of 4.30pm on Saturday that 30-minute delays remain after all lanes had reopened.

News.title: 'Failing to fix Neets crisis will be a disaster for youngsters' life chances and economy'
News.content:
'Failing to fix Neets crisis will be a disaster for youngsters' life chances and economy'

OPINION: GMB General Secretary Gary Smith writes for The Mirror as Alan Milburn prepares to publish his report into the almost million young people classed as 'Neets' - those not in employment, education, or training

View 3 Images Failing to fix the Neets crisis will be a disaster for our economy and entire country, says GMB's Gary Smith (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Right now, we have a million young people not in employment, education or training. Scarcely believable in 2026. If we don’t fix it, it’ll be a disaster for their life chances, and the prospects for our economy and entire country.

‌



‌



Another huge challenge facing us right now is how to keep the nation safe in more dangerous times. Central to this is ensuring we have the manufacturing industry to deliver the security and resilience that is so desperately needed.

‌



We can solve these two problems together if we are prepared to make the right choices. For too long, the UK has been handing out key government contracts – in defence, infrastructure, or other key industries – to overseas producers, where British taxpayers’ money is creating jobs and boosting economies elsewhere instead of here at home.

‌



It’s madness. This government has made it clear this will stop.The commitment to UK shipbuilding – in yards from Rosyth to Appledore, Belfast to Barrow, Aldershot to Plymouth, the Mersey to the Tyne – can be transformative.

The Chancellor has said the same for all kinds of other projects. While procurement might not sound like the most exciting topic, if the government chooses to buy British, it can make all the difference. Firms are able to plan for the years ahead and develop the workforce they need for it. Their suppliers will also look to train and employ more staff.

Should young people lose access to DWP benefits? READ MORE :

View 3 Images GMB General Secretary, Gary Smith (Image: Reach Commissioned)

‌



I’ve seen the benefits of such an approach when going around the country meeting GMB members in their workplaces. The thousands of new apprentices in Barrow, who are able to earn as they learn, are training to build the submarines that will help keep our defences strong. They are a vital part of a wider success story for their hometown, one that is bringing back jobs and creating prosperity in an industrial community that had been failed by Westminster.

The choice to nationalise and protect Scunthorpe’s steelworks means more young people can be optimistic about their future there too. And more of the country’s key infrastructure projects – whether railway lines, building hospitals, or roads – will be able to rely on UK supply chains, protected from shocks in global markets.

‌



Valuing these and other core industries, and using government procurement to keep a pipeline of orders, will help deliver good, union jobs that pay well in working-class towns. At the same time, we will be training our next generation of engineers, welders, electricians and boilermakers. That’s a future we can all get behind.

Reform nursery dummies

In Barnsley, a Reform-led council is trying to slash nursery workers’ pensions. These low-paid women do so much for children and families in the heartland of our once mighty coal industry. They deserve better.

‌



So, while Reform talk big about fighting for the working class, in town halls they are showing their true colours. Attacking workers and their livelihoods. These proud women are standing united. They remind me so much of the Glasgow women who battled for equal pay – sparking others in Birmingham, Brighton, Leeds, Swansea and across the country to fight for the wages stolen from them over so many years. Women are, still, system-atically undervalued and underpaid. But try and come for a GMB woman’s pay or pension? Don’t even think about it.

Trump's Iran war and Putin's invasion led skyrocketing bills

Trump’s war in Iran and Putin’s invasion of Ukraine led to skyrocketing energy bills. We are too reliant on overseas energy sources. The Tories closed our gas storage facilities: a terrible, short-sighted decision. With investment in extra gas capacity and other home-grown energy sources, we can protect ourselves from these shocks.

‌



View 3 Images 'Trump’s war in Iran and Putin’s invasion of Ukraine led to skyrocketing energy bills' (Image: Getty Images)

Change is being delivered at Amazon – and about time too

Jeff Bezos may enjoy jetting off to space, but he wasn’t smiling when Amazon staff joined GMB. Low pay and poor working conditions mean many workers want a union to represent them.

Article continues below

The new package of workers’ rights delivered by the government means they may finally get what they want. Change is being delivered at Amazon – and about time too.

News.title: Water minister issues 'small habits' advice as severe droughts continue post-heatwaves
News.content:
Water minister issues 'small habits' advice as severe droughts continue post-heatwaves

Emma Hardy said Brits don’t need to be worried about water shortages but that they should reflect on the small and minor changes that help us all collectively save water

View 3 Images Public water supplies remain under pressure in some drought-affected areas despite good rainfall in October (Image: Getty Images)

The Water Minister has urged people to think about changing “small habits and behaviours” amid ongoing drought issues after this summer’s heatwaves.

‌



‌



Emma Hardy said Brits don’t need to be “worried” about water shortages but that they should reflect on the “small and minor changes that help us all collectively save water”.

‌



In an interview with The Mirror, she said she is aware the public find it “infuriating” to be asked to save water when they then see leaks at the bottom of their street, adding that there is also a “huge push” for water companies to stop wastage.

‌



Among changes, Ms Hardy said people should consider using the eco button on their dishwashers or washing machine, turning off the tap when they brush their teeth, and ensuring they use the correct flush button on the toilet. She also said some water firms are giving out free water butts to encourage people to collect their rainwater which they can use to water their gardens in the summer.

Driest spell in more than 100 years leaves parts of UK in severe drought - what it means for households READ MORE :

Urgent water warning as severe drought declared in 6 UK counties - full list READ MORE :

View 3 Images Emma Hardy said people should consider using the eco button on their dishwashers or washing machine (Image: Katielee Arrowsmith / SWNS)

Pointing to Ofwat’s Let’s Save Water campaign, which launched in May, Ms Hardy said: “We're asking people to do really small changes like turn the tap off when you're brushing your teeth, think about how much water that you're using. Use the eco button when you're doing your washing - for your dishwasher, for your washing machine.

‌



“I mean, really small and minor changes that help us all collectively save water because we've just had the driest summer in a century. We are entering into winter now. We need in some areas of the country 120% of average long-term rainfall to make sure that we start next year out of drought.

"There is a possibility that we will next year enter into drought in more areas of the country if we continue to see what we're seeing more recently, which is these longer, drier, hotter summers, so I do think it's something that we need to not worry about, but we should care about and we should sort of reflect.”

‌



Asked if she has changed any of her habits, the minister added: " I've definitely started saving water for watering my plants. I've recently moved house, so I need to get a new water butt installed on my drain pipes as well. It's been quite interesting because before I got this brief, water use wasn't something I thought about. It wasn't something I really considered, and I spend so much time thinking about water, it has made me sort of change and think a bit differently."

View 3 Images Emma Hardy said she's started thinking about her water usage differently since becoming Water Minister (Image: Andy Commins / Daily Mirror)

‌



According to the latest official update, severe drought remains in parts of Cornwall, Devon, Dorset, Somerset, and East and West Sussex. England needs at least 120% of average rainfall over the next six months for the entire country to be out of drought by next spring.

Public water supplies remain under pressure in some drought-affected areas despite good rainfall in October. Reservoir and groundwater storage continue to decline for several water companies.

Article continues below

Since becoming PM, Andy Burnham has vowed to repair Britain’s broken water industry, which has seen increasing leakages, sewage spills and surging bills. The PM in September announced he will bring in new laws to allow the Government to take back control of water as he hit out at privatisation under Margaret Thatcher.

He told The Mirror at the time: “Water, housing, energy and transport are the essentials of everyday life and the everyday economy. We rely on them. We pay for them. And we should have more power over them.”
