News.title: AI fuels fastest economic growth in two years
News.content:
The Prime Minister and the Chancellor should not claim credit for the AI-fuelled expansion of Britain’s economy in the third quarter, a think tank said.

Julian Jessop, economics fellow at the Institute of Economic Affairs, said the 0.7pc expansion in the economy was “a tribute to the resilience of the private sector in the face of the energy shock and policy headwinds”.

He said: “This resilience is despite rather than because of anything the Government has done. In particular, the persistent weakens of the construction sector underlines the failure of flagship policies to boost housebuilding and infrastructure spending.

“The Government’s clumsy interventions are also continuing to add to labour and housing costs, including rents. Instead, the key driver of growth and business optimism has been the rollout of AI. This is an area that the Government has not got round to messing up, though that may yet be coming.

“In the meantime, the Government is still borrowing more than expected and the labour market remains weak.

“The full impact of higher inflation and higher interest rates has also yet to be felt. Early surveys for the fourth quarter already show that consumer confidence, retail spending, private sector hiring and housing market activity are all starting to slide again.

“2026 will still be a year when the economy performed much better than expected – at least in terms of GDP. But the new year will start with further increases in energy bills and high levels of job insecurity, which will matter far more to most people.”

News.title: Bird flu viruses ‘gaining function’ through natural mixing, warn scientists
News.content:
The bird flu virus’ resurgence began with an 11-year-old. In February 2023, the schoolgirl was admitted to a hospital in Phnom Penh with severe pneumonia – within a day, she was dead.

Tests soon revealed that she had contracted avian influenza: Cambodia hadn’t reported a human case of bird flu since 2014, but the hiatus was over. Since then, 39 more people have been infected and 15 have died in the Southeast Asian country – a case fatality rate of roughly 40 per cent.

Researchers have been scratching their heads as to why, after nine years, this particular stain of H5N1 suddenly started jumping from birds to people again. The strain or clade called 2.3.2.1 had been circulating for almost a decade without spilling into humans. What changed?

Now, a paper in Emerging Infectious Diseases offers clues.

Scientists say the apparent rise in human cases has coincided with the virus gaining new genetic material and, potentially, new powers of infection, from a second flu virus via a process known as “reassortment”.

Sports.title: England star reveals moment he secured Champions League transfer only for Jose Mourinho to rip it up
Sports.content:
Next

JOSE MOURINHO denied ex-England ace Glen Johnson a Champions League move while in charge of Chelsea by TEARING UP the deal in front of him.

Johnson, 42, spent four years at Stamford Bridge – two of which were under Mourinho, 63, during the Special One’s first stint with the Blues.



The former full-back didn’t get to play too much after the Portuguese tactician arrived in 2004 but still had a great relationship with him, which consisted of some “phenomenal conversations”.

Johnson told SunSport on behalf of SeatPick: “I have some great memories of working under Jose Mourinho at Chelsea. We were winning all the time, including the Premier League and League Cup double in 2004/05.



“Winning trophies always helps with fond memories, and our confidence was at an all-time high, we were one of the best teams the Premier League had ever seen. Jose and I had loads of phenomenal conversations, but one in particular stands out.”

Mourinho told Johnson he would have to go out on loan in order to get more minutes as he didn’t figure into his first-team plans.



The ex-Manchester United boss, though, insisted the former defender would have to join a Champions League club that would offer him opportunities at top level.

The ex-England international obeyed the current Real Madrid boss and secured a deal with then European giants Lyon, who ruled French football before Nasser Al-Khelaifi took over at Paris Saint-Germain in 2011.

The Liverpool hero went to Mourinho’s office to inform him of his imminent move to France with the contract in hand, but the ex-Tottenham boss would have none of it.

So much so that the Chelsea legend actually grabbed the papers and tore them to shreds before telling him he was staying put.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Johnson added: “He wanted me to go out on loan to get more game time as I wasn’t playing too much at Chelsea. But he wanted it to be a Champions League club, if I could find one, so I could get proper experience.

“So I went out and found a loan at Lyon, who at the time were a huge deal, it was in the middle of that period where they won Ligue 1 seven times in a row.

“The deal was done, and I was only young, so it was a big deal for me to get the offer. However, I went to tell Jose, showed him the deal, and he just tore it up in front of me.”



Johnson believes this was simply a “test of character” because Mourinho never thought he “had the courage” to leave his comfort zone.

The former right-back, who did go out on loan to Portsmouth in 2006 before joining the Pompey the following season on a permanent basis, is adamant he passed “with flying colours”.

Johnson said: “I don’t think he ever thought I had the courage to go out and get myself such a good deal at my age.

“I think it was supposed to be a test of character, which I must have passed with flying colours because he just ripped it up and told me I was staying.

“I didn’t have a choice. But I think he respected me more after that, and he started picking me more often.”

Sports.title: Gudjon Thordarson dead aged 71: Former Championship manager and Wembley winner passes away as clubs send condolences
Sports.content:
Next

FORMER Stoke City manager Gudjon Thordarson has died aged 71 following a battle with Parkinson’s disease.

The Icelandic coach, who guided the Potters to two famous Wembley and play-off triumphs, passed away on Friday morning.



Thordarson was diagnosed with Parkinson’s in 2023 and had recently spoken openly about his deteriorating health.

He had been using a wheelchair but remained hopeful of recovering enough to enjoy playing golf again.



The former Iceland national team boss is fondly remembered at Stoke, where he played a major role in transforming the club’s fortunes.

He helped bring together an Icelandic consortium that took control of the Potters in November 1999 before replacing Gary Megson as manager.



Thordarson made an immediate impact, guiding Stoke to victory over Bristol City in the 2000 Auto Windscreens Shield final at Wembley.

Goals from Graham Kavanagh and Peter Thorne secured the trophy in front of a crowd of around 75,000.

But promotion proved more difficult, with Stoke suffering successive play-off semi-final defeats against Gillingham and Walsall.

Their fortunes finally changed in 2002 when Thordarson masterminded a dramatic play-off victory over Cardiff City before beating Brentford in the final.



The triumph secured Stoke’s promotion to the second tier and sparked wild celebrations across the Potteries.

However, Thordarson was controversially sacked just days after leading the club to promotion following a breakdown in his relationship with the board.

He later managed Barnsley, Notts County and Crewe Alexandra before eventually returning to Iceland to continue his coaching career.

Despite his health struggles, Thordarson remained passionate about football and took pride in seeing several of his former players become managers.

Sports.title: Portugal retire Cristiano Ronaldo’s number 7 shirt in never-before-seen move
Sports.content:
Next

PORTUGAL have retired Cristiano Ronaldo’s iconic No7 shirt in an extraordinary tribute to the football legend – without stopping another player from wearing the number.

The Portuguese Football Federation has announced a permanent redesign of the famous shirt number following Ronaldo’s retirement from international football earlier this month, bringing an end to his remarkable 23-year career with the national team.



Rather than scrapping the number altogether, Portugal have changed the physical appearance of the seven on their shirts, ensuring the version worn by Ronaldo will never be used again.

The federation announced: “From today’s game with Denmark, the national team’s number seven shirt, which belonged to Cristiano Ronaldo for so many years, will have a different graphic design, with a different number seven.”



It added: “This is another way of immortalising the meaning of such a special number and paying tribute to the legacy it represents.”

The original design will be preserved as a permanent reminder of the former Manchester United and Real Madrid superstar’s extraordinary achievements.

The unusual decision also allows Portugal to comply with UEFA and FIFA regulations, which require international teams to use consecutive shirt numbers during major competitions.

Countries cannot simply retire a number in the same way as clubs, with Argentina previously encountering similar difficulties when attempting to honour Diego Maradona.

And former Manchester City youngster Carlos Forbs, 22, is set to become the first player to wear Portugal’s redesigned No7 when they face Denmark in Saturday’s Nations League clash in Braga.

The Club Brugge winger has already worn the number for his country in Ronaldo’s absence.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Portugal have also organised a special tribute for their former captain, with every player set to walk onto the pitch wearing a No7 shirt before kick-off.

Supporters will then be invited to honour Ronaldo with a standing ovation in the seventh minute, with both gestures receiving UEFA approval.

Ronaldo, 41, announced his international retirement on November 5 after a disagreement with Portugal manager Jorge Jesus.

The Al-Nassr striker brought the curtain down on a career that began against Kazakhstan in August 2003, finishing with a world-record 234 international appearances and 146 goals.

His greatest achievement came at Euro 2016, when he captained Portugal to their first major international trophy with victory over hosts France in the final.



Ronaldo also helped his country win the Nations League in 2019 and 2025, establishing himself as one of the most successful international footballers in history.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo, 41, takes up new sport in first international break since retirement from Portugal team
Sports.content:
“The day has come back for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our national team.

“I never felt it belonged to me alone. But for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.

“Today, the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision. Because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart.

“A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.

“When I look back at everything with the national team, I don’t just see the matches, goals, records or trophies.

“I see people. I see the Portuguese people living abroad who, for 90 minutes, felt a little closer to home.

“I see millions of Portuguese people I have never met but who became part of my life.

“Because at the end of the day, football is so much bigger than a game. Football is about people.

“Throughout my entire career with the national team, I always pushed myself beyond my limits.

“I wanted to win. I wanted to be better. I wanted to make history.

“I always demanded the most of myself. I always wanted more. I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this shirt.

“There were perfect afternoons and evenings, there were victories I will never forget, there were defeats that are still difficult for me to recall.

“I also failed, I also suffered, there were also moments when I was unable to give the Portuguese people what they so desired. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

“Over these years I’ve learned some very simple things. Goals fade, trophies stay in museums, records eventually get broken. But there’s something time can never erase: the place we occupy in people’s hearts.

“If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a difficult moment, or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it. Because being Portuguese is also about that.

“We suffer together, we rise together, we believe again. Portugal will always need young people who dream, players who never give up, new generations who believe it’s possible to reach where no one has reached before. Because a country that continues to create new heroes is a country that never stops believing in itself.

“To my team-mates, I want to say a special word. Thank you for every run, for every hug, for every discussion, for every silence before stepping onto the field.

“For every victory we celebrated together and for every defeat that made us stronger. I had the privilege of being your captain, but no captain walks alone. And you are part of my story.

“To all the coaches, managers, doctors, physiotherapists, kit men, staff, and so many people who have worked with me over these years, my thanks. Many of you never appeared in the photographs, but without you, none of these photographs would have been possible.

“To my family, thank you for sharing this dream with me. Thank you for understanding my absences, the sacrifices, and the times when the national team had to take up space that also belonged to you. If I’ve come this far, it’s because we’ve always been hand in hand.

“And to the Portuguese people, to all the Portuguese scattered around the world, I want to say one last thing.

“There’s an image I will always carry with me: the moment the national anthem begins. I look around, I see my teammates, I see the stands, I see children, mothers, fathers and grandparents, I see Portuguese people who have come from so far away just to be there.

“And during those minutes we cease to be different. There are no clubs, no colours, no classes, no professions, no opinions. There is only one passion: Portugal.

“I will carry this feeling with me for the rest of my life. Today my journey on the field with the national team ends. I leave with my head held high, proud of the path I have taken and with the awareness that I gave everything I had for Portugal.

“But I will never stop being one of you.

“I will continue to suffer, to thrill, and to celebrate every victory for Portugal with all my heart.

“I’ve spent my life working to be the best player in the world. Today I realise that the greatest victory was having earned the right to represent the best country in the world.

“Thank you for these 23 years. Thank you for believing in me. Thank you for allowing me to live a dream that began when I was just a boy in Madeira, chasing after a ball.

“The number 7 jersey will stay with me; the pride of having worn it will be mine forever. Portugal will always be a part of me.

“Farewell, Cristiano Ronaldo.”

Sports.title: Italy goes Ronaldinho mad as Brazil legend prepares for sensational return at the age of 46 with Serie C side Ravenna
Sports.content:
Next

ITALY has gone Ronaldinho mad as the Brazilian legend prepares to make his sensational return to professional football at the age of 46.

The former Barcelona and AC Milan superstar is set to play his first competitive match in 11 years when Italian third-tier side Ravenna host fierce local rivals Forli on Sunday.



And excitement surrounding his comeback has reached extraordinary levels, with Sky Sport Italia announcing special television coverage usually reserved for some of the biggest matches in European football.

The broadcaster will set up a pitchside studio at Ravenna’s Stadio Bruno Benelli, with transfer expert Gianluca Di Marzio joined by special guests. Commentators Antonio Nucera and Lorenzo Minotti will provide live coverage of the Serie C clash, which kicks off at 4.30pm UK time.



Sky will even introduce a dedicated ‘Ronaldinho Cam’, following the Brazilian’s every movement from his pre-match warm-up to his appearance on the pitch.

Italian commentator Fabio Caressa will also feature in a special introduction, while fans in Britain can watch the match for free on Sky Sports Football’s YouTube channel.

Speaking to CBS, Ronaldinho said: “I’m very happy to be back after 11 years. Ravenna is a great club and I am really excited. Today I do a lot of footy volley. I’m training differently and we will see what happens.”

Ronaldinho fever has swept through Ravenna, with the club erecting a temporary 1,800-seat stand named R10 in honour of the legendary playmaker.

The Brazilian star posted a video of himself doing an outrageous skill, captioning it: “People will say this is AI haha!”

The additional seating in the stadium will increase the stadium’s capacity to around 7,000, while tickets for the eagerly anticipated derby have been selling for as much as £130.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The World Cup winner arrived in Italy on Friday to a hero’s welcome and is expected to start Sunday’s match despite having just one training session with his new team-mates.

Ravenna boss Andrea Mandorlini has confirmed the Brazilian will feature in attack, although the pair will decide how long he remains on the pitch.

Ronaldinho’s remarkable return follows his decision to join Ravenna in June, when he signed for the club and subsequently acquired a minority ownership stake.

The Italian side had been purchased in 2024 by businessman Ignazio Cipriani and investment partner Black Duck, with the Brazilian becoming part of their ambitious project.

Cipriani, who grew up idolising Ronaldinho, insisted the move was about much more than publicity, with the club hoping to climb through the Italian divisions.



The former Ballon d’Or winner has also taken on an ambassadorial role, using his global profile to attract new supporters and investment.

Ronaldinho enjoyed a glittering career with Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona and AC Milan, winning the Champions League in 2006 and the Ballon d’Or in 2005.

He was also part of Brazil’s World Cup-winning squad in 2002 before playing his final competitive game for Fluminense in September 2015 and officially retiring in 2018.

But the 46-year-old has one final landmark in his sights after ending his previous playing career on 299 professional goals.

Sports.title: ‘Alcohol, depression and cocaine’- Ex-Premier League star and Brazil striker reveals he almost died after drug overdose
Sports.content:
Next

FORMER Premier League striker Mario Jardel has revealed he nearly DIED from a cocaine overdose after spiralling into depression and alcohol abuse.

The Brazilian, 53, enjoyed a glittering career in Europe before his life took a devastating turn following his omission from the 2002 World Cup squad.



Jardel, who played for Bolton Wanderers under Sam Allardyce, admitted he turned to drugs and drink after being overlooked by then Brazil boss Luiz Felipe Scolari.

The former Porto and Sporting Lisbon goal machine even revealed he once stayed awake for an entire week while taking cocaine.



Speaking to Italian newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport, Jardel said: “I fell into depression and started drinking excessively. Playing in a World Cup was the dream of my life.

“My first wife left me and there were issues regarding the custody of our children.

“I felt everything was slipping away from me, but the worst was yet to come.”

Jardel continued: “In the summer of 2003 I tried cocaine. I was on holiday and I knew I could take it during that period because there were no anti-doping controls.

“I liked it; it made me feel alive and not depressed. Once I stayed awake for an entire week.

“Then I had an overdose, I almost died, and a friend who was with me saved my life. That’s when I hit rock bottom.”



His heartbreaking downfall came despite a sensational goalscoring record that had established him as one of Europe’s most feared forwards.

Jardel claimed he scored 168 goals in 175 matches across four years at Porto before firing 55 in 42 appearances during his final full season at Sporting Lisbon.

The Brazilian won two European Golden Shoes but was still snubbed for the World Cup, which his country went on to win.



He said: “Even today I can’t explain why Scolari didn’t call me up for Brazil in 2002. I was among the five best centre-forwards in the world.”

Jardel joined Bolton in August 2003 but struggled to recapture his remarkable form, making just seven Premier League appearances without scoring.

He later endured a miserable spell at Italian side Ancona, where he claimed he went six months without receiving his wages.

However, the former striker revealed he eventually turned his life around with professional help and the support of his second wife, Sandra.

He explained: “I spent months talking to psychiatrists. I came through it for good when I met my second wife Sandra: she made me understand the meaning of life, and today I’m happy.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Jardel now lives in Fortaleza, Brazil, where he works as an entrepreneur, having left behind the darkest chapter of his life.

And reflecting on everything he has endured, he revealed the advice he would give his younger self: “To use his head and rely less on instinct.”

Sports.title: Real Madrid star submits amazing bid to buy 100 per cent of Italy’s Serie C football club Reggiana
Sports.content:
Next

REAL MADRID superstar Thibaut Courtois is looking to buy an Italian football club through his investment company.

The Belgian goalkeeper, 34, has launched an ambitious bid to take full control of Serie C side Reggiana.



According to Sky Sport Italia and La Gazzetta dello Sport, Courtois’ investment fund NXTPLAY Capital has submitted a proposal to purchase 100 per cent of the club’s shares.

The private equity company was founded in 2025 by Courtois and business partner Gonzalo Vila.



It invests in sports, media, technology and consumer brands, with interests already in French club Le Mans FC and Belgian side KRC Genk.

But Courtois is now hoping to expand his football portfolio by taking over Reggiana.



The former Chelsea star has outlined his ambitious plans for the club, with youth development at the heart of the project.

He said: “We want to build something the people of Reggio Emilia can be proud of.

“Ambitious on the field, close to the community, and built to last.

“Giving young players the right environment to grow in will be at the centre of everything we do.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

However, a deal is far from complete, with Reggiana’s current owner Romano Amadei insisting the club has yet to receive a binding offer.

He confirmed NXTPLAY Capital’s interest but stressed that negotiations remain at an early stage.

Amadei said: “The shareholders await an irrevocable offer, accompanied by the necessary caution in the sale process.”

Courtois has enjoyed a glittering playing career, winning major honours with Chelsea and Real Madrid.

The Belgian joined Madrid from Chelsea in 2018 and has established himself as one of the world’s best goalkeepers.



And he could now follow several other high-profile footballers into club ownership as he looks to build a business empire away from the pitch.

But any takeover will depend on NXTPLAY Capital reaching an agreement with Reggiana’s current shareholders.

Sports.title: New Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino to ban players’ day off after games as he cracks the whip in major fitness blitz
Sports.content:
Next

NEW MANCHESTER United coach Mauricio Pochettino is set to crack the whip with his players to improve their much-criticised fitness.

Pochettino will be flanked at United by his son, Sebastiano, who is also his fitness coach for the United States national team.



Former United coach Michael Carrick did not have his own fitness expert and United’s lack of running and intensity were exposed during his 15 games in charge this season.

United are 19th for total distance covered in the Premier League, 17th for high-speed running distance and 19th for average max speed this season.



Compared with the 17 games Carrick managed last term, United’s high-speed distance running, sprint distance, sprints, high-speed runs and accelerations have all dropped. They also rank bottom in the Gradient Sports athleticism score.

Carrick inherited United fitness coach Charlie Owen, who was not part of the coaching exodus this week as he was separate to the backroom staff that Carrick assembled in January.



Owen has been the United fitness coach since Ole Gunnar Solskjaer promoted him in the summer of 2019.

The 40-year-old usually oversees the start of United’s training sessions as players limber up through ball-work and running exercises.

Solskjaer wanted to make the United squad fitter than ever but in the first month of the 2019-20 season, Luke Shaw, Anthony Martial and Paul Pogba all suffered injuries that resulted in long-term lay-offs.

In United’s seventh Premier League game of the campaign at Newcastle, they were missing six of the players who started in their opening fixture and lost 1-0.

Several players felt Ten Hag’s training sessions were too intense. Ruben Amorim adjusted United’s training pattern so that their daily sessions became less intense as they approached matchday, ensuring the players were as fresh as possible.

Amorim was joined at United by Paulo Berreira, his fitness coach at Sporting Lisbon who has followed him to AC MIlan.

Jose Mourinho and Louis van Gaal also had their own fitness specialists in Carlos Lalin, Stefano Rapetti and Jos van Dijk.



Pochettino is set to order United to report at their Carrington training complex the day after games for recovery sessions. Under Carrick, the squad were almost always off the day after a match.

Former Tottenham defender Toby Alderweireld told the BBC: “First of all he (Pochettino) made us very fit. Pre-season was brutal.

“The way he wants to play – on the front foot, putting people under pressure, a high line, very dynamic play – you need to run.

Sports.title: Man Utd facing huge Bruno Fernandes dilemma after turning down contract offer
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes has turned down a second contract offer from Manchester United as his future looks increasingly precarious.

The United talisman's current deal expires at the end of the season, although the club do have a one-year option in their favour which would prevent him from leaving for free. They also have a clause which stops him talking to foreign clubs about a move come January.

The 32-year-old has now twice rejected improved terms, but United remain confident a deal will be agreed for their prized asset. A man who has won the club's Sir Matt Busby Player of the Year award a record-breaking five times.

However his refusal to sign on the dotted line does not paint the picture of a player committed to the cause, or one who sees himself long-term in Manchester. Fernandes is well remunerated financially and a new deal would simply be a show of faith about where the club is heading - admittedly that is a tough sell right now.

‌



United are in the relegation zone and their best player is hardly going to see that as a sign the club are tracking in the right direction. The arrival of Mauricio Pochettino could change things quickly, though Fernandes has seen plenty of new managers suggest brighter days are ahead.

He's been heavily linked with the exit door in the past, turning down offers in Saudi Arabia several summers ago.

‌



But whilst Fernandes has clearly been the outstanding player on the red side of Manchester for years, he is not without his critics. For all he offers on the pitch there are those who see him as a one-man band, someone whose exploits are not always with the team in mind. His attitude and conduct too have been questioned.

So would a Fernandes exit, as United embark on their latest new era, be the worst thing in the world? There would be those who argue both ways - as we will do now.

Keep Fernandes

The bottom line for a lot of onlookers will be, no club has ever sold their best player and seen that as a route to success. The numbers without Fernandes would paint a horrific picture for United.

This is a player who broke the Premier League record for assists in a single season last term. The Portugal star scored double digits goals in each of his first six seasons at the club, a run that was only ended last season, when he scored nine times.

‌



View 3 Images For all his flaws Bruno Fernandes remains the team's best player

A lot of those have been big goals, and it is Fernandes who has consistently stood up when the chips are down in Manchester. Gary Neville cited him as, by far, the best signing of the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. Yes, the competition has been pretty poor, but he's held himself to a standard that few have been able to match.

He's also had to adapt to a host of different systems, and largely still been able to perform. Plenty argue, if he were in a Pep Guardiola Manchester City team, his reputation and standing in the world game would be very different and that may well be true.

Sell Fernandes

So whilst he is an unbelievable individual there's plenty who will ask more pointed questions. How good is he really, when you consider the team he has around him? Would any decent player have been able to make the impact he had in Manchester, given how poor the team were?

‌



Does his quality come at the expense, rather than complement, the overall plan at United? Jamie Carragher recently suggested that Fernandes' one-man band approach might get the crowd on side, when they see him pressing solo, but if he is stepping outside of team structure, is that really productive?

View 3 Images The Portugal star's conduct has been questioned (Image: Getty Images)

He's often seen running from side to side demanding the ball as he seeks to influence games, but would the team benefit from him excelling in his role, and allowing others to, at least try, and do their job?

Of course there's also the question about his attitude. What some people see as driving standards, others see as toxic. If you watch United regularly then the image of Fernandes throwing his arms up and lamenting his teammates won't be far from your memory.

‌



He also showed that he's not afraid to throw his boss under the bus, as he did with Michael Carrick after the loss at Como. Roy Keane never shied away from speaking publicly - caveat being Fernandes is certainly not Keane - but he did so from a position of power. Criticising your manager's instructions when you're team are on a winless run is also not endearing you to anyone.

The last point being, in a team of assets that have largely devalued since arriving at Old Trafford, Fernandes could still demand top dollar. With the squad needing a major overhaul, Pochettino may see that as cash that can aid a rebuild.

Sports.title: Man Utd's keep or sell squad plan as Mauricio Pochettino's ruthless side emerges
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino may talk of landing his "dream" job at Manchester United but he arrives facing a nightmare scenario given their lowly Premier League position and troubled playing group.

The Argentine will look to arrest the slide at Old Trafford and whilst he's drawn plaudits in the past for his style of play and tactics, the truth is he'll need a transfer window or two, at least, before this team starts to look remotely competitive.

It is full of under performing players and Pochettino will have to axe a host of them - which in the eyes of many has been a long time coming.

Gary Neville recently explained on Sky Sports how the 54-year-old, when at Tottenham, came up with a list of players who he knew he had to rid off, and those he knew he could work with given the squad he inherited

‌



He'll have to do likewise in Manchester with a clear out well overdue. It won't happen overnight and, given they sit in 18th, plenty will argue that more than half the squad needs to go.

5 biggest issues Mauricio Pochettino will immediately face after arriving at Man Utd READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

It will be a gradual process, with some painful moments no doubt, but Pochettino could do worse than build himself another list with those he needs to axe, and those worth keeping. We've taken a look at which players should survive the cull and those who the club may be better off without.

Goalkeepers

Keep: Karl Darlow, Tom Heaton

‌



Both men know their roles within the club and seem happy to play them. Darlow recently arrived but knowing he would serve as a back-up whilst Heaton has been at Old Trafford for years, making limited appearances. His experience and role within the club though has value and it would be a mistake to let that walk out of the door.

View 5 Images Senne Lammens has found things much more challenging in his second year at Old Trafford

Sell: Senne Lammens

Lammens only arrived last year and, after the departure of Andre Onana, was quickly installed as the No 1. Initially things looked promising and this had the hallmarks of one of those deals no one anticipated, but could work out long-term. Now though the mistakes have become more regular and the pressure of being the United goalkeeper is beginning to tell. Harsh reality is, a team challenging for honours needs better than the Belgian.

‌



Defenders

Keep: Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven, Matthijs de Ligt

Two of these three should be kept with the long-term in mind, but of course the club need to constantly reassess if they don't develop as planned. Heaven looked good when he slotted in last year, but given his tender age is obviously still raw.

Yoro is a bit further on in his development but is making more errors than you'd like from a centre-half. There's enough to hold onto to think he could play a role in the future though.

De Ligt's fitness is his biggest problem and the fact other top clubs have moved him on has been cited as a red flag. But United cannot remove of every defender they have all at once, and the Dutchman seems worth keeping more than some of his colleagues.

‌



View 5 Images Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven still have plenty of potential growth in them (Image: Getty Images)

Sell: Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, Noussair Mazraoui, Patrick Dorgu, Diogo Dalot

This is a mismatch of players who have under performed, are past their best and are far too attached to previous managers. This list of six compromises signings of five previous bosses - Louis van Gaal, Jose Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim.

They were all signed for different systems and at different times and the club simply need to move on. Maguire's best days are past him, Martinez cannot replicate his Argentina form in Manchester and Shaw's fitness has been an issue for years.

‌



Mazraoui, Dorgu and Dalot, all full-backs or wing-backs, are solid when they want to be. But no team pushing for silverware would likely have them in a first choice back four.

Midfielders

Keep: Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes

Two of the four only arrived in the summer and their previous bodies of work merit them sticking around to see what they can add, especially Baleba, who has time on his side. Mainoo has already been through enough ups and downs to define a career but is too talented to see walk out of the door at this stage of his career.

View 5 Images Carlos Baleba moved to Manchester in the summer (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Fernandes' talent makes him the best player at Old Trafford, but his attitude remains something that needs to be managed. His impact on the team - for better or worse - is huge and he needs to have a more designated role on the pitch if he isn't to prove a counterproductive influence.

Sell: Andrey Santos, Manuel Ugarte, Mason Mount

If it wasn't for injury then Ugarte would likely already be out of the door. His move from PSG has simply not worked. Santos seemed like a bizarre signing from the start. When a rival is so willing to sell to you red flags should be raised, but that perhaps speaks to the decision making in Manchester.

Mount's time at the club has been frustrating. The overriding issue has been just where does he fit in. There's obviously a player there, but in an ideal world he'd play in Fernandes' position, which isn't happening. There's also too much flair on the flanks in the final third to afford him a regular role. All of which points to a mutual parting of ways.

‌



View 5 Images Marcus Rashford has played under five permanent managers at Man Utd, but could face an uncertain future

Forwards

Keep: Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha, Amad, Shea Lacey

Last summer United ploughed money into their frontline and it did ultimately pay off with their attackers proving to be some of their best players. They won games singlehandedly and the likes of Mbeumo and Cunha would command major roles at any team in the Premier League.

Sesko's injuries have proved frustrating and untimely, but in the latter half of his debut season he looked increasingly effective and is still in the infancy of his career. Lacey has shown huge promise and Amad, not necessarily as a regular starter, but as part of an attacking unit, offers plenty.

‌



Sell: Joshua Zirkzee, Marcus Rashford

Zirkzee, like Ugarte, was someone the club wanted to offload in the summer and the end of his time in Manchester is a case of when, not if. Rashford has had over a decade in Manchester and, despite periods of quality, the consistency has been an issue.

He is also one of the club's top earners on more than £300,000-a-week and too many managers have felt they could get the best from him, only to be disappointed. Had Barcelona activated an option clause then United would've waved goodbye to him in the summer.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino's dream Man Utd XI as Bruno Fernandes replaced and Chelsea star signs
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino's dream Man Utd XI as Bruno Fernandes replaced and Chelsea star signs

Mauricio Pochettino faces a huge rebuilding job at Manchester United

View 6 Images Mauricio Pochettino could lure some exciting signings to Old Trafford (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Mauricio Pochettino has his hands full after being sworn in as the next Manchester United manager. The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss has penned a two-and-a-half-year contract after agreeing to replace the sacked Michael Carrick.

‌



Pochettino's first task is steering a squad of misfits clear of the relegation zone, given United entered the international break in 18th with just one win from 10 games. Beyond that lies a sweeping rebuild that could attract some big names to Old Trafford, with other high-profile figures heading for the exit door.

Given his extensive knowledge of the English, European and world game, Pochettino's pulling power should be significant, provided the club can back him financially. Here's how a dream Pochettino XI could look and how he could reconstruct the team…

Mauricio Pochettino bursts into tears in first interview after getting Man Utd job READ MORE :

When will Mauricio Pochettino first take charge of Man Utd and his likely starting XI? READ MORE :

Defensive clearout

A ruthless clear-out is overdue. Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, and Diogo Dalot all need to go, and unless Lisandro Martinez undergoes a major attitude shift under his compatriot, he should be shown the door when his contract expires this summer.

Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt aren't long-term solutions either. At right-back, Atletico Madrid's Marcos Llorente would be an astute addition, especially as he is out of contract in the summer.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

He's 31 but has retired from international football, which should prolong his club career. The fact that he could operate in midfield too would be a valuable asset. If Pochettino wants a younger option - and a player he knows - he could turn to United States star Alex Freeman, 22. Or why not go for both for a bit of youth and experience?

United are also crying out for a quality left-back. Step forward, Fulham's Antonee Robinson. He ranks among the Premier League's top full-backs in tackles and interceptions and, crucially, rarely misses games through injury, unlike Shaw. He would need no introduction to Pochettino, having played under him for the US.

View 6 Images Antonee Robinson could be an option for United (Image: Getty Images)

In the centre of defence, the likes of Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Nathan Collins (Brentford) and Calvin Bassey (Fulham) have all been linked with United and all three would be welcome, forward-thinking additions. Youngsters like Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven need to stick around but as back-up options rather than regular first-teamers.

In goal, Senne Lammens hasn't been convincing recently - perhaps unsurprising given the players in front of him - but he deserves more time to prove himself.

Midfield tinkering

While he's had a mixed time at Spurs, Conor Gallagher was superb under Pochettino at Chelsea, arguably playing the best football of his career. A reunion could kickstart his career.

During the 2023/24 season, he enjoyed spells across the midfield, playing as a six, eight and a 10. Pochettino regularly spoke highly of the midfielder, once saying: "I think he is a player with a great commitment to the team. It's priceless to have a player like him."

Gallagher could form a handy partnership with Kobbie Mainoo. Youri Tielemans could still have a role to play but Andrey Santos already looks like an expensive mistake.

View 6 Images Conor Gallagher could be available (Image: Robbie Stephenson/PA Wire)

Wing wizard needed

United were linked with Crysencio Summerville in the summer before he eventually signed for Al-Hilal. At 25, a player of his dynamism and quality is wasted in Saudi Arabia.

But once he's sufficiently topped up his bank balance, he'll probably crave a move back to a big league. The Dutchman could be ideal for the Poch revolution.

View 6 Images Crysencio Summerville was on United's radar in the summer (Image: Getty Images)

Pounce for Palmer

Bringing in Palmer would be a pricey statement of intent, but the foundations are already laid. He played some of his best football under Pochettino, calling him a "top manager and a top person" and is a childhood United supporter.

Given Chelsea's track record of cashing in on talent, a deal cannot be ruled out. Palmer could replace Bruno Fernandes as playmaker in chief. For all his quality, Fernandes is in danger of becoming more trouble than he's worth. A move could be best for all parties.

View 6 Images Mauricio Pochettino has previously worked with Cole Palmer at Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Reuniting with Kane

While the England captain recently penned a new deal with Bayern Munich, Pochettino is the one manager outside of Tottenham who could tempt him back to the Premier League, following their successful five-year partnership in north London.

Should Kane lift the Champions League this season, there would be little left for him to conquer in Germany. Firing United back to the summit would be the ultimate crowning achievement to a storied career.

Another, more realistic option would be US striker Folarin Balogun of Monaco, who remains on the radar of Premier League clubs after almost joining Everton in the summer.

View 6 Images Could Pochettino tempt Harry Kane to United (Image: PA)

As for existing players, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha are talents who should stick around, while Amad can't be written off just yet. But it's getting increasingly difficult to see a United future for Benjamin Sesko. And it's surely time for Marcus Rashford to sever ties with the club once and for all.

United dream XI under Pochettino: Lemmens; Llorente, Branthwaite, Collins, Robinson; Mainoo, Gallagher; Cunha, Palmer, Summerville; Kane.

Sports.title: Man City guilty verdict could impact transfer plans as banks 'shy away' from lending
Sports.content:
Man City guilty verdict could impact transfer plans as banks 'shy away' from lending

Manchester City are nervously awaiting the outcome of their appeal after being found guilty of flouting the Premier League's financial rules, but they are already experiencing impacts

View 2 Images Manchester City may struggle to get financing for transfers (Image: Dave Howarth - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Manchester City could find financing transfers more difficult in the wake of their guilty verdict, with reputational damage already taking hold.

‌



‌



City were found guilty in September of breaking the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-year period. An independent commission found them guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled against them, finding they had used "sham" contracts to disguise funding of more than £830million.

‌



City have always protested their innocence and they have appealed against the verdict. It emerged on Friday that their appeal would be heard in December, with the verdict then due in the New Year.

‌



But despite the process still playing out, the club are already experiencing some negative impacts, which could affect their plans for the upcoming transfer windows. City spent around £450million on transfers in the summer, splashing out to sign Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez among others.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Yet their ability to spend big in the future could be hindered by banks' refusal to help finance deals. Bloomberg reports that banks are 'starting to shy away' from deals involving City while they await the outcome of their case.

It is reported that banks have been advancing money to clubs selling players to City, but are reticent to do so now due to reputational damage and potential credit risk.

‌



City could be relegated from the Premier League, hit with a significant points deduction, fined or slapped with a transfer ban in the wake of the bombshell verdict. Meanwhile, The Independent Football Regulator could strip the club from City's owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Elliot Anderson joined Man City for £116m in the summer (Image: Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Bloomberg reports that City have already experienced the cold shoulder from banks after German lender Oldenburgische Landesbank AG pulled out of a deal to help finance the £34m signing of Allan from Palmeiras in the summer. Had it gone ahead, Brazilian side Palmeiras would have received an up-front payment from the bank secured against future transfer fees.

‌



The process, called transfer receivables, benefits both clubs and banks, but could become off limits to City, depending on the outcome of their appeal. Man City chief executive Ferran Soriano is convinced they will be cleared.

"The whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation - that the owners' personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true," he said in a video message to staff in early October.

Article continues below

"Irrefutable evidence has been provided to the Premier League commission that shows that it could not happen and that it did not happen. This includes bank statements, money transfers, witnesses and everything necessary to categorically demonstrate that the money did not come from the owner. Every other false charge that has been thrown at us - and aggressively marketed and promoted - comes from the simple, central, and completely false accusation."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel warns England can’t repeat Argentina mistake if they want to beat Spain
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel wants his England players to prove they are winners - against a team which “has forgotten how to lose.”

England face the ultimate test in the Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday because world champions Spain are on a record-breaking 43 game unbeaten run.

Spain have already beaten England in the Nations League at Wembley but the rematch in Madrid has now become a winner-takes-all to top the Group. Tuchel believes England must go out with an attacking mindset and a belief they can beat Spain if they play to their own strengths.

But it is also about having the confidence they can beat the best and lay down a marker for the future that England can win against top opposition.

‌



England boss Tuchel said: “It's a massive stadium, it's a massive occasion. It's a team that has forgotten how to lose, so of course it requires a top performance first of all, and if we can deliver this performance, it will give us a big boost.

England hold talks about leaving the pitch vs Spain if they suffer racist abuse READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

“It's not a must-win game if you go to Spain. But I think the mindset is important that we got the win today to have this match would feel very, very different if not.

“So that is the first step, and now it's important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home, and attack them and try to make it a physical game, and try to impose our strength. I think that's what we want to see.

‌



“And then you can never predict the result in football, never. But it's important that we show the mindset that you speak of and the spirit, and we will. I'm very confident about that.”

England enjoyed a brilliant World Cup campaign until their undoing against Argentina in the semi-final when they retreated back into themselves and surrendered.

View 3 Images The world champions are on a 43-match unbeaten record

But since then, England beat France in the third-place play-off, lost to Spain at Wembley 3-2 but then beat Czech Republic, thrashed Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka and then beat Slaven Bilic’s side again at Wembley on Thursday night.

‌



Tuchel believes England have “come a long way since the summer” and have now set up the final that he wanted. It makes it a big pressurised occasion.

“Push our limits. See where we are,” said Tuchel. “We all feel that we deserved more in the first game, so we want to take it back in the second.

“I think we're there, and I think we're ready to to win on Sunday. I know what it takes, and like no one can ever guarantee it, but I think it's it's the moment to check how far we are and to push our limit and proof of concept.”

View 3 Images England suffered World Cup heartache after retreating in the semi final vs Argentina (Image: Julian Finney/FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



Tuchel also believes while Spain are daunting, they are not unbeatable. It was competitive at Wembley. Harry Kane missed a penalty at 2-1. It was there for England.

Tuchel added: “It took us a while in that game, and we had maybe the worst start that you can have going 1-0 down against a team full of confidence. But once we got our energy going and played with this for the equaliser, we were strong.

“Had a very good second half, and strangely enough, Harry missed the penalty, and it was maybe the key moment for us because we were very strong then and deserved to be 3-1 up. It would have been very difficult to come back against us on that day.

“We had too many big individual mistakes in our own half on the night. But honestly, if you deeply look into the matches, even of Spain, they had some crucial ball losses against Croatia. They got away with it.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"They conceded some big, big chances against Croatia, and still managed to win the game in the end. So no one is unbeatable.

“We need a top performance, and we're full of confidence, and we're getting there. I think it's exactly what we wanted, and we feel that we have something to take that we that we lost the last time.”

Sports.title: Meetmebythesea gives McManus a first Paddy Power Gold Cup
Sports.content:
Ben Pauling’s Meetmebythesea showed his liking for Cheltenham once more and delivered owner JP McManus with his first victory in the prestigious Paddy Power Gold Cup.

Sent off the heavily backed 2-1 favourite on his first run since winning as a novice at the Festival in March, he put in some tremendous leaps on the way round for Harry Cobden.

Blueking d'Oroux, having his first run for Dan Skelton, looked the biggest danger after long-time leader Quebecois faded but Meetmebythesea powered away up the hill to win by two and a half lengths to give Cobden a second big victory in two days in the McManus colours.

Pauling said: "Harry wanted to ride him forward because not many are coming from behind today and he jumped brilliantly and travelled so well.

"I was a little worried turning for home that Dan's horse was going so well but he showed a lot of guts and then won well. Jumping the last he had plenty left and he has so much pace for a big horse.

"He needed to do that today and he showed a lot more than we have seen from him so far because he found plenty for pressure. He's just really good and you don't know what you have got until you run in races like that - that was cool, very cool.

"I didn't get nervous until 20 minutes before as you just want it so much when you believe in them so much and it's great that it has all come off.

"This is the race that really made me tick growing up and I've been coming to this meeting since I was 14. This has always been a big race for me and to have the favourite was a dream so to win it is even better.

"I had so much faith in this horse and I talked him up plenty in the lead-up. It's all well sitting on the fence but I knew he was good, just not how good. You just have to believe he is going to keep on improving and hopefully that puts him bang there for some of the better races."

BetVictor make Meetmebythesea 12-1 from 25s to now step up to the highest level at Kempton on Boxing Day where he could be given the opportunity to replicate The Jukebox Man's King George VI Chase heroics for Pauling last Christmas.

"I suppose we have to think about Kempton at Christmas and I think he's going to stay every yard of three miles," added the local handler.

"To keep a horse like this improving is cool and we need these types of horses to keep us going the right way. It's not easy when you're in the top 10 and you need to find horses of this calibre. He looks to be one of them.

"It's one of the big ones of my career and he has a bright future. I hope he could be as good as any I've trained but we've a long way to go. He might have to improve another 10 to 15lb to be winning a big one.

"I think this might be his trip or a nice flat three (miles) for now. Kempton felt nice last year, so who knows."

Having provided McManus with one of the major races absent from his trophy cabinet, a trip to Kempton at Christmas could represent the chance to tick off another missing from the mantlepiece.

However, festive dreams may be on hold for the Irishman, who was content to relish yet another fantastic result at Prestbury Park.

"I left it to Ben and this was his plan, you have to give him all the credit," said McManus.

"It's always nice to win a race at Cheltenham and I've tried to win this race many times but just come up short. Today thankfully it happened.

"You don't get tired of days like this and I've never won the King George, Champion Chase and Arkle, so we've got to try get those next.

"He could be a King George horse, but this was the plan for this lad today and he's only six. I know six-year-old's have won it before but we'll just have to see."

Atomic City lays down credentials in Triumph Trial

Atomic City laid down an early marker for his division in the JCB Triumph Trial Juvenile Hurdle at Cheltenham when displaying a smart turn of foot.

Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old was ridden with great confidence by J J Slevin at the back of the field and the 88-rated performer from the Flat jumped with aplomb bar one sticky leap at the second last.

Charles Darnay hit the front off the home bend under Harry Cobden but Slevin had him in his sights and brought his mount up against the rail before quickening clear to win by four lengths and justify 11-10 favouritism.

Coral cut him to 14-1 from 25s for the Triumph Hurdle in March with his rider suitably impressed.

Slevin said: "He's a high-class Flat horse who was quite good in Cork the first day and the aim today was to get him to spit it (the bridle) out today.

"He would be high up in Joseph's pecking order I would say, at least this stage, and I'd say he's going to be a Triumph Hurdle horse, he's a fair horse.

"I'd say he will be better with softer ground. He's jumped and travelled well and he couldn't have been better there.

"He's won easy and it's still early days. A lot of the lads won't have gone to the well yet with their juveniles and as the year goes on we'll find out more. But he was very impressive today."

Sports.title: McKenna to defend world title live on Sky Sports on December 4
Sports.content:
Aaron McKenna will defend his middleweight world title on Friday December 4, live on Sky Sports.

IBF champion McKenna will fight unbeaten Latvian Jevgenijs Aleksejevs at The Venue in Riyadh in the main event of Riyadh Season Zuffa Boxing 14.

It will be McKenna's first defence of the world title belt he won by beating Etinosa Oliha on a memorable night in Dublin.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Aaron McKenna's IBF middleweight world title fight against Etinosa Oliha.

McKenna, 21-0 (10), who hails from Monaghan, Ireland, is a nine-year pro who vaulted into title contention with his April 2025 decision over former world champion Liam Smith.

While McKenna fought many times in Ireland as a top amateur, he returned home for the first time as a pro in August, capturing the world title with a one-sided victory over Oliha at Dublin's 3Arena.

Aleksejevs, a world-ranked contender who has had 10 stoppage victories in his 20 professional wins, will be challenging for a world title for the first time.

A former kickboxing standout, Aleksejevs has been perfect in gloved combat, securing a regional title last October with a unanimous decision over Przemyslaw Zysk. In February, he outlasted Italy's Damiano Falcinelli over 10 tense rounds.

Former European champion and world title challenger Jack Massey returns to action against Andrew Tabiti.

Sports.title: Immense Wales pull off sensational first victory over All Blacks since 1953
Sports.content:
Nations Championship - Wales 35-28 New Zealand: Hosts display immense defence to pull off first win vs All Blacks since 1953

Eddie James was among the try-scorers as Wales pulled off one of rugby's biggest shocks of recent times with victory over New Zealand

Wales pulled off one of rugby's biggest shocks of recent times as immense defence saw them to a 35-28 Nations Championship victory over New Zealand - a first vs the All Blacks since 1953.

Wales' victory was built on the foundation of some of their best 40 minutes of rugby for some time in the first half, leading 14-0 and 21-7 after tries from scrum-half Tomos Williams, hooker Dewi Lake and tighthead Archie Griffin.

A decision to keep playing deep in the first half instead of kicking out proved costly, though, allowing New Zealand to level the contest by the break via tries from scrum-half Cortez Ratima, No 8 Wallace Sititi and wing Fehi Fineanganofo - the last score coming three minutes into dead time at the end of the first half.

Yet, Wales emerged and flew into a big lead again at the start of the second half, scoring converted tries through centre Eddie James and wing Louis Rees-Zammit for a 35-21 advantage.

Peter Lakai quickly narrowed the deficit to seven with an All Blacks try, and the remainder of the contest was played out almost exclusively inside the Wales 22, only for the home side to repel wave after wave of attack, holding New Zealand up three times in-goal.

Wales 35-28 New Zealand - Score summary Wales - Tries: Williams (2), Lake (6), Griffin (24), James (44), Rees-Zammit (48). Cons: Costelow (3,7,25,45,49). New Zealand - Tries: Ratima (10), Sititi (31), Fineanganofo (43), Lakai (53). Cons: Mo'unga (10,32,44,54).

Story of the match

Wales made an astonishing start to the contest, creating space down the right for Rees-Zammit to chip ahead and Williams to score a try off a kind bounce after just 90 seconds.

Tomos Williams scored for Wales after 90 seconds of the contest

Into the sixth minute, Wales had a second try as their early pressure and exuberance gave way to a strong finish from captain Lake, scoring after a rolling maul had made decent ground in the New Zealand 22.

Wales captain Dewi Lake charged over for their second try of the Test inside six minutes

Staring at a 14-0 scoreline, New Zealand quickly woke up to score their opening try in the 10th minute: scrum-half Ratima breaking off a maul to dart over past poor Welsh defence.

Cortez Ratima scored New Zealand's first try of the Test in the 10th minute

Yet, Wales came strong again as centre Max Llewellyn knocked on a chance he should have scored in the 23rd minute, with the hosts maintaining their composure to grab a third through impressive prop Griffin from close range.

Archie Griffin got over for Wales' third try in a sensational first-half performance

Past the half-hour mark, New Zealand hit back again as back-row Sititi fought his way over after another driving maul in the Wales 22.

As the half drew to a close, Wales twice had opportunities to kick the ball off and bring things to the break, but instead played on in search of further points.

It proved a major error when the All Blacks attacked from deep, and kept making ground and offloading until wing Fineanganofo finished by the posts.

Fehi Fineanganofo scored deep into dead time at the end of the first half to level the contest

When Richie Mo'unga converted, the score was level at 21-21 at half-time, with Wales no doubt disappointed not to be in the lead after their impressive first half.

The home side came out in the second half undeterred, however, building through Rees-Zammit down the right again, and eventually creating space for James to finish in the left corner.

Sam Costelow converted brilliantly for a 28-21 lead, and moments later the Welsh had a fifth try through Rees-Zammit - turning down a kickable penalty in favour of a five-metre lineout, and executing perfectly off the set-piece to score.

Louis Rees-Zammit scored as Wales made a fast start to the second half too

With a lead of 35-21, James then made a remarkable tackle on Anton Lienert-Brown to save a try, but it proved little more than a delay of the inevitable as Lakai dived to ground on the line, narrowing the gap to seven points just five minutes after Wales' latest try.

On the hour mark, Sititi was held up over the try-line by Gareth Thomas when a try looked easier to score, before 21 phases of All Blacks attack was ended by a superb Jac Morgan breakdown turnover.

With 15 minutes to play, James Botham held up Asafo Aumua to deny the All Blacks again, before Wales somehow denied the visitors once more after a lengthy stanza of attack gave way to another call of held-up.

The All Blacks kept coming, but Wales' defence proved inspired to get them over the line for a famous, and wholly unexpected, victory.

'I can't even describe the emotions'

Wales back row James Botham, speaking on ITV:

"I can't even describe the emotions. 1953 was the last time we beat the All Blacks.

"It's come from belief. The crowd was behind us - I just want to thank the energy and the noise behind us - you were unbelievable.

"It shows how tight we are as a group.

"It would be rude not to have a celebration tonight!"

Warburton 'Proud to be Welsh'

Former Wales international Sam Warburton, speaking on ITV:

"To every fan, the 55,000 who put their hands in their pockets to still watch Wales, this will be so sweet.

"We forget what this playing group has gone through. From Grand Slam champions to one of the longest losing streaks for a tier one nation - they were in the pits.

"Proud to be Welsh on a day like today - those players were magnificent."

What's next?

For Wales, they next face Australia in their third Nations Championship Test of the autumn at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Saturday, November 21 (8.10pm kick-off).

New Zealand travel to face England at Allianz Stadium Twickenham for their next Test, also on Saturday, November 21 (2.10pm kick-off).

Sports.title: A new No 1? How to stop Lamine Yamal? Tuchel's selection issues
Sports.content:
Against the best team in the world, Thomas Tuchel's defensive decisions will be key. And he has many to make.

The England head coach said before Croatia at Wembley on Thursday that he was quite happy to go full-strength in both matches, despite the three-day gap, and he was true to his word. All the big guns were out for Harry Kane's big night.

Barring unexpected late injury or illness, the best player in the world will lead the line against the world champions. Morgan Rogers should start at right wing, Anthony Gordon left wing. England's Madrid maestro Jude Bellingham will play No 10, and Elliot Anderson and Declan Rice will form the double-pivot at No 8.

But behind that, is where Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry will be pondering their options.

Do England have a new No 1?

The decision Tuchel makes about his goalkeeper could be one of the most important we have seen for eight years.

Since the World Cup of 2018 in Russia, Jordan Pickford's consistent brilliance has seen him largely unchallenged as England's first-choice keeper. Not so now.

As he nears his century of international caps (Pickford has 94) there is a new pretender to his throne, James Trafford. In the last international camp, Tuchel shared the four games out equally between the two and he has hinted he will do the same this time round.

Seeing Pickford walk out at Wembley on Thursday, in the lesser of the two matches, was a surprise. Most onlookers expected him to get the nod against the world champions in Madrid. He may yet do so. But if he doesn't, if Tuchel sticks to the plan he outlined at the start of the camp and brings Trafford in then it will feel like a real "changing of the guard" moment for the England No 1 shirt.

How to stop Lamine Yamal?

Image: Lamine Yamal celebrates scoring against England

In terms of outfielders, no decision is bigger than who should play left-back, to try to combat the most potent of Spain's threats, Lamine Yamal. The man who finished third in the Ballon d'Or rankings stayed in Barcelona for treatment on a troublesome right knee rather than travelling to Prague on Thursday night. He was being saved for England and he is fit and back with the national team now.

Most likely, Lewis Hall will be given the task of keeping Lamine Yamal quiet, keeping his place on the left side of England's defence. Tuchel said after his performance against Croatia that Hall is "doing all he needs to do" to nail down the role as England's first choice and that he is playing "top level".

The Newcastle defender has already proved himself against Barcelona's wondrous winger. In the spring of this year, in the Champions League, he put in a performance that led the Spanish-based newspaper Mundo Deportivo to label Hall the "anti-Lamine".

On the other side of England's defence, it feels like a straight shoot-out between Ben White and Djed Spence, with Trent Alexander-Arnold no doubt expecting to be dropped. Tuchel has consistently questioned his defending and so he is likely to sit out the test in Spain.

Image: Djed Spence was a standout performer for England at the World Cup

Spence missed two England training sessions and Thursday night's game against Croatia as he nursed himself to be ready for this one. He was one of England's most formidable finds of the World Cup, proving himself to be the team's best one-on-one defender.

White has only started one game for his country since before the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and that was the 1-0 home defeat to Japan. If he does get the nod over Spence, both he and Tuchel will hope he avoids the boos which marked his substitute appearance against Croatia on Thursday night.

Alex Baena, who is likely to be Spain's left winger, doesn't pose the same threat as Lamine Yamal on the other flank but he did score against Czech Republic a few days ago - and against England at Wembley.

In the centre of England's defence, again, Tuchel has some big calls. If Ezri Konsa, rested against Croatia, is now fully fit, as he seems to be, he will almost certainly be recalled straight to the heart of the defence. In the absence of the injured Marc Guehi and John Stones he is England's most senior and most influential defender.

Jarell Quansah, who had a howler for Croatia's equalising goal, may well drop out because he is considered a right-sided centre-back, as is Konsa. So that would mean the left-leaning Dan Burn or Jarrad Branthwaite coming in alongside the Arsenal man. Best bet there is Burn.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player David Reed and Pete Smith deliver their England player ratings following the Three Lions’ 2-1 victory over Croatia, as Harry Kane makes history on a record-breaking night and England secure their place in the Nations League quarter-finals.

A significant match for Tuchel's England 2.0

Significantly, Trafford was the preferred choice when Tuchel's men played Spain in September.

For that reason, and also because this is England's final game of 2026, and because it is their last until the Nations League quarter-finals in March - it feels a hugely significant match.

The animosity from large chunks of England's support, and from some England players, towards Tuchel for those now infamous tactical choices of the World Cup semi-final against Argentina, have melted away. The national team's autumn performances have reignited hope and belief.

Which way the result - and the performance - goes against the World Cup winners, will almost certainly dictate the mood and the direction of travel for England from here on in.

In the persistent rain of Madrid, the game will be a barometer of where England are, in project Thomas Tuchel 2.0.

Sports.title: Chacarra reveals plan for 'dream' win over McIlroy and 'Dubai double'
Sports.content:
Eugenio Chacarra is eyeing more than just holding off Rory McIlroy to Race to Dubai victory at the DP World Tour Championship, following a strong finish to his third round.

Chacarra entered the week with a 533.93-point lead over McIlroy in the season-long standings, having won three times this year, only to lose ground with rounds of 72 and 71 over the first two days at Jumeirah Golf Estates.

McIlroy temporarily moved above Chacarra into projected top spot, as he chases a record-equalling eighth Order of Merit title, with the world No 2 also briefly jumping to the top of the leaderboard before stuttering to a third-round 72.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul McGinley reviews Rory McIlroy's mixed third round in Dubai and whether he can play his way back into the tournament

Chacarra made nine birdies - including four in his last six holes - to post a four-under 68 and join McIlroy on five under, four strokes behind leader Tyrrell Hatton, but the Spaniard remains hopeful of challenging for tournament victory and 'Dubai double'.

"A lot of good and a lot of bad," Chacarra said about his performance. It has been a grind and I've been fighting. I've played all year on DP World Tour and I've played a lot.

"I want to really win that ranking, so I want to show the world I'm capable of playing under pressure. I think, so far, I've been doing that.

Image: Eugenio Chacarra is looking to secure the Race to Dubai by winning the DP World Tour Championship

"I just want to win the tournament. I'm not far away. I know if I win the tournament, I win the ranking, so that's what I wanted to do in Abu Dhabi and I want to do it here.

"That's what we prepare for and I'm going to have a chance on Sunday. That's what we dream of since I was little is to win big events on Sunday.

Late twist in the Race to Dubai battle?

Nine players started the week with a mathematical chance of topping the season-long standings, with South Africa's Jayden Schaper - needing a win and results to go his way - five strokes back and Jon Rahm a further shot behind.

McIlroy needs solo fourth or better to have any chance of surpassing Chacarra, who can guarantee the Order of Merit with victory, with the Spaniard still heading into the final round top of the projected Race to Dubai standings.

"There's a number of scenarios that could unfold tomorrow," former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley told Sky Sports. "I don't think Jon Rahm is not out of it yet - I could still see him coming through with a really strong last throw of the dice.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Jamie Weir explains how Rory McIlroy can win the DP World Tour's Race to Dubai for a record-equalling eighth time

"I think Rory [McIlroy] will reset and [Eugenio] Chacarra is going to battle some way or another. I don't think he's going to win the tournament, but he's going to really make it difficult for those guys.

"I think there are a few little things that can bob and weave there. At the moment, it does look like Chacarra is the favourite for the Race to Dubai. Rory has fallen a lot off the pace and it's going to take a big reset now for him tomorrow to really go at it and shoot a low score.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy briefly moved above Tyrrell Hatton with this brilliant eagle at the par-five seventh

"McIlroy's still there, or thereabouts and he will reset overnight, so I expect a better Rory coming out tomorrow. If he can hit fairways, I think the rest of the game will be in good shape."

Hatton expects 'tough day' in search of Dubai win

Starting the week 12th in the Race to Dubai standings and too far back to win the Harry Vardon Trophy, Hatton leads the tournament on nine under - one ahead of France's Victor Perez - as he looks to close out a ninth DP World Tour title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyrrell Hatton breaks down his third round and his hopes of closing out a first DP World Tour Championship win

"It was a good day," said Hatton, a two-time runner-up at the DP World Tour Championship. "It was tricky - the greens were so fast on the back nine. Every putt I had coming in I think from the 13th was just unbelievably fast. Really happy with how I putted today.

"I know tomorrow is going to be a tough day. I've got enough experience down these last few holes to know that anything can happen. I'll just go out tomorrow and try my best. I know I can play well around here, and that's what I'll try to do."

Sports.title: Le Tissier hits stunner to mark milestone in Man Utd win
Sports.content:
Maya Le Tissier marked her 150th club appearance with a stunning strike as Manchester United moved fourth in the WSL with a dominant 2-0 win over Crystal Palace.

Le Tissier cracked in the opening goal from around 25 yards out to give United the lead during a first half they spent almost entirely on the front foot.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Maya Le Tissier scores a screamer to put Manchester United ahead against Crystal Palace on her 150th appearance

Battling Palace made it trickier for their hosts after the break but were undone too easily for the second, when Hinata Miyazawa and Jess Park combined to play in Elisabeth Terland for a clinical finish.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Elisabeth Terland slots home Manchester United's second against Crystal Palace after a beautiful piece of play

United will feel they should have taken more from a game which saw them rack up 22 shots but hit the target just three times, with Lea Schuller wastefully lobbing wide late on.

The win was never in doubt, though, with goal-scorer Le Tissier repeatedly snuffing out counter-attacks from a Palace side who failed to test United goalkeeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce at all.

With United on the rise ahead of the later kick-offs, Palace stay 11th.
