“Nobody is left out. All we need to do is to ensure that we put more effort into strengthening the existing unity that we are all enjoying in the party today,” he said.

He expressed confidence that the reconciliation drive would consolidate the party’s electoral strength and deliver victories for Tinubu, senators, members of the House of Representatives and candidates for the state and national assemblies.

Meanwhile, the Commissioner for Women Affairs, Dr. Seun Osamaye, pledged the mobilisation of women across Ondo State to secure at least one million votes for Tinubu, attributing the anticipated support to the Federal Government’s interventions in women’s economic empowerment, education and social protection.

Osamaye said the state had benefited from more than 20 interventions under the Renewed Hope initiatives of the President and First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu.

She listed the distribution of 10,000 professional kits to nurses and professional healthcare assistants, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), youth agribusiness initiatives and the Every Home Garden programme among the interventions, adding that thousands of women had also benefited from economic empowerment programmes.

“For the first time, government is not for the privileged few. Many women now benefit without having to beg or lobby,” she said.

The commissioner expressed optimism that the interventions would translate into unprecedented electoral support for Tinubu on January 16, 2027, insisting that women across the state were prepared to work collectively towards the target.

She also dismissed suggestions of strained relations among party leaders, describing Princess Oladunni Odu, the state’s first female Secretary to the State Government, as a respected leader with whom she maintained a cordial relationship.

Osamaye further described Governor Aiyedatiwa as the undisputed leader of the APC in the state, enjoying the support of party members.

On concerns about political violence ahead of the 2027 elections, APC chieftain, Chief Olusola Oke, maintained that Ondo State remained peaceful, insisting that no opposition member or political party had been attacked by political thugs.

Oke, who commended the media for its vigilance and professionalism, said reports of rising political thuggery in other parts of the country did not reflect the situation in Ondo State.

World.title: Chemical Engineers Urge FG to Revive Ajaokuta Steel to Save $4bn Annually
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The Nigerian Society of Chemical Engineers (NSChE) has called for the urgent revival of the moribund Ajaokuta Steel Company, warning that Nigeria loses about $4 billion annually to steel imports while missing out on millions of jobs and enormous industrial development opportunities.

The Society said reviving the steel complex through a transparent, private sector-led investment arrangement would significantly reduce the country’s dependence on imported steel, conserve foreign exchange, stimulate mining and manufacturing, and accelerate infrastructure development.

National President of NSChE, Bayo Olarewaju-Alo, made the call at the Society’s 56th Annual Conference, Annual General Meeting and Exhibition in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, yesterday.

Olarewaju-Alo disclosed that Nigeria’s annual steel demand stood at approximately 10 million tonnes, while domestic production was only about 1.2 million tonnes, largely from scrap-based operations.

He described the situation as a major economic setback, arguing that the country’s continued dependence on imported steel was draining its foreign reserves and undermining the development of indigenous industrial capacity.

“In my briefing, I stated that currently Nigeria imports about 10 million tons per annum of steel. That’s our need. If we have our own steel-making industry, we wouldn’t be importing that amount of steel. Rather, we’d be saving about $4 billion in foreign exchange,” he said.

He stressed that the benefits of reviving Ajaokuta would extend beyond foreign exchange savings to employment generation, improved infrastructure, technological advancement and stronger industrial capacity.

“The multiplier effect is that we will create a lot of jobs, not just for engineers, but all categories of people. People will be supplying materials that are required. People will be engaged in mining coal and iron ore,” he added.

According to him, a functional Ajaokuta would stimulate activities across the mining, transportation, power, engineering and manufacturing sectors, while strengthening the country’s capacity to execute major infrastructure projects.

“There is no country in the world that has very good infrastructure development that does not need steel input. Any major project to be executed in Nigeria will require steel input,” he said.

To achieve this, the NSChE president advocated majority private ownership by a Nigerian consortium or conglomerate, supported by strategic technical partners and a minority Federal Government stake.

He, however, warned that changing ownership alone would not guarantee success, insisting that investors must have access to reliable iron ore, natural gas, electricity, transportation infrastructure, financing and sustainable markets.

The Society recommended transparent privatisation through competitive international bidding, resolution of Ajaokuta’s legacy liabilities and contractual disputes, and enforceable agreements for critical production inputs.

It also proposed a phased rehabilitation programme, beginning with the restoration of existing rolling mills using imported billets within the first three years to generate revenue, rebuild technical capacity and restore investor confidence.

The Society further urged investors to evaluate conventional blast-furnace technology alongside gas-based direct-reduced iron and electric arc furnace technology, noting that Nigeria’s natural gas resources could provide a competitive advantage.

Olarewaju-Alo said gas was equally critical to the country’s industrial transformation, not only as an energy source for steel production but also as feedstock for fertilisers, methanol, hydrogen and petrochemicals.

He maintained that increased domestic gas utilisation could support manufacturing, improve electricity supply and strengthen Nigeria’s energy security.

The conference themed, ‘Advancing Nigeria’s Industrial Revolution Through Gas Valorisation and AI-Driven Engineering Imperatives’, also examined artificial intelligence, smart manufacturing, energy efficiency and indigenous technological development.

The Society called on the federal government to prioritise gas infrastructure, local equipment fabrication, research commercialisation and responsible adoption of artificial intelligence to accelerate industrialisation.

It urged policymakers and investors to move beyond repeated promises and translate the Ajaokuta revival agenda into a commercially viable industrial project.

“Ajaokuta must become a productive industrial asset whose output serves Nigeria’s development. The time for a private sector-led revival is now,” the Society declared.

World.title: NAWOJ Tasks Members On Maternal, Child Health Reporting
World.content:
Segun Awofadeji in Bauchi

The Nigeria Association of Women Journalists (NAWOJ) has called on female journalists to intensify reporting on maternal and child health issues to promote public awareness, strengthen advocacy and hold relevant authorities accountable for healthcare delivery.

The Chairperson of NAWOJ Bauchi State chapter, Rashida Yusuf, made the call during a training on maternal and child health reporting organised for members of the association in the state on Thursday.

Yusuf said female journalists had a critical responsibility to give visibility to issues affecting women and children, particularly at the grassroots level.

“As female journalists, we have a very important role to play in promoting maternal and child health by giving visibility to issues affecting women and children,” she said.

She stressed the need for journalists to amplify the voices of women and children while ensuring that government and relevant authorities were held accountable for their policies, programmes and interventions.

“We must also amplify the voices of women and children to ensure that their concerns are heard and that they have access to the information and awareness they need, especially at the grassroots level,” Yusuf added.

She urged members to move beyond event coverage to sustained, solution-driven reporting that puts pressure on policymakers to improve healthcare services for women and children.

World.title: Lalong, Dariye, Badaru Lead Plateau Leaders to Back Tinubu’s Second Term
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

Former governors Simon Lalong and Joshua Dariye, alongside other political heavyweights in Plateau State, have thrown their weight behind President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

The leaders, under the banner of Arewa for Asiwaju (A4A), endorsed Tinubu at a high-level stakeholders’ meeting in Jos on Thursday, pledging to deliver massive votes for the All Progressives Congress (APC) across the state.

The meeting held yesterday in Jos brought together former ministers, former senators, former members of the House of Representatives, former commissioners and former local government chairmen.

By voice vote, participants unanimously adopted Tinubu, the Plateau State Governor and all other APC candidates for the forthcoming elections.

The meeting, chaired by Lalong, who is Deputy Chairman of the A4A Board of Trustees, also resolved to ensure the APC wins all elective positions in the state.

Lalong told the gathering that stakeholders were convinced Tinubu is committed to Nigeria’s development.

He said the President’s continued leadership would guarantee accelerated socio-economic growth and national transformation.

Dariye, in his remarks, commended the Tinubu administration for what he described as its contributions to Plateau State and the country.

According to him, President Tinubu deserved another term to consolidate on the achievements of his administration.

Also, the Director General of A4A and former Governor of Jigawa State, Badaru Abubakar, said the North should repay Tinubu’s spirit of equity, fairness and political inclusion with overwhelming support in 2027.

Badaru said he was satisfied with the commitment shown by the Plateau stakeholders, describing the endorsement as a major boost for the APC’s chances in Plateau and across Northern Nigeria.

He expressed optimism that the political commitment on display would translate into millions of votes for Tinubu and other APC candidates.

The meeting closed with a renewed pledge by A4A and its Plateau stakeholders to sustain political mobilisation, grassroots engagement and coordinated efforts to secure victory for the APC in 2027.

World.title: Seychelles Ambassador, St.Ange, Travels to Madagascar to Woo Investors
World.content:
Charles Ajunwa

Following an official initiative by the Chairman of the Board of the Madagascar’s Diego Suarez Regional Tourism Office, Dr Herilaza Hugues Randrianjohany, who addressed the President of the Republic of Seychelles, His Excellency Dr Patrick Herminie, on 16 August 2026, through the island’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Diaspora, and after receiving approval from the Seychellois government via Mrs. Sherin Francis of the Ministry of Tourism and Culture of Seychelles, the Diego Suarez Regional Tourism Office, in collaboration with the Madagascar National Tourism Office,

will host a high-level delegation from November 15 to 20, 2026.

Alain St.Ange, Seychelles’ Tourism Ambassador-at-Large, will lead the delegation. It will also include Mr Pascal Viroleau, Chief Executive Officer of the Vanilla Islands organisation. Ambassador St.Ange is remembered in the Indian Ocean Islands Group as one of the founding tourism personalities responsible for creating the Indian Ocean Vanilla Islands Organisation and served as its First President.

St.Ange, regarded as a tourism expert, has been invited to help guide Madagascar’s Diego Suarez Regional Tourism to become a stronger player in the Indian Ocean tourism region.

The mission will begin in Antananarivo with meetings with the Malagasy government to present the initiative to the highest authorities, reaffirm Madagascar’s role in the regional Vanilla Islands strategy, and secure the institutional support required for its implementation. The delegation will then travel to northern Madagascar, where an extensive programme will showcase the region’s tourism assets. The visit will begin at the Red Tsingy, a remarkable laterite formation sculpted by erosion from the Irodo River, followed by a tour of Diego Suarez, which will highlight its historical identity, cultural atmosphere, and high-quality hospitality infrastructure. On the second day, the guests will visit the Montagne des Français and the famous Three Bays, then enjoy lunch in Ramena, focusing on local cuisine and gastronomic tourism.

A key highlight of the mission will be a meeting at the Grand Hotel, bringing together local authorities, tourism operators, institutional partners, private-sector stakeholders, and the Tourism Office. Discussions will focus on practically integrating regional tourism products into combined Vanilla Islands travel itineraries.

Beyond the programme itself, the visit is expected to pave the way for several important developments for the destination: the creation of integrated tourism products that fully showcase Madagascar, the establishment of B2B partnerships with targeted tour operators and travel agencies, and the strengthening of northern Madagascar’s credibility in an increasingly competitive international tourism market.

Madagascar tourism is banking on Alain St.Ange’s extensive network to provide privileged access to key source markets and cruise companies. At the same time, the mission also aims to mobilise institutions and investors for hotel and infrastructure projects. Supported by the reputation of its two prominent guests, the initiative further seeks to generate lasting international media exposure commensurate with the destination’s potential.

World.title: MAGGI Celebrates 60 Years in Nigeria, Consumers to Win 12 SUVs, 60 Become Millionaires
World.content:
MAGGI, a brand of Nestle Nigeria Plc, has marked 60 years of being part of Nigeria’s food culture, family traditions and shared celebrations in MAGGI -NIFICENT style, with the launch of its MAGGI @ 60 Text and Win promotion, offering consumers the opportunity to win 12 brand new SUVs, 60 cash prizes of N1 million each, and thousands of other rewards, including household appliances, airtime and additional cash prizes.

Over six decades, MAGGI has evolved alongside the changing tastes, preferences and needs of Nigerian consumers, continually innovating its products while Nestle has invested in the local manufacturing capabilities and partnerships that support the brand’s growth.

Speaking at the anniversary press conference in Lagos, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Nestle Nigeria Plc, Wassim Elhusseini, described the milestone as a celebration of the trust Nigerians have placed in the brand over the years.

“When we look back on 60 years of MAGGI in Nigeria, we see far more than the history of a brand. We see generations of families who have made us part of their lives, investments that have helped strengthen local capabilities, and partnerships that have created opportunities for people and businesses across the country. These contributions remind us of the responsibility that comes with the trust Nigerians have placed in us. That means maintaining the quality and standards consumers expect from us, while continuing to listen to their needs. As we celebrate this milestone, our commitment is to keep earning that trust and contributing positively to Nigeria’s future,” he said.

Nestle’s investment in local manufacturing has also supported the development of MAGGI’s value chain, bringing together farmers, suppliers, transporters, distributors and retailers who contribute to the brand’s production and distribution across Nigeria.

To mark the anniversary, MAGGI is recognising and rewarding the consumers and business partners who have contributed to its journey.

Speaking on the anniversary celebrations, Category Business Manager for Culinary at Nestle Nigeria, Funmi Osineye, said the brand had planned a series of exciting activities to reward consumers and recognise the partners who have contributed to its success.

“We wanted to celebrate 60 years of MAGGI in a truly MAGGI-NIFICENT way, with the people who have made this journey possible at the heart of it all. Through our MAGGI @ 60 Text and Win promotion, we are giving 12 lucky Nigerians the opportunity to drive home brand-new SUVs and making 60 other millionaires, with N1 million each. There are also thousands of other exciting prizes to be won, including lots of deep freezers, triple-door refrigerators, cookers, ovens, microwaves, fans, airtime and several cash prizes to be won. It is our way of saying thank you to Nigerians for six wonderful decades and inviting everyone to celebrate with us,” she said.

To participate, consumers aged 18+ and above can purchase promotional packs of MAGGI Star, MAGGI Star Double Cube or MAGGI Chicken Flavour, find the unique code inside the pack and dial *8011*3# or scan the QR code on the packaging to follow the entry instructions and stand a chance to win in the weekly draws. The promotion runs from 1 November to 31 December 2026.

Beyond consumer rewards, MAGGI is recognising 15 of its leading distributors with an all-expenses-paid trip to Cairo Egypt, in appreciation of their longstanding partnership and contribution to the brand’s growth.

The anniversary will also feature the unveiling of a commemorative documentary chronicling MAGGI’s six-decade journey in Nigeria. Told through the experiences of consumers, farmers, distributors, creators and individuals who have helped shape the brand, including its first Marketing Manager, the documentary captures the people and defining moments behind MAGGI’s enduring place in Nigerian life.

Six decades on, MAGGI’s story continues to be told through the experiences of Nigerians who have grown up with the brand, shared it across generations and made it part of their own stories. It is this enduring connection that gives the anniversary its significance and makes the milestone worth celebrating.

World.title: FG Declares War on Food Poisoning, Says 53,000 Die Yearly
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The federal government has pledged to strengthen enforcement of food safety laws and professional regulation, following warnings that foodborne illnesses claim more than 53,000 lives annually in Nigeria.

The Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr. Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh, made the commitment in Abuja during a courtesy visit by the Nigerian Council of Food Science and Technology (NiCFoST), held to commemorate the World Science Day for Peace and Development themed ‘Common Ground through Science Diplomacy’.

Citing the World Health Organisation, Dr. Udeh said about 866 million people worldwide suffer foodborne illnesses yearly, leading to 1.552 million deaths, including 143,000 children under five, at an economic cost of $310 billion. Unsafe food, he said, can cause more than 200 diseases.

He listed widespread unsafe practices in Nigeria, including ripening fruit with calcium carbide, treating beans and grains with dichlorvos (sniper), using paracetamol to soften meat, applying detergents or bleaching agents in cassava processing, and adulterating palm oil with prohibited colours such as Sudan IV.

Udeh said Nigeria produces about 3,000 food science and technology professionals annually from about 70 tertiary institutions, but their utilisation, particularly in the public service, has been constrained by the absence of an established professional cadre. He urged institutions to conclude outstanding approvals for the cadre and to engage only qualified, NiCFoST-licensed professionals.

He said the priority is now effective implementation, noting “We have the laws, we have the structures, we have the framework, but we have to translate this to action.” He also drew attention to Sections 243 to 245 of the Criminal Code Act, which prescribe six months to two years imprisonment for offences involving harmful food, diseased meat and contaminated water.

To strengthen coordination, the minister announced plans to convene a high-level National Food System Stakeholders Meeting within the next one or two months, saying “Hold me accountable to making this happen.”

Corroborating the Minister, the Registrar of NiCFoST, Mrs. Veronica Ezeh, warned that consumers are unknowingly buying food laced with dangerous chemicals, particularly red palm oil adulterated with Sudan IV dye to make it look richer and more attractive.

Speaking at the briefing, Mrs. Ezeh demonstrated how the dye deepens the colour of palm oil, making adulterated oil almost indistinguishable from genuine oil. She said the same dye is also added to Bambara nut products used in preparing moi-moi, especially when traders lack enough palm oil to achieve the desired colour.

She said some traders know the practice is wrong but continue for financial gain, operating secretly while unsuspecting consumers purchase the contaminated products.



Ezeh also raised concerns over the chemical treatment of fruits to accelerate ripening, washing fruits in potentially contaminated water, and the open display of garri in markets, which she said exposes food to dust, human saliva, rodents and other hazards.

She warned that food contaminated by rodents carrying Lassa fever could expose consumers to infection, while poor handling and storage could facilitate cholera and other foodborne diseases, with unsafe food causing illnesses ranging from diarrhoea to cancer and, in severe cases, death.

“The solution to curb food safety practices in Nigeria is to allow the professionals to do their work. That is the missing link in food safety in Nigeria,” she said, insisting monitoring must begin from the source of raw materials.



Ezeh advocated improved packaging for locally processed foods, particularly garri, urging traders to seal products in clean nylon bags instead of exposing them openly in markets.

She stressed that effective government regulation, not individual tests by buyers, must guarantee safety, citing the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution, which assigns local governments responsibilities for markets and public health regulation.

She therefore urged the three tiers of government to deploy trained food science and technology officers to local government areas to monitor production, processing and sales, and restore public confidence in food safety.

World.title: FirstPower Pledges to Help Anambra Achieve 1,000MW Power Target, Commits N13.3bn Investment, Others
World.content:
David-Chyddy Eleke in Awka

First Power Electricity Distribution Company Limited, a subsidiary of Enugu Electricity Distribution Company (EEDC), has pledged to support Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, in achieving its electricity sector target of 1,000 megawatts in the state.

The Chairman of EEDC, Sir Emeka Offor, stated this yesterday at Anambra State Electricity Market Investment Roundtable, held in Awka, Anambra State.

Offor, who was represented by the MD/CEO of EEDC, Engr. Vincent Ekwekwu, stated that its subsidiary, FirstPower Electricity Distribution Company Limited, which manages power in Anambra State will fully support the vision of Anambra State government under Governor Soludo.

He said, “We are committed to building a strong, inclusive and commercially sustainable Anambra Electricity Market.

“We recognise that achieving reliable electricity supply requires the participation of government, regulators, existing operators and new investors. We therefore warmly welcome credible investments in generation, embedded power, renewable energy, distribution infrastructure and other electricity services.”

Speaking about the company’s investment in power sector in the state, Offor said, “FirstPower has committed the following; N13.3 billion, within next year 2027 in priority network investments. Another N40 billion has been planned for the following 2 years 2028 and 2029. These investments will strengthen distribution infrastructure, improve metering, increase network capacity and enhance electricity reliability across the state.

“We are also finalising arrangements with generating and Renewable Energy companies for approximately 205 megawatts of additional electricity capacity, while exploring over 420 megawatts of potential Embedded Distributed generation and interconnected mini-grid opportunities for collaboration with interested investors.

“These initiatives demonstrate our determination to support the state’s growing electricity requirements and provide the infrastructure necessary for sustainable economic development.

“I am pleased to announce that FirstPower is concluding PPA discussions to procure 55MW over the next few days. FirstPower and Greenewable Energy Ltd have also signed an MOU to develop 100 MW of embedded generation.

“Today, in this forum, FirstPower will sign Memoranda of Understanding with its investment partners to further our commitment to improving electricity reliability across the State. These partners include: Capstone Energies Limited for Distributed Embedded supply of 50 MW And North South Power Company Ltd for Distributed Embedded supply of 17 MW,” Offor said.

World.title: Hail, lightning and damaging winds are expected in Gauteng
World.content:
The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has warned Gauteng residents to brace for severe thunderstorms this weekend.

SAWS issued a Yellow Level 2 warning for severe thunderstorms over Mpumalanga, Limpopo and Gauteng, valid for Saturday, 14 November.

The weather service said that after a week of heatwaves across the central and eastern parts of the country, thunderstorms are expected over the Free State, North West, Gauteng, Mpumalanga, KwaZulu-Natal, Eastern Cape and Limpopo. The storms should bring some relief from the heat, but SAWS cautioned that severe thunderstorms are possible.



What Gauteng residents can expect

The stormy conditions are expected to continue until Sunday, with flooding possible in parts of the affected provinces.

The Gauteng Weather account on X said the whole province faces a 60% chance of rain, with storms expected between 14:00 and 23:59 on Saturday.

The overall forecast for Gauteng is partly cloudy and warm to hot, with scattered showers and thundershowers in the afternoon.

According to SAWS, the severe thunderstorms could cause localised flooding, damage to property, and disruptions to power and communications in Gauteng and parts of the North West, Free State, Limpopo and Mpumalanga.

How to stay safe during the storms

Residents should take precautions before the storms arrive. These include:

Avoiding crossing flooded roads, bridges and low-lying areas, whether on foot or in a vehicle

Staying indoors and away from windows during lightning

Parking vehicles under cover to protect them from hail

Unplugging electrical appliances to protect them from power surges

Keeping cellphones charged in case of power outages

Motorists should drive slowly, increase their following distance and switch on their headlights during heavy rain.



Residents living in informal settlements and low-lying areas should keep a close eye on rising water levels and move to higher ground if necessary.

SAWS will continue to monitor the weather system and update its warnings as conditions develop.

World.title: Report: Percy Tau on the verge of signing with top PSL club
World.content:
Former Bafana Bafana winger Percy Tau could be closing in on a sensational return to Mamelodi Sundowns.

The 32-year-old has been training with Masandawana over the past few weeks, with the club reportedly impressed by what they have seen from the former Al Ahly star.

According to Soccer Laduma, Sundowns head coach Miguel Cardoso has been impressed with Tau’s performances during training, with talks already underway over a possible deal.



“As you already know, Percy Tau is back at Chloorkop and training with the team. So far, he has been impressive, and the club has been impressed. Talks have already started about the possibility of a deal. Signs are pointing to the possibility of signing in the coming days if all goes well in the negotiations,” a source told the Siya crew.

There are also growing hints that Tau could be on his way back to the Tshwane giants.

Over the weekend, Sundowns defender Grant Kekana posted a picture of Tau at the club’s training ground on his Instagram page, further fuelling speculation about a possible reunion.

Tau training with Sundowns

Tau previously enjoyed success at Sundowns before moving to Europe, where he played for Brighton and Hove Albion and several clubs before joining Egyptian giants Al Ahly.

A return to Chloorkop would see the experienced attacker reunite with the club where he first established himself as one of South Africa’s most exciting football talents.

At 32, it seems likely that Sundowns will give the Lion of Judah a one year contract.



Will Percy last more than a year?

World.title: School calendar: When does Term 4 end?
World.content:
Public school learners across South Africa have less than four weeks of classes left before the 2026 academic year comes to an end.

According to the Department of Basic Education’s (DBE) official 2026 school calendar, public schools will close for the year on Wednesday, 9 December.

The closing date marks the end of a busy final term for learners, teachers and parents, with many schools now in the middle of year-end examinations.



When does Term 4 end?

Term 4 started on Tuesday, 6 October and runs for 10 weeks. The DBE’s calendar shows that Term 4 has 47 calendar days, all of which count as school days because the term has no public holidays.

Teachers will stay on slightly longer than learners. The calendar gives educators two additional administrative days, which extend their school year to 11 December.

The same dates apply to public schools in every province, including those in Johannesburg, Tshwane, Ekurhuleni, Sedibeng and the West Rand.

For reference, the full 2026 public school calendar runs as follows: Term 1 from 14 January to 27 March, Term 2 from 8 April to 26 June, Term 3 from 21 July to 23 September, and Term 4 from 6 October to 9 December. ; Term 2 from 8 April to 26 June; Term 3 from 21 July to 23 September;

The first national public holiday after teaching ends is the Day of Reconciliation on Wednesday, 16 December.

What about private schools?

Parents with children at independent schools may see an earlier closing date. Guidelines from the Independent Schools Association of Southern Africa (ISASA) show independent schools concluding the year on 4 December.



However, no single calendar applies to every independent school in South Africa. Many follow the public-school calendar, others follow an association calendar, and some set their own dates.

Parents whose children attend private schools should confirm dates directly with their schools.

When do schools reopen in 2027?

Learners will enjoy just over a month off before returning to class. The DBE’s published 2027 calendar shows Term 1 running from 13 January to 19 March.

Meanwhile, matric learners are still working through their final papers. The class of 2026 began writing their National Senior Certificate final examinations on Tuesday, 13 October.

World.title: Springboks back to No 1 in rankings after Wales beat New Zealand
World.content:
The Springboks slumped to defeat against France on Friday night, and as a result also lost 1.56 rankings points to slip to second in the World Rugby rankings behind New Zealand.

All expectations were that the All Blacks would claim a comfortable win over Wales on Saturday, and also take control of the southern standings in the Nations Championship.

However, no one could have predicted the historic turn of events, which saw Wales clinch a 35-28 victory to beat the All Blacks for the first time since 1953.



Tries from Tomos Williams, Dewi Lake, Archie Griffin, Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit inspired a remarkable result after the scores had been tied 21-21 at half-time.

In the World Rugby rankings, the All Blacks lost two full points, enabling the Springboks to leapfrog immediately back into No 1 spot.

Yet, New Zealand still have a one-point advantage over the Springboks in the Nations Championship southern standings after claiming two losing bonus-points on Saturday.

HOW THE RANKINGS NOW LOOK AFTER SPRINGBOKS, ALL BLACKS LOSE

Rank Country Points 1 Springboks 91.53 2 All Blacks 90.65 3 France 89.05 4 Ireland 88.70 5 England 86.99 6 Scotland 84.40 7 Australia 83.12 8 Argentina 82.09 9 Wales 79.37 10 Fiji 77.79 11 Italy 76.30 12 Japan 75.25 13 Georgia 74.23 14 Portugal 68.24 15 USA 67.80

no excuses from rassie erasmus

After the Springboks’ disappointing defeat, Rassie Erasmus was frank about his assessment of the game.

“France played really well and we didn’t, so I can’t find a lot of excuses. They took their opportunities when they got them and we didn’t.

“It’s probably a cliché, but I definitely think we had enough opportunities and there were simple tries we could have scored with one last pass, and perhaps one or two wrong decisions, such as not kicking for the corner and rather expecting the referee to give four penalties in a row.



“In front of a crowd like this you might feel you have dominance, but it’s just human not to keep on penalising the home team if they’ve already got a card or two. But in the end, it comes down to the fact that they played well, and we didn’t.”

World.title: Johannesburg Water announces an 18-hour water outage in this suburb on Tuesday
World.content:
A modern kitchen sink with running water, a sleek faucet, and a vase on the countertop. Image: Pexels

Johannesburg Water has announced a planned water supply interruption that will leave parts of Bedford Park without water for 18 hours next week.

The utility will shut off supply from 6:00 on Tuesday, 17 November 2026, until 00:00 on Wednesday, 18 November 2026. The outage will affect all streets in the parts of the suburb that receive water from the Linksfield Reservoir.

Johannesburg Water listed the maintenance under Region E in its daily water supply system status update, issued on the afternoon of 13 November.



Why Johannesburg Water is cutting supply

According to Johannesburg Water, the interruption will allow its teams to install a bulk meter. Customers will have no water while the work is under way.

Bulk meters measure the volume of water flowing into a supply zone, helping utilities track consumption and detect losses in the network.

Johannesburg Water said the project will benefit customers through improved service delivery and continuity of water supply.

Alternative supply still to be confirmed

Johannesburg Water has not yet confirmed whether it will provide alternative water supply, such as water tankers, during the shutdown. The utility said it will provide further details later.

Residents can prepare ahead of Tuesday by:

Filling clean containers with drinking and cooking water on Monday evening

Storing extra water in buckets for flushing toilets

Keeping taps closed during the outage to prevent flooding when supply returns

Checking on elderly neighbours who may struggle to collect water

Households with water tanks should fill them before 6:00 on Tuesday. Businesses in the area, including restaurants and salons, should also plan for disruptions.



Water may take some time to return to full pressure after the work ends, especially in higher-lying areas. Residents may notice discoloured water or air in the pipes once supply returns. Running taps briefly should clear it.

Residents can log calls or report problems through the following channels:

Call: 010 061 4470 or 086 056 2874

X: @JHBWater

Facebook: Johannesburg Water

Customers should keep their account number or street address handy when logging a call.

Johannesburg Water also publishes daily system status updates, which residents can follow for any changes to the maintenance schedule.

Residents who still have no water by Wednesday morning should report it through one of these channels.

World.title: Eskom announces an 11-hour power outage in Gauteng on Sunday
World.content:
Silhouette of power lines and pole against a vibrant sunset sky. Image: Pexels

Eskom has announced a planned electricity supply interruption that will leave the whole of Clayville in Gauteng without power for 11 hours on Sunday, 15 November.

The power utility will switch off supply from 8:00 to 19:00 to carry out maintenance on its distribution network.

Eskom’s Gauteng Communication and Stakeholder Management team issued the notice in its November 2026 Connect bulletin for the Gauteng Cluster.



Why Eskom is switching off the power

According to Eskom, the interruption is necessary to perform essential maintenance on its distribution power lines. The outage will affect the entire suburb rather than selected streets or sections.

Planned maintenance outages are separate from load shedding. Eskom schedules them in advance to reduce the risk of unplanned breakdowns on the network.

Eskom thanked customers for their cooperation and apologised for any inconvenience the maintenance may cause.

However, the utility also warned that the work may not go ahead as planned. Its disclaimer states that if circumstances beyond its control arise, the maintenance may not proceed as communicated.

Safety warning for Clayville residents

Eskom urged customers to treat all electrical appliances as live at all times during the outage. Residents should not attempt electrical repairs or touch exposed wiring, as power could be restored without warning.

Households can prepare ahead of Sunday by:



Charging cellphones, power banks and laptops on Saturday evening

Keeping fridges and freezers closed to preserve food

Switching off sensitive appliances to protect them from power surges when supply returns

Planning meals that do not require electric cooking

Households that rely on electric gates, alarms or medical equipment should make backup arrangements before 8:00.

Eskom has listed several channels for customers who need assistance:

Download the self-help MyEskom Customer app

WhatsApp: 08600 37566

USSD: Dial *120*37566#

Bill-related enquiries: csonline.eskom.co.za, Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 16:00

Supply-related enquiries: Eskom Contact Centre on 08600 37566, 24 hours a day

Customers should keep their account or meter number handy when they contact the utility.

Residents who still have no power after 19:00 on Sunday should log a call through one of these channels.

World.title: Weather: Brace for a wet, stormy and windy Sunday across SA
World.content:
Dark clouds gather as South Africa prepares for a wet, stormy and windy Sunday. Image: AI Illustration

Here is what the weather has in store for KZN, the Free State, and the North West on Sunday 15 November 2026.

Orange Level 5 severe thunderstorm warning: Flooding of roads, settlements and low-lying areas, as well as power and communication disruptions, are expected in the far eastern parts of the Free State and western parts of KwaZulu-Natal.

Yellow Level 2 severe thunderstorm warning: Severe storms could cause localised flooding, property damage and power and communication disruptions in parts of the Free State and North West and KwaZulu-Natal.



Extremely high fire danger conditions are expected in parts of the Free State and North West.

KWAZULU-NATAL

World.title: SAPS report raises questions in Zim opposition leader’s case
World.content:
Job Sikhala and his uncle were arrested in Pretoria in November 2025. Images: Facebook/Crime Watch zw

A South African Police Service (SAPS) forensic report has reportedly found no fingerprints belonging to Zimbabwean opposition politician Job Sikhala or his uncle, Alexander Thema, among the prints lifted at the scene of an explosives case they are facing in Pretoria.

SAPS forensic report finds no matching fingerprints

The report, dated 16 July 2026, was compiled by the SAPS Local Criminal Record Centre in Pretoria.

It compared the fingerprints and palm prints of the two men with those recovered during investigations.



The findings were marked “NEGATIVE”, indicating that neither man’s prints were identified, either fully or partially.

The development raises fresh questions about the prosecution’s case against the two Zimbabweans, who have consistently denied possessing the explosives allegedly discovered in their vehicle.

Sikhala and his uncle deny explosives charges

Sikhala and Thema were arrested on 6 November 2025 after police stopped and searched their vehicle along Kgosi Mampuru Street in Pretoria.



According to reports of the case, officers discovered 26 blasting cartridges and 15 connector cap fuses during the search.

The two men were subsequently charged with possession of explosives and granted bail of R10 000 each.

The state did not oppose their release.

Job sikhala case: Defence alleges explosives were planted in vehicle

Sikhala, a former Zimbabwean legislator and leader of the National Democratic Working Group (NDWG), has maintained that he was framed.



His defence has alleged that he was lured to a meeting in Pretoria, where one of the individuals briefly left with the vehicle keys.

The lawyers believe this provided an opportunity for the explosives to be planted in the vehicle.

Outstanding forensic evidence raises further questions

The case was postponed to 3 August 2026 to allow investigators to complete outstanding forensic investigations.



According to a report by House of Africa, the matter was subsequently postponed to 28 August to allow prosecutors to assess the investigation docket and determine whether there was sufficient evidence to proceed.

The latest developments have also raised questions about the handling of the forensic evidence.

The Observer Zim reported that fingerprint and DNA results, together with CCTV footage allegedly showing the explosives being planted, were missing from documents handed to the defence.

World.title: Discontinuation claims about popular drink turn out to be a prank
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africans were briefly left wondering whether a popular party favourite was about to disappear from shelves.

This comes after a statement claiming that Jägermeister would be discontinued began circulating online.

The statement, dated 9 November, claimed that the decision followed an internal review of South African market operations, with 31 January 2027 set as the final date.

But there was a catch.

World.title: From heatwave to thunderstorm: Heavy downpours expected in these areas
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The South African Weather Service has issued a warning for severe thunderstorms and heavy downpours across parts of the country this weekend.

The warning, valid from this afternoon, is expected over Free State, North West, Gauteng, Mpumalanga, KwaZulu-Natal, and Limpopo.

For the Western Cape, a Yellow Level 1 warning of damaging winds for Saturday has been issued.

It comes after a week of heatwaves in various areas.

READ | Joburg residents urged to take precautions as heatwave continues

The City’s Emergency Management Services has urged residents, particularly those in low-lying areas, to avoid crossing flooded roads, rivers and streams.

Emergency Services spokesperson Robert Mulaudzi extended the same caution to motorists.

“We are pleading with our residents, especially those in our low-lying areas, to avoid crossing rivers and streams while conducting their daily activities. “We encourage our motorists to exercise caution while driving, extend a safe following distance and try to avoid crossing flooded roads and low-lying bridges.”

Mulaudzi said emergency service authorities will remain on high alert, monitoring all seven regions of the city for any emergencies which might occur.

World.title: No major incidents reported as matric exams near end
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Department of Basic Education is gearing up for the marking phase as the 2026 National Senior Certificate examinations near their end.

To date, the department's spokesperson, Terence Khala, said they have noted a few minor incidents reported, but none are serious enough to affect the integrity of the examinations.

READ | Senior teachers opt for early retirement as government trims wage bill

This is as he points to taxi violence in the Western Cape and scholar transport challenges in Gauteng as some of the issues experienced during the examination period.

But upon being notified of this, the department acted.

“The sector kicked in and was able to make sure that the requisite protocols were put in place. Learners in Gauteng were able to write adequately and equally in the Western Cape. “And I think it's only for us to commend the system and commend every individual that forms part of the system that assists us to make sure that we can really take this massive undertaking and make it a seamless one,” Khala said.

Markers, according to the department, will get to work on 1 December.

World.title: Six people killed in head-on collision on Eastern Cape N2
World.content:
At least six people have died in a horror crash on the N2 in the Eastern Cape.

The victims were travelling in a minibus taxi when it collided head-on with a truck on Saturday morning.

Provincial transport spokesperson Unathi Binqose said the minibus taxi was travelling from Alice towards Bizana while the truck was travelling from Kokstad towards Mzamba when the accident happened.

"Preliminary information suggests that the Toyota Quantum crossed into the path of the oncoming truck, resulting in a head-on collision. "There is also a suspicion that driver fatigue may have contributed to the crash. However, the exact circumstances surrounding the collision remain subject to police investigation," he said.

Three others were seriously injured, while three others sustained slight injuries.

"The injured were attended to by emergency services and transported for medical treatment".

The victims are believed to be university students travelling home to Bizana.

This comes just a day after seven people died in another crash on the N2 near Ndabakazi.

World.title: Madlanga Commission hears ex-JMPD top cop allegedly forced officers to take bribe
World.content:
PRETORIA - A major drug bust operation in Johannesburg has led to explosive testimony at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry.

The commission heard on Friday how former JMPD superintendent Phineas Manyama allegedly instructed officers to release suspects and accept whatever money was offered in return.

READ | LIVE | JMPD corruption under the spotlight at Madlanga

Testifying at the commission Tactical Response Unit officer Michael Potsane said refusing the instruction came with threats of dismissal, arrest or even death.

He testified that he regarded the instruction as unlawful and did not comply with it.

World.title: Hot weather, dry taps, fuming Joburg residents
World.content:
SOWETO - Water shortages are worsening across various parts of Johannesburg, with residents reporting days without water supply amid the heatwave.

In Soweto, one resident detailed how the community has been without water since Tuesday, with supply returning briefly during the early hours of the morning.

“We've been having challenges with water in this community whereby each and every weekend we don't have water at all. It is becoming a new normal now,” the resident said.

The resident adds that the situation becomes more concerning during the current heatwave when residents need water the most.

“We are encouraged to drink more water because people are going to suffer because of dehydration, but at this particular moment, Joburg Water is not doing justice to us."

He said adding to the frustration is the lack of communication between Joburg Water and residents.

READ | Joburg residents urged to take precautions as heatwave continues

In a statement on Saturday, Joburg Water said bulk supply meters in the Roodepoort and Soweto regions, which were closed on Thursday to rescue and boost bulk supply levels, commenced reopening on Friday afternoon.

The water utility said it is worth noting that systems were not fully opened but taken back to their original curtailment before being fully closed on Thursday.

“While some bulk supplier systems have stabilised and recovered, there are still several systems which will take time to recover over the next few days. The recovery is also impacted by the demand for the system as they are integrated. “The affected Johannesburg Water reservoirs will first need to fill to acceptable levels before the system stabilises. Customers may experience low pressure or intermittent supply and, in some cases, no water until the system recovers,” the statement read.

In the meantime, Joburg Water said alternative water arrangements are being made and deployed through the central and regional coordination groups.

World.title: A grave clash: One family's search, many families' pain
World.content:
LICHTENBURG - A quest for closure for one family has thrown Boikhutso’s cemetery in Lichtenburg, North West and countless other families into chaos and heartache.

The families claim graves were disturbed and their dignity upended during an exhumation process conducted by the North West Department of Health after it got a court order in June 2023 to dig up graves, searching for a man missing from the old Thusong Hospital.

It was suspected that he had died and received a pauper’s burial at this cemetery.

However, families say the process has left the cemetery in disarray, with some unable to identify the graves of their relatives.

Mmakhumo Moja’s family is among those affected.

READ | Fort Jackson SAPS building turns into haven for criminals

She says both her parents’ graves have since vanished, lost in the shuffle. They found the graves disturbed, soil scattered and headstones missing.

"We want our graves, and we want to know exactly where they are located. After the exhumation, we were supposed to come and clean up, but we didn't know whose graves we were cleaning. When we're supposed to do some of our cultural rites at the grave, it's a problem. “When you carry out traditional rituals, you have to come to the ancestors and engage them. But the place is a mess; it's dug up, and there are holes everywhere,” Moja said.

The North West Health Department spokesperson Tebogo Lekgethwane insists it consulted some families ahead of the dig, and flat-out denies leaving the cemetery in shambles.

But three years on, the cemetery is still in a mess, and the family’s still waiting.

They’re holding out for answers, longing for restoration, and just a little respect for their dear departed.

eNCA Bafedile Moerane filed this report.

World.title: Fort Jackson SAPS building turns into haven for criminals
World.content:
MDANTSANE - Once a well-resourced police station where officers carried out their duties but today the Fort Jackson SAPS building in Mdantsane in the Eastern Cape has become a haven for criminal activity.

Criminals have taken over the building, vandalising offices that were meant to benefit the people of Mdantsane and surrounding areas.

This has left Mdantsane residents questioning how a government-owned building intended to strengthen policing could be allowed to deteriorate while crime escalates.

READ | Vandals savage Eastern Cape school

According to the community crime organisation, the Buffalo City Special Team Task Force, criminals have had easy access to the building since a taxi crashed into the perimeter fence earlier this year.

The full extend of the damage remains unclear, however police suspect opportunists trashed the premises after hours.

Eastern Cape police spokesperson Siphokazi Mawisa said following the incidents, cases were opened, and arrests were made.

"The cases are currently before court, and the suspects are out on bail,”she said.

Measures are being put in place to deploy police units that will utilise the building on a 24-hour basis to safeguard it.

eNCA's Ronald Masinda filed this report.

World.title: Love under watch: How technology is fuelling intimate partner abuse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Your enemy is closer than you think. For many Kenyan women, the person who demands a phone password, reads private messages and tracks their movements through a screen is not a faceless troll. He is the man they live with, or the one they used to.

That is the uncomfortable picture painted by the recently released 2025–2626 Kenya Mini Demographic and Health Survey (KMDHS), which measured technology-facilitated gender-based violence, abuse committed, assisted, aggravated or amplified through digital tools.

The most common form of abuse is online control, reported by 19 per cent of women, followed by hacking at 5 per cent and online sexual harassment or cyber sexual abuse at 3 per cent. Most of it happens on platforms women use every day.

“Sixty-seven per cent of women who experienced digital gender violence say it happened on social media, with Facebook cited by 59 per cent. Messaging apps follow at 47 per cent, with WhatsApp at 26 per cent. Among girls aged 15–19, 77 per cent reported abuse on social media.”

The report shows how widespread the abuse is. “Twenty-six percent of women age 15–49 have ever experienced technology-facilitated violence from any perpetrator,” the report says, and 21 per cent experienced it often or sometimes in the 12 months before the survey. Among women who have ever had a husband or intimate partner, 27 per cent have experienced it at the hands of a current, most recent or previous partner.

The burden is not spread evenly, the report states that Nairobi City records the highest lifetime experience from any perpetrator at 33 per cent, followed by Murang’a and Baringo at 32 per cent each.

“For abuse by an intimate partner, Homa Bay 36 per cent and Baringo 35 per cent lead, while in the 12 months before the survey Trans Nzoia topped the list at 31 per cent. At the other end, Mandera and Wajir report just 3 per cent, a figure that may say as much about silence as about safety,” the report says

The picture is similar among young people. A 2024 rapid study by the Collaborative Centre for Gender and Development, working with the UNFPA and Women Economic Empowerment, found that nearly 90 per cent of young adults enrolled in three Nairobi tertiary institutions had witnessed TFGBV, and 39 per cent had experienced it personally.

Among women who have ever had a husband or intimate partner, 27 per cent have experienced gender violence committed by a current, most recent or previous partner, and 22 per cent did so in the past year. When women were asked who was responsible, the answer was blunt. Current husbands or intimate partners accounted for 61 per cent of perpetrators, former partners for 22 per cent and strangers for just 13 per cent.

Women who have never been married or had a partner face a different threat. For them, the most common perpetrators are strangers at 45 per cent, online attackers at 23 per cent and friends or acquaintances at 20 per cent.

Warning signs

Control is the common thread. The report describes such behaviours by a male partner as “important early warning signs that may escalate into violence within a relationship.”

Sixty-one per cent of ever-partnered women say their current or most recent partner has shown at least one controlling behaviour, and 27 per cent report three or more. Half say he has been jealous or angry when they spoke to other men, and 36 per cent say he insists on knowing where they are at all times. Others describe partners who demand passwords or read messages without consent.

Age and marital status matter. Technology-based gender violence is lowest among girls aged 15–19 at 10 per cent and highest among women aged 20–24 at 37 per cent. Forty-one per cent of divorced, separated or widowed women have experienced it, compared with 27 per cent of married women and 19 per cent of the never married.

Yet the digital rights advocate Cherie Oyier, a programmes officer at the Kenya ICT Action Network (KICTANet), says the low figures in some places should not be read as safety. Much of the abuse happens where nobody can see it.

“Closed applications, meaning like WhatsApp, those are the ones that most people, intimate partners will usually use,” she says. “Even as you are scrolling the internet to look for these instances, we may not be able to catch it. But it does not mean that it is not happening or that it is at a lower level.”

Culture also silences women. “Most women are told just endure, this is what marriage is about,” Oyier says. “Sometimes they don’t know, it’s so overt, like it doesn’t come out clearly that this is abuse. So most of the times, it is not reported.”

Online, abuse has been turned into entertainment. “It has become banter,” she says. “Even the people who are experiencing it have trivialised it. It’s now ingrained to you, like this is something that happens, you should expect it actually. If you post a picture, one of the things that you are thinking about is what kind of comments am I going to get.”

A 2023 report by KICTANet found that more than 30 per cent of Kenyans have experienced some form of TFGBV, while 90 per cent have witnessed it. In 2025, KICTANet and Equality Now released survivor testimonies showing how deceptive online job offers, grooming and image-based abuse leave women exposed, and how many had never received counselling despite years of trauma.

The stakes are not only digital. The 2025 Report of the Technical Working Group on GBV Including Femicide, cited in the KMDHS, indicated that many cases of homicide of women and girls, and of sexual and physical harm directed towards them, “are preceded by online and offline harassment using digital tools.”

For survivors, the law offers little comfort. “The technology is moving at a very fast pace compared to the laws,” Oyier says. In an attempt to bolster the gaps, Kenya has many fragmented laws. “You’ll have the Data Protection Act, the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, the Children’s Act, that to some extent touch on online issues, but they don’t really cohesively cover the different instances of TFGBV.”

The police, she says, often do not know either. “Just imagine you’re a woman who is in a village, for example, a village in Siaya, and you encounter violence. For you to even understand which law apply is very stressful.”

“You’re going through psychological stress and depression, and you’re also supposed to figure out which law applies in your situation. It causes even more problems for victims and survivors.”

Flagging abusive language

Artificial intelligence is adding a new layer. Even so, Oyier cautions against writing it off. “We should not vilify AI completely,” she says. KICTANet has built a lexicon to help flag abusive language and runs a tracker for online gender-based violence. “One person cannot sit down and look at everything on social media. When AI is able to pull every post that has this word, a human content moderator is able to look through it with local context and see is this TFGBV or not.”

The KMDHS findings further show that exposure to TFGBV varies across age groups and digital platforms.

“Younger women are particularly exposed on social media, with 77 per cent of women aged 15–19 and 72 per cent of those aged 20–24 who experienced TFGBV reporting abuse on social media platforms, compared with 50 per cent of women aged 40–49.”

However, messaging applications tell a different story. Women aged 40–49 reported the highest exposure through these platforms at 54 per cent, compared with 30 per cent among teenagers aged 15–19.

Wealth also influences where women encounter online abuse. Exposure on social media increases from 45 per cent among women in the lowest wealth quintile to 74 per cent among those in the highest. Conversely, women in the lowest wealth quintile report greater exposure through messaging applications, at 62 per cent, compared with 39 per cent among those in the highest wealth quintile.

These differences suggest that TFGBV cuts across age and economic backgrounds, although the platforms through which women experience it vary.

World.title: Not so fast: Court slams brake on ARA over wealth forfeiture
World.content:
Felix Mecha Nyakundi could not provide a plausible explanation for how he amassed his wealth.

The Court of Appeal has ruled that the government cannot go after a person’s wealth without prior investigations to establish reasonable grounds for suspecting that the property constitutes proceeds of crime.

In a landmark judgment, Justices Patrick Kiage, Jamila Mohammed and Nduma Nderi said that although it does not require a person to be charged for a crime for the Asset Recovery Agency (ARA) to come knocking, it bears the responsibility to link the wealth or cash to a crime.

World.title: Back to sender: Aisha Jumwa returns to UDA
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto welcome former Cabinet Secretary Aisha Jumwa back to the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA) on November 12, 2026. [PCS]

Former Cabinet Secretary Aisha Jumwa has returned to President William Ruto’s United Democratic Alliance (UDA), ending a three-month political fallout with the ruling party that saw her join opposition outfit Wiper Patriotic Front and declare support for the one-term movement ahead of the 2027 General Election.

President Ruto welcomed Jumwa back into UDA at State House, Mombasa, on Thursday, November 12, 2026, in a political reunion that could reshape alignments in Kilifi County and the wider Coast region as parties position themselves for next year's elections.

The reunion comes barely three months after Jumwa dramatically announced her departure from UDA, accusing the party leadership of frustrating her political ambitions and failing to support her quest for the Kilifi gubernatorial seat.

On July 30, 2026, Jumwa announced her resignation during a press conference at her Kakuyuni home in Malindi, saying her attempts to have her grievances addressed by the President had repeatedly been unsuccessful.

Among her concerns was what she described as humiliation and rejection within the ruling party, including an alleged incident in which she was chased out of State House during a meeting between Ruto and Coast leaders.

She also accused sections of the ruling coalition of undermining her gubernatorial ambitions, claiming that the political arrangements being pursued in Kilifi were designed to deny her an opportunity to contest for the county's top seat.

President William Ruto recieve former Cabinet Secretary Aisha Jumwa back to the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA) on November 12, 2026. [PCS]

Jumwa, who was among UDA's founding members and one of Ruto's most vocal mobilisers at the Coast during the 2022 elections, said her loyalty to the people of Kilifi outweighed her allegiance to any political party.

"My loyalty to the people of Kilifi will always be greater than my loyalty to any political party. The voice of the people of Kilifi is louder than the voice of UDA," she declared during her exit announcement.

Her departure marked a significant political shift, particularly given her central role in mobilising support for Ruto in the Coast region.

In August, Jumwa turned to the opposition, where she was warmly received by Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka, who visited her at her Kakuyuni residence on August 14 alongside a delegation of party leaders, including Nyali MP Mohamed Ali, Kitui Senator Enoch Wambua and Wundanyi MP Danson Mwashako.

Kalonzo subsequently proposed Jumwa for the position of Wiper Deputy Party Leader, citing her political experience and influence, while also backing her ambition to contest the Kilifi governorship on a Wiper ticket.

Jumwa embraced the new political alliance, declaring support for the one-term movement and threatening to mobilise UDA supporters in Kilifi to deregister from the ruling party and join Wiper.

"We are the ones who registered UDA members in Kilifi, and we are embarking on a grassroots campaign to deregister them from UDA and join Wiper," she said at the time.

On September 8, she attended a meeting involving Wiper leaders and Coast gubernatorial aspirants, including Mohammed Ali and Danson Mwashako, as the party intensified efforts to expand its influence in the region.

However, the political alliance has now taken another turn, with Jumwa returning to the party she had accused of frustrating her ambitions.

Announcing her return, President Ruto welcomed the former Cabinet Secretary back into UDA, signalling renewed efforts to consolidate the ruling party's support in the Coast region.

"I look forward to working with her to advance the party’s transformation agenda at the Coast and across the country. We remain committed to uniting leaders and Kenyans around our shared vision of a united, inclusive and prosperous Kenya," the President said.

Her return comes as Ruto steps up political mobilisation in the Coast region ahead of the 2027 elections, with Kilifi emerging as an important battleground for competing political formations.

Jumwa's political journey has been characterised by shifting alliances. She previously served under the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM), representing Malindi in Parliament before becoming Kilifi's first Woman Representative between 2013 and 2017.

She later became one of Ruto's key political allies and served in his Cabinet.

World.title: Buxton estate tensions escalate after county officials attacked
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units. [Robert Menza, Standard]

A dispute over the multibillion-shilling Buxton Point housing project in Mombasa turned violent after county officials were allegedly attacked while enforcing a government order suspending construction over outstanding contractual obligations.

The confrontation came a day after County Executive Committee Member (CECM) for Lands, Housing, and Urban Development Mohamed Hussein ordered GulfCap Real Estate to halt all construction activities pending the resolution of disputes involving the county government and hundreds of former Buxton Estate residents.

The officials were reportedly pelted with stones as they attempted to serve the developer with an enforcement notice, with allegations that individuals linked to businessman Suleiman Shahbal were involved in the confrontation.

Hussein condemned the incident, saying attempts to intimidate government officers would not derail efforts to enforce the law and protect public interests.

"Let them bring goons, machetes, and stones if they want. I am not intimidated. I will execute my duties, and nobody will threaten me. The law must be followed, regardless of who you are or how much money you have," he said.

"We are here for the people of Mombasa, and we will ensure their rights are protected. Nobody is above the law," he added.

The November 10 enforcement notice, issued by County Director of Physical Planning Qassim Ali, directed GulfCap Real Estate to stop further development activities and obtain valid construction permits.

The notice, issued under Section 72(1) of the Physical and Land Use Planning Act, cited construction under a varied development plan without county approval and an ongoing dispute involving the developer, former tenants, and the county government.

The notice was reportedly received by the project's manager, Billy Okendo.

At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units. [Robert Menza, Standard]

At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county government and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units and commercial spaces developed in the first and second phases.

An addendum to the agreement signed on January 15, 2020, outlines the county's entitlement, with the allocation expected to be transferred upon completion of the second phase.

In a letter dated April 30, 2025, the county demanded 10 per cent of the proposed 1,800 housing units, translating to 180 apartments. The demand was renewed in February 2026, with the county seeking details on how the allocation would be implemented.

However, in correspondence dated September 22, 2026, the Department of Lands, Urban Planning and Housing expressed concern over what it described as the developer's failure to provide substantive responses to previous demands.

The county also questioned whether GulfCap had provided performance security equivalent to 10 per cent of the total construction cost for each phase, as required under the agreement.

It further demanded proof of payment of the Project Development Fee, which is payable in instalments as the project progresses.

The county said it had also raised technical and planning concerns during a meeting with the developer on April 15, 2026, including the need to address outstanding issues and resubmit the masterplan application.

But the dispute goes beyond the county's financial and contractual entitlement, with more than 500 former residents accusing the developer of failing to honour promises made when they were displaced in 2019.

John Tsuma, Secretary-General of the Buxton Tenants Welfare Association, said former residents had waited for more than seven years to return to their homes despite assurances that they would be prioritised once construction was completed.

"We are very disappointed by what happened. We had a meeting with the CECM, and he made it clear that all construction activities should stop until the outstanding issues are resolved. We did not go there to fight anybody. We wanted the directive implemented," Tsuma said.

He accused the developer of benefiting from the project while former residents continued to struggle to secure the houses they were promised.

"The developer has benefited from A to Z. He was given land by the county government, and the houses were sold off-plan. Yet, when it comes to fulfilling the promises made to former residents, we are still being taken around in circles," he said.

Tsuma said residents were not demanding free houses but wanted the affordable tenant-purchase arrangement they were promised before leaving the estate.

"We are not asking for free houses. We want the tenant-purchase arrangement that was promised to us so that we can pay for the houses and return to our homes," he said.

He also questioned why the developer had allegedly failed to surrender the county government's 184 housing units under the joint venture arrangement.

Mohamed Mzee Rubea, chairman of the evicted Buxton residents, said the money paid to the families during their displacement was a relocation allowance and not compensation for their homes.

He said the former tenants were given Sh240,000, with assurances that they would rent alternative accommodation for 12 months and return once the houses were completed.

"What we received was relocation money, not compensation for our houses. We were told to take the money and rent houses for 12 months and that we would be the first people to return once construction was completed. But here we are, more than seven years later, still waiting," Rubea said.

He said the original agreement involved 522 former tenants who were promised priority access to houses under the redevelopment.

Rubea added that each household was also promised Sh60,000 as a deposit towards acquiring a house under the tenant-purchase scheme.

"We were promised Sh60,000 as a deposit for those who would take up the houses. The developer later said the money would only be given to those who actually acquired the units. We are still waiting, and many of us have not received anything," he said. At the heart of the dispute is a joint venture agreement between the county and the developer, which provides for the county to receive 10 per cent of all housing units. [Robert Menza, Standard]

He further claimed that the county had written to the developer in 2023, 2024, and 2025 seeking engagement over the outstanding commitments.

Mutua Mutia, another former resident, said the prolonged dispute had left families frustrated, especially after they were promised they would return within a year.

"I have lived in Buxton since I was a young boy. My firstborn child is now more than 30 years old, and the history of Buxton is one that pains us. We were evicted with the promise that we would return after one year, but today it is seven years and we are still struggling," Mutia said.

The former residents are also demanding the reconstruction of an Early Childhood Development (ECD) centre demolished to pave the way for the project, as well as the construction of a promised community social centre.

Hussein said the county had yet to receive either facility or its share of the housing project.

"The county has not received its 10 per cent share to date. There was an agreement that the demolished ECD centre would be reconstructed and handed over to the county, alongside a community social centre, but we have not received either," he said.

The first phase of Buxton Point delivered 584 housing units in 2023, while the second phase is expected to provide between 1,400 and 1,500 additional apartments. Completion had been scheduled for August 2027.

However, GulfCap Real Estate Chief Executive Officer Chris Ochieng defended the developer's position, saying 492 housing units would be handed over to buyers by December.

While urging the county to stop politicising the project, Ochieng warned that the ongoing controversy risks disrupting the project’s completion and affecting hundreds of workers who depend on it for their livelihoods.

He said the county government's 10 per cent share would be transferred upon completion of the project.

He also maintained that the developer had supported displaced residents by providing Sh240,000 for relocation and offering them preferential rates to purchase apartments.

Ochieng said the continued involvement of county officials in the dispute was unfortunate, particularly at a time when 492 homeowners are expecting to take possession of their houses in December.

He noted that the controversy was not only creating uncertainty among prospective homeowners but also threatening the livelihoods of hundreds of people employed directly and indirectly through the project.

“It is very unfortunate that Mombasa County officials are bringing politics into a national project. We have 492 homeowners who expect to take possession of their units by December. Beyond the homeowners, hundreds of people depend on this project for employment and their daily livelihoods,” said Ochieng.

He called on the county leadership to allow the project to proceed without unnecessary political interference, arguing that Mombasa has previously witnessed housing projects that stalled despite significant public interest.

World.title: Sakaja defends Sh43.7b drop in Nairobi County's pending bills before Senate
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja tells Senate that the Sh118 billion in pending bills was inherited from his predecessors. [File, Standard]

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has told the Senate that pending bills in the city have been reduced from Sh118.79 billion to Sh75.07 billion through verification and payment.

Sakaja revealed that internal verification established that the Sh43.73 billion reduction was not achieved solely through payments but also involved legal assessments, court-ordered adjustments and the verification of disputed claims.

The governor, who appeared before the Senate County Public Accounts Committee at Parliament Buildings in Nairobi on Monday, said addressing the inherited debt required establishment of a verification committee to scrutinise the entire outstanding amount and establish the validity of the claims.

“The reduction of Nairobi County pending bills by Sh 43.73 billion was not achieved entirely through cash payments but also involved adjustments arising from legal assessments, suspended government-guaranteed loans, court-ordered reductions and disputed claims,” said Sakaja.

He told the Senate Committee chaired by Homa Bay Senator Moses Kajwang that the Sh118 billion in pending bills was inherited from his predecessors and that he had constituted a committee to undertake an internal verification of the entire amount before payments were done.

Sakaja explained that the verification established that the reduction was not solely through payments but also involved adjustments arising from legal assessments, suspended government-guaranteed loans, court decisions and disputed claims.

“I would like to inform Senators that my administration has provided a detailed schedule accounting for the Sh43.73 billion pending bills reduction through adjustments and reconciliations,” he said.

The governor said that of this amount Sh1.63 billion related to legal assessments, while Sh19.14 billion represented government-guaranteed loans whose servicing had been suspended due to a lack of supporting documentation and loan schedules.

Sakaja told Senators that Sh19.2 billion related to LAPFUND interest and penalties which the County said had been reduced following a court consent that brought the claim down to approximately Sh8.2 billion.

He said that they had provided a signed indemnity form, in accordance with County Treasury rules governing misplaced payment documents, alongside a financial memo confirming that the works had been undertaken and payment made.

“The audit further raised concerns over Sh16.04 million in receivables from non-exchange transactions, which lacked sufficient supporting documentation,” said Sakaja.

The governor told senators that beyond the verification of pending bills his administration had also strengthened the county’s legal department to reduce expenditure on external legal services and protect public resources.

Sakaja noted that through the reforms, Nairobi saved approximately Sh8.48 billion in legal costs over two financial years by expanding its in-house legal capacity, handling more litigation internally and negotiating reductions in legal fees claimed by private advocates.

According to the County Assembly’s Justice and Legal Affairs Committee, of the 174 court cases concluded during the period under review, 84 were handled by the County’s in-house legal team, with 47 determined in Nairobi’s favour, representing a 56 per cent success rate.

Kajwang, commended the County for reducing its pending bills but asked the Governor to provide additional documentation supporting the payments and processes undertaken to account for the Sh43.73 billion reductions.

“The Senate County Public Accounts Committee requires further clarification on the verification exercise and the adjustments made to the outstanding debt,” said Kajwang.
