MTN Nigeria, a leading Nigerian mobile operator, told him he used it, he says. —Next. He says a meeting with the operators is set for Wednesday 18 November 2026 at the Federal High Court in Abuja, Nigeria’s capital. —As of 14 November 2026, 17:37 GMT

Kel Armstrong Amobi, a Nigerian podcaster who hosts the KaaTruths Podcast, says more than 150GB of his mobile data disappeared. He announced on Saturday 14 November 2026, on the social network X, that he will take MTN Nigeria and other mobile operators to court.

What the Podcaster Says

Amobi, who goes by the nickname KAA, announced on X on Saturday 14 November 2026 that he will sue MTN Nigeria and other operators. By his own account, more than 150GB of his data disappeared, including 20GB within eight minutes while his data was switched off.

Amobi says MTN replied publicly on X that he had used the data, and that a later callback, after an MTN agent apologised and said she would escalate the case, put his use that day at 30GB on Google services and 19GB on YouTube. He disputes this: he says he was in a hotel meeting in Abuja, YouTube used 2% of his battery and about 20 minutes of screen time, and his iPhone’s usage logs show 23.8GB of YouTube use over 10 months.

File photo. The National Mosque in Abuja, Nigeria’s capital.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on MTN Nigeria Email address Follow

The Court Date and an Earlier Suit

Amobi says he and other parties will meet the operators at the Federal High Court in Abuja, a national trial court, on Wednesday 18 November 2026. That date is his statement, and we have not seen a court listing for it.

A separate suit at the same court, case FHC/ABJ/CV/886/2026, was brought by KaaTruths Podcast Ltd and a plaintiff listed as Ophoke Armstrong Amobi (KAA), whom we have not confirmed to be the same person, against MTN Nigeria Communications Plc, the phone operators Globacom and Airtel Networks, the pay-TV firm MultiChoice Nigeria and the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC, the consumer-protection regulator). It seeks N50 billion in damages (about US$37 million at N1,342 per US$, market rate on 13 November 2026) and cites a 75GB MTN bundle allegedly used up in under seven days, a claim separate from the 150GB complaint above.

The court had not decided the claims in that suit as of 14 November 2026, and the defendants are entitled to respond. MTN Nigeria said at an Abuja event on Monday 26 October 2026 that lost data comes from phone settings and app habits, as our report on that explanation covers.

What Is Not Known

MTN Nigeria has not published a response to this claim that we could find as of 14 November 2026. We have not read his post ourselves, so his account is given as his own public statement, and it is not stated whether the 18 November meeting belongs to the earlier case or whether any new suit has been filed.

What It Means for You

The people affected are Nigerian mobile users, counted in our report on Nigeria’s telecom subscribers. MTN Nigeria is majority-owned by MTN Group, a South African telecom company, and our Nigeria news hub carries further coverage.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Amobi claiming against MTN?

Amobi says more than 150GB of his mobile data disappeared, including 20GB in eight minutes. He announced on X on 14 November 2026 that he will sue.

What does MTN say?

MTN Nigeria has not published a response to this claim that we could find as of 14 November 2026. In Amobi’s account, it earlier said publicly on X that he had used the data.

When is the court meeting?

Amobi says a meeting with the operators is set for Wednesday 18 November 2026 at the Federal High Court in Abuja. We have not seen a court listing confirming that date.

Sources Kel Armstrong Amobi’s public statements of 14 November 2026 · Federal High Court, Abuja, case FHC/ABJ/CV/886/2026 (earlier suit)

World.title: Mauritius Group Owner Profit Up 49%
World.content:
Key Facts —What. CIEL Limited, a Mauritian group, lifted profit to its owners 49% in July to September 2026. —Group. Profit after tax rose 42% to MUR 1,090M (US$23.1M); MUR means Mauritian rupees. Free daily brief — no card needed Get every Africa story in one morning email We build you a personalized brief around the topics you follow — free for 7 days. Love it? Your first month after that is US$1. Start my free brief Yes, email me my free daily brief — I can unsubscribe any time. —Helped by. A MUR 63M (US$1.3M) gain on selling an asset and a MUR 91.6M (US$1.9M) loan-loss release. —Not known. No dividend figure, no full-year guidance numbers and no confirmed date for the next results. —As of 14 November 2026, 17:37 GMT

Mauritius’s CIEL Limited, a listed investment group with hotels, a bank and hospitals, reported a sharp profit rise for July to September 2026. Group profit after tax reached MUR 1,090M (US$23.1M), but the part that belongs to CIEL’s own shareholders was MUR 529M (US$11.2M).

What Happened

CIEL Limited, a Mauritian investment holding group listed on the Stock Exchange of Mauritius, published its results for the quarter on Friday 13 November 2026. Its board approved the unaudited figures that day, the company’s notice of 13 November 2026 says.

CIEL’s financial year ends on 30 June, so July to September 2026 is the first quarter of its 2027 financial year. The comparison is the quarter ended 30 September 2025, and CIEL converts rupees at MUR 47.17 per US$ on average for the quarter and at MUR 45.62 for the year-earlier quarter, and balance-sheet items at MUR 47.76 on 30 September 2026.

Revenue rose 6% to MUR 9,888M (US$209.6M) from MUR 9,285M (US$203.5M), CIEL’s earnings release of 13 November 2026 says. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, amortisation and expected credit losses, known as EBITDA, jumped 29% to MUR 2,059M (US$43.7M).

Profit attributable to CIEL’s owners rose 49% to MUR 529M (US$11.2M) from MUR 355M (US$7.8M), the release says. The other MUR 562M (about US$11.9M) goes to minority shareholders in subsidiaries, and earnings per share were MUR 0.31 (about US$0.007).

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Mauritius Email address Follow

Hotels and Banking Lead the Gain

Mauritius is a tourist island and a financial centre, and CIEL’s hotel and finance clusters, its business groupings, drove the quarter. Hotels & Resorts revenue rose 15% to MUR 2.4 bn (US$50.7M), the release of 13 November 2026 says.

File photo. A cruise ship and coast guard vessels in Port Louis harbour, Mauritius.

Hotel EBITDA climbed to MUR 643M (US$13.6M) from MUR 374M (US$8.2M), a gain of MUR 269M (US$5.7M). Revenue per available room, a standard hotel yardstick, rose 11.3% at Sunlife, a hotel business in CIEL’s cluster, while revenue at Riveo, a CIEL hotel company, more than doubled as its Four Seasons hotel traded for the full quarter after being closed a year earlier, the company says.

Finance, mainly BNI Madagascar, a bank, grew revenue 8% to MUR 1.8 bn (US$37.6M). Finance EBITDA rose 23% to MUR 772M (US$16.4M), according to the release of 13 November 2026.

Healthcare revenue rose 7% to MUR 1.7 bn (US$36.8M), with EBITDA up 16% to MUR 400M (US$8.5M) in Uganda and Mauritius. Property revenue rose 2.2 times to MUR 215M (US$4.6M), while Textile, CIEL’s textile cluster, slipped to a loss after tax of MUR 29M (US$0.6M) from a MUR 22M profit, on revenue down 2% to MUR 3.7 bn (US$78.9M).

More island coverage sits in our Mauritius news hub.

How Clean Is the Profit

CIEL itself says that certain items supported the quarter. Its outlook states: “While certain items supported the first-quarter result, the underlying performance of the portfolio remains positive.”

Finance EBITDA includes a MUR 63M (US$1.3M) profit on the disposal of MITCO, an asset that CIEL sold. The company also booked an expected credit loss release of MUR 91.6M (US$1.9M), provisions for bad loans no longer needed, mainly at BNI Madagascar.

A year earlier that release was MUR 2.8M (about US$0.06M), CIEL’s 13 November 2026 release shows. Profit from associates and joint ventures, firms CIEL part-owns, fell 37% to MUR 95.8M (US$2.0M) from MUR 152.9M (US$3.3M).

Cash, Debt and Valuation

Net interest-bearing debt stood at MUR 16.6 bn (US$346.6M at the closing rate) on 30 September 2026, with gearing, CIEL’s debt ratio, easing to 29.4% from 29.6% at 30 June 2026. Free cash flow, cash from operations after working capital and maintenance spending but before project spending, rose to MUR 1,340M (US$28.4M) from MUR 600M (US$13.2M).

CIEL says higher working capital of MUR 394M (US$8.4M) in its woven textile business in India lifted debt. The MUR 259M (US$5.5M) paid for Roswell Hospital in Kampala, Uganda’s capital, added to it.

Group chief financial officer Issam Sarkis said on 13 November 2026: “This quarter reflects the adaptability of our portfolio, with stronger profitability and cash generation giving us the capacity to keep investing with discipline while responding to opportunities as they emerge.” CIEL sees “encouraging momentum across most of its businesses”, and the share price of Sun Limited, a hotel company in its portfolio, rose 10% between 30 June and 30 September 2026, the release says.

In Plain English EBITDA is operating profit before interest, tax and certain accounting charges. Gearing is CIEL’s debt ratio. Minority shareholders, formally non-controlling interests, are outside owners of CIEL’s subsidiaries. They receive MUR 562M (about US$11.9M) of the quarter’s profit.

What Is Not Known

The release gives no dividend figure and no full-year guidance numbers. It also gives no date for the next results.

Date not confirmed: CIEL’s half-year results to 31 December 2026 have no scheduled date in the sources we used. We therefore name no dated checkpoint.

What It Means for You

For investors in Mauritian stocks, the quarter shows hotels and banking pulling ahead, though CIEL itself says certain items helped. The mechanism is hotels: Hotels & Resorts EBITDA rose by MUR 269M (US$5.7M) as Riveo, a CIEL hotel company, traded a full quarter, and free cash flow of MUR 1,340M (US$28.4M) against MUR 600M a year earlier gives CIEL room to invest, CIEL’s release of 13 November 2026 says.

There is no direct US consequence, because CIEL is listed in Mauritius. The nearest effect falls on any US investor who holds Mauritian shares.

Frequently Asked Questions

What profit did CIEL make in the quarter?

Profit after tax was MUR 1,090M (US$23.1M), up 42%. Profit attributable to CIEL’s owners was MUR 529M (US$11.2M), up 49%.

Why are there two profit figures?

The larger figure covers the whole group, including subsidiaries that CIEL does not fully own. The smaller one is the share that belongs to CIEL’s own shareholders, after MUR 562M (about US$11.9M) goes to minority holders.

Did one-off items help the result?

CIEL says certain items supported the quarter, including a MUR 63M (US$1.3M) disposal profit on MITCO. It also booked a MUR 91.6M (US$1.9M) expected credit loss release.

Does this affect US readers directly?

Not directly, since CIEL is listed in Mauritius. US investors who hold Mauritian shares are the group most affected.

Sources CIEL Limited earnings release for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 (cielgroup.com) · CIEL notice of 13 November 2026 (cielgroup.com)

World.title: Peru Calls Itself Land of Pope Leo
World.content:
Peru

Peru’s government has declared the whole country the “Land of Pope Leo XIV” in a Supreme Decree, a top-level government order, signed by President Keiko Fujimori. The honour comes as the first US-born pope, Robert Prevost of Chicago, is on his apostolic visit, an official papal trip, to Peru from Wednesday 11 to Monday 16 November 2026, which began when he landed in Lima.

The decree also gives the northern city of Chiclayo the title “Pueblo Fiel”, or Faithful People, because the Pope once served there as bishop. For readers abroad, it shows a government turning a papal visit into a national tribute.

Key Facts —Decree. Supreme Decree No. 017-2026-JUS, from Peru’s Justice Ministry, names Peru “Tierra del Papa León XIV”. —Chiclayo. The northern city in the Lambayeque region receives the honorary title “Pueblo Fiel”, meaning Faithful People. —Basis. The decree cites more than 40 years of ties between Robert Prevost and the Peruvian people. —Cost. The Justice Ministry must run its programmes within its own budget, and the decree adds no new money. —As of. Saturday, 14 November 2026, 17:45 GMT

The decree is a tribute rather than a policy, adding a title and a task for the Justice Ministry. It comes as the Pope’s visit moves toward its final Mass in Lima.

What We Know

Supreme Decree No. 017-2026-JUS, issued by the Justice Ministry, declares the Republic of Peru “Tierra del Papa León XIV”, Spanish for Land of Pope Leo XIV. It does so “in homage and solemn testimony of the Nation’s gratitude” for “more than forty (40) years of pastoral, civic and community ties” between Robert Prevost and the Peruvian people.

The decree notes that he embraced Peruvian nationality in 2015. It adds that he has devoted his priestly, episcopal and apostolic ministry “especially to vulnerable populations”.

Latin America Power Index · November 2026 edition Peru ranks 5th of 14 with 53.9 points. Strongest pillar: military means (71); weakest: future resources (37). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The text calls him “un ciudadano ilustre del mundo”, an illustrious citizen of the world. President Keiko Fujimori signed it with Luis Fernando Galarreta Velarde, President of the Council of Ministers (prime minister), and Ernesto Julio Álvarez Miranda, Minister of Justice and Human Rights.

Chiclayo’s cathedral seen from the Plaza de Armas, pictured in 2017. Photo: Pitxiquin / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

In Plain English —Supreme decree. A government order signed by the president and ministers. —Pueblo Fiel. Spanish for Faithful People, the new honorary title for Chiclayo. —Urbi et orbi. Latin for “to the city and the world”, the pope’s formal address. —El Peruano. Peru’s official gazette, where state decrees are published.

Free download · Expat checklist Get the free checklist as PDF Moving to Peru 2026: the step-by-step checklist. This guide condensed into 2 printable pages with tick boxes and the key official links. Email address Get the PDF Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

Why Chiclayo Gets a Title

The decree grants Chiclayo, a city in the Lambayeque region of northern Peru, the honorary title “Pueblo Fiel”. It does so “in commemoration of having been the home, episcopal seat and community of life” of the Pope.

The decree says this ratifies a name the Pope himself gave the Diocese of Chiclayo. He used it in his first urbi et orbi address after he was elected the 267th pope on 8 May 2025.

The title joins the older honour “Heroica Ciudad de Chiclayo” (Heroic City of Chiclayo), granted by decree on 15 April 1835. Together they form the protocol name “Heroica Ciudad y Pueblo Fiel de Chiclayo”, the decree says.

Before his election, Robert Prevost served as bishop of Chiclayo. Our report on Friday’s Mass in Pimentel, near Chiclayo, covers that visit.

What the Justice Ministry Must Do

Article 6 of the decree tells the Justice Ministry to promote actions, forums and programmes, in coordination with competent entities. They are to spread the values of social solidarity, defence of vulnerable groups and civic fraternity that inspired his community work in Peru.

The decree says the ministry must do this “at the expense of their own institutional budgets”. Our report on how Peru funds the visit covers the separate cost of the trip itself.

Why It Matters

Chiclayo and the people of Lambayeque gain a formal title, and the Justice Ministry gains a mandate to run programmes on its existing budget. The decree, issued in November 2026, puts the Pope’s ties to Peru at more than 40 years.

For readers in the United States, Robert Prevost was born in Chicago and is the first US-born pope. The step is symbolism rather than policy, and as reported it changes no law.

The Pope’s Saturday in Peru

Today, Saturday 14 November, the Pope celebrates Mass in Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, in the Cajamarca region. He then returns to Chiclayo to close the jubilee year of Saint Turibius of Mogrovejo, a 16th-century archbishop of Lima.

Our report on the Santa Cruz Mass gives the start as 11:00 Peru time. That equals 11:00 a.m. US Eastern.

What to Watch Next

According to details El Peruano reported on 29 October 2026, the visit closes with a Mass on Monday 16 November at the Las Palmas Air Base in Surco, a district of Lima. It starts at 10:30 Peru time, or 10:30 a.m. US Eastern, and more than one million faithful are expected.

According to the same report, public entry opens from 22:00 on Sunday 15 November through 14 perimeter gates under the control of the National Police, Peru’s national police force. After a farewell ceremony at the Callao air base near Lima, the Pope’s plane leaves for Rome at 13:45 Peru time on Monday 16 November.

What It Means for You

The people of Chiclayo and the Lambayeque region receive the title, and the Justice Ministry receives the instruction to promote its values. Catholic readers in the United States may note that the first US-born pope is honoured by a country whose nationality he chose.

What Is Not Known

The decree was signed in Lima on Friday 13 November 2026 and published in the gazette on Saturday 14 November. Its text names no budget figure and no deadline for the Justice Ministry’s programmes.

As reported, the decree attaches no money, law changes or new rights, and it gives no budget figure. We found no named public critic of the decree.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Peru declare?

Peru declared itself “Tierra del Papa León XIV”, or Land of Pope Leo XIV, in Supreme Decree No. 017-2026-JUS. The decree cites more than 40 years of ties between Robert Prevost and the Peruvian people.

What does Pueblo Fiel mean?

Pueblo Fiel means Faithful People. The decree gives Chiclayo the honorary title because the city was the Pope’s home and episcopal seat.

Does the decree create new spending?

The decree tells the Justice Ministry to promote its programmes at the expense of its own institutional budget. The text names no budget figure.

When does the Pope leave Peru?

According to El Peruano and the Vatican itinerary, his plane leaves for Rome at 13:45 Peru time on Monday 16 November. A farewell ceremony at the Callao air base comes first.

Sources: El Peruano, official gazette of Peru (Supreme Decree No. 017-2026-JUS), El Peruano report on the Las Palmas Mass, 29 October 2026.

World.title: Mayagüez Man Shoots Wife, Then Dies
World.content:
Puerto Rico

A 55-year-old man shot his wife and then took his own life in Mayagüez, Puerto Rico, early on Saturday 14 November 2026, the Puerto Rico Police said. The woman survived and is in stable condition in hospital.

Puerto Rico is a US territory, and its residents are US citizens. The Puerto Rico Police, the island’s police force, says its detectives are now investigating.

Key Facts —What. A man, 55, shot his wife in the thigh, then took his own life during talks with police. —Where. A home in the Parcelas Soledad area of Mayagüez, a city on Puerto Rico’s west coast. —Her condition. Stable at the Mayagüez Medical Center, where police took her after he let her leave. —Case status. The Criminal Investigations Corps, the police detective unit, is investigating. —As of. Saturday 14 November 2026, 17:45 GMT (12:45 p.m. Eastern Time)

The man let his wife leave the home while police talked with him. He died during those talks, after she was already receiving care.

What We Know

The incident at a home in the Parcelas Soledad residential area was reported to police at about 12:15 a.m. local time on Saturday 14 November. Inspector Joel González, director of the Criminal Investigations Corps (CIC) in Mayagüez, told reporters that morning.

He said the man fired several shots at his wife and hit her in the thigh. The man, 55, worked for an electricity company, according to the police account.

A Puerto Rico beach, file photo, not from the scene. Photo: Arturo Donate / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Puerto Rico Police Email address Follow

How the Night Unfolded

The police say the couple had been at a business together, and an argument began after they returned home. The woman tried to get into a vehicle, and the man fired several shots at her, the police said.

He then took her back into the home by force, the police said on 14 November. When officers arrived, they began to talk with him.

He let the woman leave, and police took her to a hospital in the area, the Mayagüez Medical Center. She is in stable condition with a bullet wound to the thigh, the police said.

During the talks, the man took his own life, the police said. The Puerto Rico Police has not released the woman’s name.

In Plain English —CIC. The Criminal Investigations Corps, the police detective unit for the Mayagüez area.

The Investigation

The Criminal Investigations Corps is investigating the case. Investigators are seeking security-camera recordings from the home.

The police account describes an argument that ended in a shooting at the couple’s home. The man died during the talks with officers.

What to Watch Next

The police have not announced further briefings, and no court or hearing date is known. Any new details would come from the Puerto Rico Police, with dates not confirmed.

What It Means for You

The case directly affects the woman and her family in Mayagüez. Puerto Rico residents are US citizens, so US readers with ties to the island may know people affected.

If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, or call Línea PAS at 1-800-981-0023. Línea PAS is the crisis line run by the Mental Health and Addiction Services Administration (ASSMCA), open around the clock, free and confidential.

What Is Not Known

The police have not said who the woman is, or how she is doing beyond “stable” at the time of the briefing on 14 November. They did not say whether any charges or protective orders existed earlier.

The exact number of shots is not known, and neither is what the camera recordings show. Further details may follow.

For related reporting, see our report on two women’s deaths under investigation on 12 November. More coverage is on our Puerto Rico news page and in our story on a bill to hire retired police.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happened in Mayagüez?

A 55-year-old man shot his wife in the thigh at a home in Mayagüez early on Saturday 14 November 2026, the Puerto Rico Police said. He then took his own life during talks with officers.

Where did it happen?

The shooting took place at a home in the Parcelas Soledad area of Mayagüez, a city on Puerto Rico’s west coast. The incident was reported to police at about 12:15 a.m. local time.

How is the woman?

Police say she is in stable condition at the Mayagüez Medical Center. They have not released her identity or further medical details.

Is anyone charged, and is the case under investigation?

The man died during the talks with officers, and police have announced no charges. Police are investigating and are seeking security-camera recordings from the home.

Sources: Puerto Rico Police Bureau (Negociado de la Policía de Puerto Rico), police briefing by the CIC Mayagüez director, 14 November 2026; ASSMCA Línea PAS.

World.title: Venezuela Hate Law Rewrite Still Has Fines
World.content:
VENEZUELA · POLITICS

Key Facts The bill Venezuela’s National Assembly passed a rewrite of its 2017 hate-speech law in first debate on 3 November.

The objection Opposition deputy Stalin González said on 13 November that fines still punish opinions.

The change Prison terms become fines for most offences; the Interior Ministry would impose them.

Next step A second debate is required; no date has been published.

As of 14 November 2026, 17:30 GMT (12:30 p.m. US Eastern).

Power Index Venezuela ranks 12th of 14 in Venezuela ranks 12th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 29.4 points (November 2026 edition).

Venezuela would swap prison terms for fines for most offences in its hate-speech law, but an opposition leader says the fines keep the law’s sting.

Published Saturday, 14 November 2026, 12:30 p.m. ET · Source: Venezuela’s National Assembly (first-discussion bill), Supreme Court Constitutional Chamber ruling 1,034, Foro Penal; El Diario and Monitoreamos (dated below)

Venezuela’s plan to soften its 2017 “Law Against Hatred” still lets the government punish speech, opposition deputy Stalin González said on Friday, 13 November. The bill removes prison terms for most offences but keeps administrative sanctions, which are fines imposed by officials rather than judges.

Alignment group: Closer to Beijing. Some pillar data are incomplete for Venezuela; see the index notes. WatchSovereign in selective default; inflation of 252%; public debt at 309% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

González leads the Libertad bloc, a group of opposition deputies, in a National Assembly controlled by the ruling chavista movement (the political camp built by the late President Hugo Chávez). He spoke at the fourth public hearing on the bill, held at the Central University of Venezuela in Caracas, according to the Venezuelan outlet Monitoreamos on 13 November.

What We Know

The Assembly approved the reform in first discussion on Tuesday, 3 November, according to the Caracas outlet El Diario. Acting president Delcy Rodríguez had asked for it on 29 September, saying it would decriminalise some conduct covered by the law.

On 15 October the Supreme Court’s Constitutional Chamber (ruling 1,034) found the draft consistent with the Constitution, according to the legal group Acceso a la Justicia. The same ruling says the Assembly needs two-thirds of its members to approve the change.

The law was issued in November 2017 by the Constituent Assembly, a body then-president Nicolás Maduro created that year, and it set long prison terms, up to 20 years, for inciting hatred. The bill drops “hate” from the title and replaces prison with administrative sanctions for most offences, according to El Diario’s report of 3 November on the text.

Fines would run from 500 to 10,000 times the central bank’s published rate of its highest-value currency, El Diario reported on 3 November. The press-freedom group Espacio Público called them disproportionate and put the ceiling at about €10,000 (about US$11,000, at the latest EUR/USD rate of 1.10 from RT, a market-data provider).

File photo. A corridor of the Aula Magna hall at the Central University of Venezuela in Caracas. The 13 November hearing took place at the university’s botanical garden auditorium. photo. A corridor of the Aula Magna hall at the Central University of Venezuela, Caracas, 2009. Photo: Trinitro Tolueno, CC BY 2.0, Wikimedia Commons.

Why It Matters

Foro Penal, a Venezuelan legal-aid group, said on 30 September that at least 927 people have been accused of inciting hatred since 2017. Six remain in detention and 638 face court-ordered restrictions, it said.

If the fines stay, the same law could still silence critics, journalists and broadcasters, only through a ministry instead of a court. Espacio Público says sanction procedures would sit with the Ministry of Interior, Justice and Peace, which is part of the government.

González said his bloc wants any remaining sanctioning article removed, in his words “no estamos de acuerdo con las sanciones, ni las administrativas” (we do not agree with sanctions, not even administrative ones). He also called the choice between full repeal and reform a “trampa” (trap).

The Government’s Case

Jorge Rodríguez, president of the Assembly, said on 3 November that the ruling movement wants to be sure the law is not used for “la persecución de nadie” (the persecution of anyone). He argued a coexistence law is still needed, according to El Diario.

The bill also lifts the loss of electoral registration for parties and deletes fines of 3% to 4% of income for broadcasters. Two journalists’ groups, the National Press Workers’ Union (SNTP) and the National Journalists’ Association (CNP), which want the law repealed outright, say the changes do not go far enough.

What To Watch

The bill is now in public consultation led by a special commission, and the Assembly must hold a second discussion before it becomes law. No date for that vote or for the next hearing has been published.

González said “veremos cuando la comisión hable” (we will see when the commission speaks). Watch whether the final text keeps administrative fines at all, the point González disputes.

What Is Not Known

The vote count in first discussion was not published, and the full bill text was not available to us. Which unit inside the Ministry of Interior, Justice and Peace would impose the fines is not yet specified.

What It Means for You

For readers outside Venezuela, the test is practical: whether people there can criticise the government without facing an official penalty. Anyone with relatives, business partners or sources in Venezuela should expect the rules on public speech to stay uncertain until the second debate.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Venezuela’s Law Against Hatred?

A 2017 law issued by the Constituent Assembly that punishes inciting hatred, discrimination or violence with up to 20 years in prison. Critics say it has been used against opponents and journalists.

What does the reform change?

It replaces prison terms with administrative fines for most offences, deletes some penalties for parties and broadcasters, and renames the law. The Assembly passed it in first discussion on 3 November.

Who is Stalin González?

He heads the Libertad bloc of opposition deputies in the National Assembly. On 13 November he said his bloc opposes keeping even administrative sanctions.

When will the reform become law?

That is not yet known. A second discussion is required, and no date has been published.

Sources: Supreme Court Constitutional Chamber ruling 1,034 of 15 October 2026 (https://accesoalajusticia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/SC-1034-151026.pdf); Foro Penal (a Venezuelan legal-aid group) figures of 30 September 2026 (https://eldiario.com/2026/09/30/acusaciones-incitacion-odio-venezuela/); El Diario, 3 November 2026 (https://eldiario.com/2026/11/03/an-aprobo-proyecto-de-ley-de-reforma-de-la-ley-contra-el-odio/) and 29 September 2026 (https://eldiario.com/2026/09/29/reforma-ley-contra-odio/); Monitoreamos, 13 November 2026 (https://monitoreamos.com/venezuela/stalin-gonzalez-reforma-ley-contra-el-odio-sanciones-administrativas).

World.title: Colombia Arrests Suspect Said to Fake Death
World.content:
COLOMBIA · SECURITY

Key Facts The arrest Soldiers captured alias “Primo Gay” in Briceño, Antioquia, on Saturday, 14 November 2026.

The suspect Néider Yesid Uñates López, aged 24, who authorities say led a unit in the armed group of Calarcá, a FARC dissident leader.

The case He is wanted for aggravated homicide and conspiracy; no court has ruled.

Reward The Defence Ministry had offered up to 640 million pesos (about US$194,000) for information.

As of 14 November 2026, 17:30 GMT (12:30 p.m. US Eastern).

Power Index Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 51.1 points (November 2026 edition).

Colombian soldiers have captured a 24-year-old suspect who authorities say led a unit of a FARC dissident group, survived a March raid and was reported to have turned on his own front.

Published Saturday, 14 November 2026, 12:30 p.m. ET · Source: Colombian Presidency, Ministry of Defence and Army statements, Fiscalía

Colombian soldiers captured the man known as alias “Primo Gay” on Saturday, 14 November 2026, in the village of Santa Ana in Briceño, a rural town in the north-western state of Antioquia. President Abelardo de la Espriella announced the arrest on X, and El Tiempo, a Bogotá daily, named the suspect as Néider Yesid Uñates López, aged 24.

Latin America Power Index · November 2026 edition Colombia ranks 6th of 14 with 51.1 points. Strongest pillar: military means (91); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (28). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The Gaula Militar, the Army’s anti-kidnapping and extortion unit, made the arrest with the Army’s Seventh Division, a regional command, the National Police and the Attorney General’s Office (Fiscalía), La FM, a Colombian radio network, reported on 14 November. Authorities say he led a unit of what they call FARC “dissidents”, a breakaway group from the rebel army that signed a peace deal with the state in 2016.

What We Know

Defence Minister Jorge Mora called the arrest “a forceful blow against narcoterrorism in Antioquia”, La FM quoted him as saying on 14 November. Army commander José Bertulfo Soto said the capture radically weakens the group’s chain of command, according to the same report.

EFE, the Spanish news agency, reported on 14 November that the man was wanted for aggravated homicide and aggravated criminal conspiracy. Two 9 mm pistols, magazines and ammunition were seized, and a second member of the group, his security chief, was also detained, La FM reported.

The president described those held as members of a “narcoterrorist structure” and said the man was linked to the laying of minefields and to attacks on the security forces. These are the authorities’ allegations, and the suspect has not been convicted of anything.

File photo. A Colombian Army Black Hawk helicopter; not from the Briceño operation.

Free download · Expat checklist Get the free checklist as PDF Moving to Colombia 2026: the step-by-step checklist. This guide condensed into 2 printable pages with tick boxes and the key official links. Email address Get the PDF Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

The Faked Death and the Calarcá Link

El Tiempo reported on 14 November that the suspect survived an Army raid in March 2026 in the hamlet of La Palestina, also in Briceño, and then spread photos suggesting he had died. Minuto30, a Colombian news site, wrote that authorities rejected that version at the time; his escort and a woman described as his partner were captured in that raid.

Authorities link him to the Estado Mayor de Bloques y Frentes (EMBF), a FARC splinter coalition led by alias “Calarcá”, a dissident leader. Sources disagree on his unit: EFE and the Defence Minister, as quoted by La FM, say substructure 5, while El Tiempo and Minuto30 say Front 36.

El Tiempo said intelligence reports from August 2026 suggested he had betrayed Calarcá’s front after a quarrel with a commander known as “Chejo” and joined the Clan del Golfo, a large drug-trafficking organisation. Minuto30 noted that this was never officially confirmed.

Why It Matters

Northern Antioquia is a mountain corridor where armed groups fight over drug routes, extortion of shopkeepers, ranchers and miners, and illegal mining. El Tiempo said the arrest followed a sustained offensive by the Army’s Fourth Brigade, an Army unit, and the Gaula, and described him as one of the most wanted leaders in northern Antioquia.

Residents of Briceño and nearby towns are the people most affected, because authorities link him to forced displacement and killings of soldiers and police in the area. The Defence Ministry had raised the reward for him to up to 640 million pesos (about US$194,000 at 3,302 pesos per dollar on 14 November), El Tiempo reported.

What To Watch

A judge is expected to rule on his custody; no hearing date had been announced. The Defence Ministry and the military leadership were also expected to give the official details at a news conference, El Tiempo said.

What Is Not Known

The exact hour of the arrest, the formal charges filed by the Fiscalía and the suspect’s own account were not public when we published. Whether he really betrayed Calarcá, and which unit he led, remain unconfirmed.

What It Means for You

Most visitors to Antioquia go to Medellín, the state capital, and we found no announcement of any change to travel conditions after the arrest. Anyone planning to visit the rural north should check the current advice from their own government.

Connected Coverage

Read our Colombia news hub and our earlier reports on the Guaviare air strike on a camp tied to Calarcá. See also Calarcá-linked attacks on soldiers before the election.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is alias Primo Gay?

Authorities identify him as Néider Yesid Uñates López, aged 24, accused of leading a unit of an armed group in northern Antioquia. He is a suspect, and no court has ruled on the allegations.

Where and when was he captured?

Soldiers captured him on Saturday, 14 November 2026, in the village of Santa Ana in Briceño, Antioquia, with the Army, police and prosecutors involved.

Who is Calarcá?

Alias “Calarcá” is a dissident leader who heads the Estado Mayor de Bloques y Frentes, a FARC splinter coalition. Reports say Primo Gay belonged to a unit under his command.

Did he really fake his death?

El Tiempo reported that he spread photos suggesting he had died after an Army raid in March 2026, and authorities rejected that version. Details of his motive were not confirmed.

Sources: Presidency of Colombia (President De la Espriella, post on X, 14 November 2026); Ministry of Defence and Army statements as quoted by La FM (https://www.lafm.com.co/orden-publico/gaula-militar-captura-alias-primo-gay-frente-36-calarca-antioquia-417223); EFE via Infobae (https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2026/11/14/detienen-a-alias-primo-gay-lider-de-una-disidencia-de-las-farc-en-el-noroeste-de-colombia/); El Tiempo, 14 November 2026 (https://www.eltiempo.com/colombia/medellin/de-adolescente-en-el-eln-a-disidente-y-narcoparamilitar-el-prontuario-de-alias-primo-gay-quien-habia-fingido-su-muerte-y-traiciono-a-calarca-3601093); Minuto30, 14 November 2026 (https://www.minuto30.com/capturado-primo-gay-uno-de-los-cabecillas-mas-buscados-de-antioquia/1730504/). World.title: Paraná River Floods Force 63 Families Out
World.content:
ARGENTINA · FLOODS

Key Facts Where Paraná River flooding in Entre Ríos, a province in north-east Argentina, with four towns past evacuation level.

Who The provincial Civil Defence emergency service counted 63 families out of their homes on 12 November: 56 in Paraná city, 7 in La Paz.

River Paraná city stood at 5.64 metres on Saturday morning; its evacuation level is 5.00 metres.

Next INA, the national water institute, expects Paraná city to reach 5.82 metres by mid-November and stay there to month-end.

As of 14 November 2026, 17:30 GMT (12:30 p.m. US Eastern).

Power Index Argentina ranks 4th of 14 in Argentina ranks 4th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 60.2 points (November 2026 edition).

The Paraná River is still rising in Argentina’s Entre Ríos province, and families are leaving riverside homes while the national water institute expects high water to last to the end of November.

Published Saturday, 14 November 2026, 12:30 p.m. ET · Source: Entre Ríos Civil Defence, the national water institute INA, the Argentine Coast Guard (Prefectura Naval)

The Paraná River, one of South America’s largest, is still rising in Argentina’s Entre Ríos province, and families are leaving riverside homes. Provincial Civil Defence said on 12 November that 63 families were out of their homes, 56 in the provincial capital Paraná and 7 in La Paz.

Latin America Power Index · November 2026 edition Argentina ranks 4th of 14 with 60.2 points. Strongest pillar: future resources (68); weakest: economic relationships (23). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (B-); inflation of 42%; public debt at 80% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

On 14 November the daily Diario Panorama reported that families in Paraná city were taking shelter in improvised camps as the water kept rising. We have no official count of those camps.

What We Know

Civil Defence reported on 12 November that four towns had passed their official evacuation levels: Paraná (5.49 metres against 5.00), La Paz (6.26 against 6.15), Hernandarias (6.32 against 6.00) and Diamante (5.61 against 5.50). Of the 56 families in Paraná city, 20 were at an official evacuation point at the Mirador de Bajada Grande, a riverside lookout, and 36 had left on their own.

The 7 La Paz families were also self-evacuated, the report said. The Argentine Coast Guard, Prefectura Naval, measured the Paraná at 5.64 metres in the city at 9 a.m. on 14 November, 9 centimetres higher than its first reading on Friday, according to the news site Elonce on 14 November.

The water institute INA, the state hydrology agency, expects the river to keep rising for about seven days, more slowly, as reported by Elonce. By 14 November the news site Elonce reported the Paraná at 6.30 metres at La Paz, 6.43 at Hernandarias and 5.74 at Diamante.

All three are above the evacuation levels Civil Defence listed on 12 November.

File photo. The National Flag Memorial in Rosario at dawn, with the Paraná River in the background. photo. The National Flag Memorial at dawn beside the Paraná River in Rosario, Santa Fe province, Argentina, 2015. Photo: Scarabinol, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Civil Defence (Argentina) Email address Follow

Why It Matters

The Paraná is the main waterway for Argentina’s farm exports, and Rosario, in Santa Fe province, is the hub of its soy industry. For US readers the direct effect is limited so far, and we found no report of port or shipment disruption.

The risk lies ahead if high water lasts to month-end, as INA expects.

What To Watch

For Paraná city, INA projects 5.82 metres by mid-November, holding to month-end, according to Elonce on 14 November. INA expects the rise to ease after about seven days and levels to stay near the peak for a further week.

What Is Not Known

We do not know how many people sleep in improvised camps, because no official count of them has been published. We also do not have a Civil Defence total dated 14 November.

What It Means for You

If you plan to travel to the Entre Ríos riverside towns, check local advice. Reports we reviewed did not mention flight, bridge or port closures.

Buyers of Argentine soy should follow INA updates for the Paraná. A shipping effect is possible but not reported.

Connected Coverage

Read the Argentina news hub for more coverage.

Frequently Asked Questions

How high is the Paraná River in Entre Ríos?

On Saturday, 14 November, the river stood at 5.64 metres at Paraná city at 9 a.m., according to the Argentine Coast Guard figures. The local evacuation level is 5.00 metres.

How many people have left their homes?

The provincial Civil Defence office counted 63 families on 12 November, 56 in Paraná city and 7 in La Paz. Newer official totals were not available when we published.

What do forecasters expect next?

The national water institute INA says the Paraná keeps rising for about seven days, more slowly, and then stays near its peak for a further week. It expects Paraná city to reach 5.82 metres by mid-November.

Sources: Entre Ríos Provincial Civil Defence report, 12 November 2026; national water institute INA (ina.gob.ar) forecasts; Argentine Coast Guard (Prefectura Naval) river readings. Named outlets: Elonce (12 and 14 November), Diario Panorama (14 November). Provincial and national agency pages: https://www.entrerios.gov.ar/ and https://www.ina.gob.ar/
