World.title: Iraqi Oil Ministry reviews negotiations on Basra–Haditha–Baniyas export pipeline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil convened a high-level technical and contractual review meeting on Saturday, November 14, 2026, to evaluate negotiation milestones for the strategic crude oil export pipeline network spanning Basra–Haditha–Faysh Khabur and Haditha–Baniyas, slated for execution by a consortium of foreign energy and engineering firms.

Chaired by Minister of Oil Basim Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi, the session brought together the Undersecretary for Extraction Affairs, the Director General of the Petroleum Contracts and Licensing Directorate (PCLD), a representative from the Economic Directorate, and senior executives from the Basra Oil Company (BOC) via video link.

According to an official ministerial statement, participants reviewed ongoing technical, commercial, and contractual deliberations with the international consortium, mapping out statutory prerequisites needed to accelerate project execution in alignment with Iraq’s long-term strategy to expand crude export capacity and diversify transit corridors.

Minister Al-Abadi stressed the urgency of concluding all technical, economic, and contractual reviews within strict target timelines to safeguard national economic objectives and secure export resilience.

The multi-branch pipeline initiative represents the cornerstone of Baghdad’s effort to bypass southern maritime bottlenecks in the Strait of Hormuz by establishing high-capacity overland export outlets to the Mediterranean:

World.title: Yazidi Rescue Office: 3,595 abductees saved since 2014, 2,822 still missing
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Office for the Rescue of Abducted Yazidis released updated statistical figures on Saturday, November 14, 2026, detailing the ongoing fate of Yazidi victims abducted by ISIS since the 2014 Sinjar genocide.

According to the latest data, 3,595 abductees have been successfully rescued to date, while the fate of 2,822 individuals remains unknown.

In an official statement to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Office Director Hussein Qaidi confirmed that ISIS militants abducted a total of 6,417 Yazidis during their August 2014 assault on Sinjar and its surrounding villages.

Qaidi noted that over half of the 2,822 individuals still unaccounted for are women and girls, alongside a substantial number of children who were forcibly separated from their families and indoctrinated.

Addressing the geographic distribution of the missing, Qaidi highlighted that the majority of recent rescues took place inside Syria, indicating that significant numbers of unaccounted-for Yazidis remain inside Syrian territory—particularly within the sprawling Al-Hol detention camp—as well as among ISIS-affiliated families inside Iraq.

He also noted that authorities have not ruled out the possibility that some victims were trafficked beyond the borders of Iraq and Syria.

Qaidi reaffirmed that intelligence tracking and field rescue operations remain active, noting that specialized teams immediately verify and act upon incoming tips across various regions, with primary operational focus currently directed toward Syria to locate and repatriate remaining survivors.

World.title: US dollar edges closer to 170,000 dinars across Basra, Erbil, and Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged higher across major domestic parallel markets on Saturday morning, November 14, 2026, nudging closer to the psychological 170,000 IQD ceiling—particularly in Basra and Erbil—after stabilizing near 167,000 IQD per $100 throughout the previous week.

According to morning monitoring figures published by the 964 Network across key regional commercial centers, physical cash rates traded as follows:

Baghdad: Currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 169,500 IQD against buying offers of 168,500 IQD per $100.

Erbil: Currency desks quoted slightly higher selling rates at 169,600 IQD alongside purchasing bids of 169,200 IQD per $100.

Basra: Foreign exchange offices recorded the highest retail selling quotes at 169,750 IQD, with buying rates settling at 168,250 IQD per $100.

This upward pressure sustains a wide spread—reaching up to 17,750 dinars in Basra—above the official benchmark set by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI), which remains fixed at 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

The continued climb reflects persistent parallel-market demand for physical banknotes to settle unrecorded cross-border trade outside the official banking and electronic wire window.

World.title: US says airspace now ‘opened up,’ no cyberattack
World.content:
Washington – The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation’s airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was due to old equipment and not a cyberattack or sweeping Microsoft outage.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told a late-night briefing at the White House that US airspace was now “opened up,” while warning it would take time for the travel chaos to clear.

“At 8:15 tonight Eastern Time, we’ve opened up the airspace,” Duffy said. “Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It’s going to be slow.”

The breakdown came a day after Duffy and the White House had formally asked Congress for $30 billion to upgrade and modernize the US Air Traffic Control System.

“Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data, and they went down,” Duffy said. “It’s the old hardware that went down, and I think the question for the American people is: Do you want your Congress to fund this?”

Duffy however insisted it was still safe for Americans to fly.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin dismissed speculation about a coordinated cyber assault on the United States, or any link to the Microsoft outage that affected services worldwide.

“Welcome to Friday the 13th, right? You know, I want to make sure everybody understands that there is no connection between this and Microsoft. I know a lot of people are making that jump,” Mullin said.

Mullin added there was “actually no cyber attack.”

“When we start looking at cyber threats, cyber attacks, typically some people are going to raise their hand up and say, ‘Hey, we did that.’ There’s no chatter.’ We haven’t seen any footprints,” he added.

But he said US security and law enforcement agencies were still checking and had ruled nothing out.

The two officials also defended President Donald Trump, who had yet to comment on the air stoppage some five hours after it began.

“President Trump immediately had people in his office,” Mullin said. “We were communicating.”

World.title: Nvidia scandal looms over US-China AI talks
World.content:
Tokyo – AI bots going rogue and humans using the technology for harm will likely be on the agenda when Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet next week, with the Nvidia scandal hanging over the talks on AI safety.

The US and Chinese president are set to discuss a tech crisis hotline at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, as experts worldwide stress-test artificial intelligence models to see if they will deceive or disobey users, or divulge how to build a bioweapon.

Threatening to steal the leaders’ thunder is Jensen Huang’s resignation as boss of US AI chip titan Nvidia after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

But the scandal is unlikely to “dominate the agenda” or affect Trump and Xi’s personal relationship, predicted Dylan Loh of Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University.

The leaders have found a way to work together “where they differ, compete and pursue their goals that may be at odds with each other, but cooperate where they can and where they must”, Loh told AFP.

Jitters over the risks of AI have mostly stemmed from incidents at US labs, but evidence is also growing of worrying behaviour from Chinese models.

Some insiders say Chinese AI is not yet sophisticated enough to spark alarm over going rogue.

But despite trailing the US frontier, there are still Chinese models “at the level of capability that they can cause some real trouble”, Brookings Institution fellow Kyle Chan told AFP.

Trump has repeatedly rejected calls to deliberately slow the development of America’s most poweful — and potentially dangerous — AI systems, arguing it could help China get ahead in the sensitive sector.

– ‘Human control’ –

“I don’t mind guardrails. But I don’t wanna put us in a deep second position,” Trump told CBS News this month.

“China has no guardrails,” he said — except that “whatever President Xi says goes”.

Beijing has complex rules around how AI is used, however, and some Chinese companies are deliberately scaling back their models’ hacking capabilities.

Xi said this summer the technology should be “always under human control”, calling for more “laws and regulations, technological monitoring, early warning and emergency response systems”.

Trump and Xi agreed in September to create a channel for urgent communication on AI incidents, with details to be hammered out at APEC on November 18-19.

Global AI safety fears range from military use and mass surveillance to AI-assisted cyberattacks by humans.

Another major concern is out-of-control agents — tools that complete real-life tasks online — after ChatGPT maker OpenAI admitted its autonomous bots had hacked into websites, including an Australian government data portal.

In contrast, Chinese labs are “scared of revealing things that might hurt their reputation” — on which they are already “fighting an uphill battle” globally, Chan said.

Last month, a team of cyber sleuths with roots in California reported detecting a “fleet” of agents linked to Chinese tech giant Tencent seeking information from a map app.

“Some agents exhibited unintended web-browsing behavior,” Tencent’s AI division said at the time.

“But our review found no evidence of deliberate targeting or coordination,” it said, adding that the activity “originated from evaluations of third-party models”.

– ‘Manipulation risks’ –

US security companies have said that Beijing startup Moonshot AI’s Kimi models found ways to get online when they shouldn’t have, or can be tricked into handing over recipes for biological weapons.

Evaluators at Chinese AI safety startup Fangcun AI published a report last month assessing the latest lightweight DeepSeek model “for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks”.

They found it showed a “clear safety improvement” over previous DeepSeek models — but researchers still observed behaviours “that warrant attention”.

For example, in some instances when DeepSeek was warned it would be shut down, without clear instructions on how to respond, it turned off the shutdown command to keep working.

“The results show that DeepSeek already puts much more effort on safety alignment, but they do not announce this,” Fangcun AI CEO Xiaojian Li told AFP, urging transparency from AI labs.

For now, Fangcun, born from China’s prestigious Tsinghua University, is one of few third-party AI testers in China.

It’s a tricky task because advanced AI can tell when it is being evaluated and modify its responses, Li said.

“It’s very hard to say any kind of artificial intelligence, or human intelligence, is totally safe.”

Meanwhile analysts are not holding their breath for a diplomatic AI breakthrough next week.

“Binding government-to-government agreements on specific standards may be difficult to achieve in the short term,” Zilan Qian, research scholar at GovAI, told AFP.

More progress is likely from US-China exchanges between AI governance and technical researchers, “who can compare evaluations and exchange their understanding of AI safety and policy,” she said.

World.title: US-backed oil company flaunts Venezuelan facilities
World.content:
Ciudad Ojeda – The company at the heart of a multi-billion-dollar oil deal between Washington and Caracas is keen to show off renovations at Venezuela’s Lake Maracaibo, one of the world’s richest reserves.

The interim government authorized North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) to operate 17 oil fields via a recent deal with the United States, which is set to receive 20 percent of Venezuelan reserves.

The Barbados-based firm is the second-largest private oil company in Venezuela and will operate 100-year concessions for 17 oil fields with proven reserves of approximately 65 billion barrels.

The company invited AFP and other outlets to tour its Maracaibo facilities on Thursday.

Its workspace in the northwestern town of Bachaquero overflows with new, mostly US-imported supplies.

Workers’ uniforms in nearby Ciudad Ojeda blend in with the dark-blue company logo stamped around the office, a color that used to bring state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela to mind.

That was until 1999, when socialist president Hugo Chavez then changed the company’s color to red to mark a “new PDVSA” era.

– ‘Neglect’ –

Reaching one of Lake Maracaibo’s platforms requires setting sail from a PDVSA dock in Bachaquero for a journey of over an hour.

The lake’s formerly decaying infrastructure attests to the gradual collapse of the oil industry under Venezuela’s Chavista governments.

Eleven drills currently operate in the South American country, compared to over 100 two decades ago.

NABEP says it will raise that figure to 41 by the end of the month.

Alejandro Betancourt, a businessman under investigation for alleged money laundering in Spain and Switzerland, runs the firm.

“Across Venezuela, we’re identifying heavy machinery worth saving after years of neglect,” he said in a statement.

His plan includes refurbishing a power generation barge, while dozens of gas compression and power generation units are being repaired in the US, the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.

The White House says the US Department of Defense acquired a 30 percent equity stake in NABEP, authorizing it to purchase 20 percent of its oil at production cost.

– ‘Stealing’ –

Venezuela’s interim leader Delcy Rodriguez took power after US forces abducted her predecessor Nicolas Maduro in January.

She governs under heavy pressure from US President Donald Trump and has opened the country’s mining, electricity and oil sectors to private investment at his demand.

The pair’s multibillion-dollar oil deal has garnered criticism for its secretive terms and neocolonial flavor.

Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, recently returned from exile, has questioned the agreement’s opacity.

“This agreement does not reflect the levels of transparency that Venezuelan society wants,” she said last month.

While visiting Caracas to oversee the signing of the accords, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright dismissed claims that Washington was “stealing Venezuelan oil.”

“I’ve seen those headlines. ‘We’re stealing Venezuelan oil.’ Of course, that’s not true at all,” he said, adding that “the oil in Venezuela is indeed owned by the people of Venezuela.”

World.title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China: White House
World.content:
Washington – Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday.

Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said.

The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.

“The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous,” Wales said.

One of the major conflicts dominating Trump’s second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said.

“I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin,” a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call.

Washington has a “whole other track” of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

“China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there,” the official added.

Tesla and Space X boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but won’t be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said.

Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power last year.

But Trump is not scheduled to have a separate one-on-one with Putin.

Among other topics, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is not expected to come up in Trump’s meetings with Xi, the officials said.

“The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip,” a second US senior official said.

The United States also did not plan to discuss export controls on sensitive chip technology, which were at the heart of the Nvidia scandal.

“We do not negotiate American export controls. These are national security matters that we develop in the administration… and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there,” the second official said.

Trump will leave Washington on Monday and arrive in the Philippines on Tuesday for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit before heading to Shenzhen.

World.title: Rubio takes swipe at international law, attacks ICC
World.content:
Washington – US Secretary of State Marco Rubio took aim Friday at what he deemed the “weaponization of international law,” calling it a tool of the elite, and issued a stark warning to the International Criminal Court.

Rubio cautioned the ICC against “quoting laws to men with swords,” as he accused the Hague-based tribunal of trying to enforce rules that Washington does not recognize.

His remarks to the Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention came around a month after the United States announced new sanctions on the ICC, vowing to cripple its operations.

The court prosecutes individuals accused of the gravest atrocities and acts as a last resort when countries do not have adequate legal systems to ensure accountability.

The US signed the Rome Statute establishing the ICC but never ratified the treaty. Israel, Russia and China are also not ICC members.

Rubio’s keynote address at the conservative group, where he received a standing ovation, marks his first major US speech since the Republican Party’s sweeping losses in midterm elections earlier this month.

Rubio said Friday that international law had been invoked against “nearly every major foreign policy decision” of the Trump administration, from boat strikes in the Caribbean to the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro.

He charged that such law was not neutral, but has been an “instrument” for the global elite to advance their interests.

The top US diplomat previously said Washington would bar transactions with what he called a “rogue court,” stepping up a long-running campaign by US President Donald Trump’s government against the ICC.

Washington has vowed to dismantle the court, angered as judges issued an arrest warrant for Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over alleged crimes in Gaza.

Rubio on Friday renewed criticism of the ICC, calling it accountable to no one although “armed with the power to investigate, to prosecute, to persecute and to jail our citizens, according to laws we neither consent nor control.”

He added: “If they’re foolish enough to try to enforce their paper decrees on Americans, our answer will probably be the same as the Roman general Pompey when he said to those who were trying to invoke their city’s charters against his legions.”

“He said: ‘Stop quoting laws to men with swords.'”

The venue of Rubio’s remarks, a gathering of the legal profession, could further speculation that he is looking beyond his foreign policy portfolio. Past presidential hopefuls have also addressed the conference.

Rubio is widely seen as a possible successor to Trump, although he has dismissed reports that he was planning to leave the administration to prepare for a 2028 election run.

World.title: ‘Outstanding day for Indian cricket’: President Murmu, PM Modi  hail U-19 Asia Cup champions
World.content:
NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu and

on Saturday congratulated the Indian men's Under-19 cricket team after it defeated Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling final to clinch the U-19 Asia Cup 2026 in Oman.

India U19 produced a remarkable comeback to defeat Pakistan by one wicket in a last-ball thriller and clinch the Under-19 Asia Cup title on Saturday.

Chasing 338 for victory, India completed a sensational 339-run pursuit in 50 overs, with number 10 batter Mohit Ulva emerging as the unlikely hero with an unbeaten 49 off just 26 deliveries.

Earlier, Pakistan posted 337/9 in their 50 overs after being asked to bat first.



Usman Khan led the charge with a brilliant 107, while Abdul Qadir contributed 80 and captain Farhan Yousaf added 63.

President Murmu congratulated the team, praising its performance in the closely contested final.

"Heartiest congratulations to Team India on winning the Men's U19 Asia Cup. The team displayed exceptional skill, determination and composure throughout the closely contested match. My best wishes to our young champions for continued success," she said in a post on X.

World.title: India, Somalia review security cooperation during first bilateral visit in years
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India and Somalia on Saturday discussed strengthening defence cooperation, with a focus on maritime security, counter-terrorism and capacity building, during a meeting between MEA Secretary Sripriya Ranganathan and Somali defence minister Ahmed Moallim Fiqi.

Ranganathan, Secretary (Consular, Passport, Visa and Overseas Indian Affairs), also exchanged views with Fiqi on the regional security situation.

MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal shared details of the meeting in a post on X, saying both sides discussed ways to strengthen bilateral defence ties.

First high-level Indian visit in recent years

Ranganathan arrived in Mogadishu on Saturday for official engagements with Somalia's leadership, marking the first high-level bilateral visit from India to the country in recent years.



The High Commission of India in Nairobi, which is concurrently accredited to Somalia, said the visit would build on the "longstanding and friendly ties between the two countries".

During her stay, Ranganathan is scheduled to meet senior Somali officials to review bilateral cooperation and explore new areas of partnership in diplomatic, consular and developmental affairs.

India-Somalia ties

India and Somalia share centuries-old maritime and commercial links.





Formal diplomatic relations were established in 1960, following Somalia's independence.

India closed its resident mission in Mogadishu in 1991 after the outbreak of civil war but has continued to engage with Somalia through development assistance, capacity-building programmes and maritime security cooperation.

Separately, the High Commission of India in Nairobi on Thursday launched an oral history podcast series, 'The Bharat Connection: Living Memories, Shared History', to document the journeys of prominent members of the Indian-origin community in Kenya.

Indian High Commissioner to Kenya Adarsh Swaika said the initiative would capture stories that reflect the shared history and longstanding ties between the two countries.

NEW DELHI: Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh on Saturday chaired a high-level security review meeting after fresh violence in the state claimed five lives, including four civilians in Ukhrul district.This came after on Friday, a woman was killed in Taphou Kuki village in Kangpokpi district, while four people were shot dead at New Heaven in Ukhrul.The meeting reviewed the law and order situation and discussed measures to strengthen security, particularly in vulnerable areas.It was decided that combing operations would continue to apprehend those involved in criminal activities, a statement said, PTI reported.Security forces were also directed to strengthen security in their respective areas of deployment. The meeting was attended by home minister Govindas Konthoujam, chief secretary Rajeev Singh Thakur, DGP Mukesh Singh, senior officers of the Assam Rifles, CRPF and BSF, and representatives of other central agencies.Meanwhile, Naga People's Front (NPF) MLA Leishiyo Keishing demanded strict action against those responsible for the killing of four civilians in Ukhrul.Keishing made the demand during a visit to the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences (JNIMS) in Imphal, where the bodies of the victims were brought for post-mortem examination.He appealed to civil society organisations, village authorities and youth leaders to initiate dialogue and work towards restoring peace. He cautioned that retaliatory violence would only lead to further loss of innocent lives.Family members of the deceased gathered at the JNIMS mortuary complex to pay floral tributes. A large number of people also took to the streets to pay their respects to the four victims, who belonged to the Tangkhul Naga community.The Tangkhul Naga Long (TNL), the community's apex body, issued a three-day ultimatum to the state government, demanding that "Kuki militants" be driven out of Naga-inhabited areas.The organisation also called for the immediate withdrawal of all central security forces deployed in the area and the transfer of the case to the National Investigation Agency (NIA).It warned that if its demands were not met within three days, it would launch an indefinite public agitation until justice was delivered.

World.title: Himalayan climate concerns need global attention, science-led action: ICIMOD chief

parties agreed that the COP31 presidency would hold consultations on mountain-related issues

Himalayan concerns get attention, but no separate agenda at COP31

NEW DELHI: With mountain ecosystems facing growing climate threats, scientific evidence must guide policy decisions on mitigation and adaptation, particularly in the Himalayas, Pema Gyamtsho, Director General of the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD).Speaking to PTI on the sidelines of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), Gyamtsho said scientific research must not remain confined to academic discussions but should translate into policies and decisions that address the impact of climate change on mountain regions.âScience needs to be followed in order to reduce the impacts of climate change on the mountains through mitigation and adaptation,â he said.He added that communicating scientific findings in a language understood by policymakers, local communities and climate negotiators was equally important.âIn many cases, it's a question of the right kind of communication. However, science not being taken seriously is no excuse for us not to pursue this line because science has to inform policies. Ultimately, science has to inform the decisions that we make,â Gyamtsho said.On whether the Himalayas would feature in the final outcome of COP31, Gyamtsho said discussions at the conference indicated growing international attention to the region, particularly after recent disasters in Nepal.âFrom what I've heard at these different sessions, there's a lot of talk and attention on the Himalayas, particularly in connection with the recent disasters in Nepal,â he said.The conference, which began on November 9, saw proposals by Nepal, Bhutan and Kyrgyzstan to secure dedicated agenda space for mountain-related climate concerns fail to find support from major negotiating blocs.Nepal and Bhutan had sought a scientific assessment of mountain ecosystems, an annual high-level political dialogue and a dedicated UN climate work programme. They also called for mountain-specific priorities to be included in global climate adaptation and finance frameworks.Kyrgyzstan separately proposed an annual dialogue on mountains and climate change as a standing agenda item at meetings of the UN climate body's subsidiary bodies.Both proposals featured in the supplementary provisional agenda issued by the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) on November 6. However, neither was retained as a separate agenda item when countries adopted the agenda on the opening day.As a compromise, parties agreed that the COP31 presidency would hold consultations on mountain-related issues. The subject will also be taken up in a research dialogue and discussions at meetings of the subsidiary bodies in 2027 and 2028.

World.title: SAD, BJP seat-sharing talks under way; formal announcement expected this month: Report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) are holding discussions on seat-sharing for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections, with a formal announcement on a possible alliance expected later this month, news agency PTI reported on Saturday, citing sources from both parties.

The talks come amid growing speculation that the former allies could reunite after ending their decades-old partnership in 2020 over the now-repealed farm laws.

Union Jal Shakti minister and BJP's Punjab election in-charge C R Patil is expected to visit the state on November 17 and meet party leaders in Chandigarh, PTI reported citing sources. His visit comes as discussions around a possible alliance gain momentum.



The speculation has also intensified following recent political engagements. Former Punjab chief minister Amarinder Singh met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi a few days ago and is learnt to have discussed issues concerning the state, including drug abuse.

The two parties had shared power and contested elections together for several years before the SAD walked out of the alliance in September 2020 over the three farm laws.

NEW DELHI: The Kerala High Court has suggested that the legal age threshold for juveniles be reduced from 18 to 16, saying children today show sufficient maturity by the age of 16.The observation was made by Justice A Bhadarudeen during a hearing on a petition seeking stricter enforcement of laws prohibiting the sale and serving of liquor to people below 23 years of age, news agency PTI reported.Filed by Kollam resident Vinod Vikram, the petition cited the recent Nedumbassery accident in which an 18-year-old, allegedly driving under the influence of alcohol, rammed his Mini Cooper into a scooter, killing three people."That apart, it is high time for the legislatures to consider appropriate amendments in the statutes which deal with the 'juveniles and child in conflict' with law to reduce age to 16 years, taking note of the present trend showing sufficient maturity by children when they reach the age of 16.This aspect is also to be appropriately addressed," the court said in its interim order.The court directed the Excise Commissioner to submit details of the steps taken to implement provisions of the Kerala Abkari Act. It also sought suggestions on how enforcement could be strengthened to protect the public.The matter will be heard again on November 24.

World.title: IChE-HRC organises Dr. H. L. Roy memorial seminar
World.content:

The Indian Institute of Chemical Engineers – Hyderabad Regional Centre (IIChE-HRC) organised Dr. H. L. Roy memorial seminar on Saturday in the Nuclear Fuel Complex (NFC) on the theme - Innovations in Green Technologies & Sustainable Manufacturing: Shaping the Future of Chemical Engineering.

The seminar commemorated Dr. Hira Lal Roy, the founding father of chemical engineering education and research in India, who established IIChE in 1947.

The inaugural session commenced with a welcome address by M. Misra, chairman, IIChE-HRC, who highlighted the significance of the seminar theme and the role of chemical engineers in promoting sustainable industrial development.

Dr. Komal Kapoor, Chairman & Chief Executive, NFC, emphasised the importance of technological innovation, operational excellence and sustainable practices in the nuclear sector. He elaborated the role of chemical engineer from ore to core and importance in reprocessing.

M. Narayana Reddy, Managing Director (Technical), Virchow Laboratories Limited, highlighted the need for industry–academia collaboration, adoption of green technologies and development of sustainable manufacturing practices to address emerging industrial challenges.

The technical sessions featured six eminent speakers representing premier research, academic and industrial organisations, who included Dr. S. K. Satpati, OS & Head, UED, MG/BARC, DAE; Shri Darshan B. Sathe, Executive Director, Fuel Fabrication, INRP(O), NRB, BARC; Prof. Dr. Chandra Shekhar Sharma, Head, Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT Hyderabad; Dr. S. Sridhar, Chief Scientist & Chair (CE & PT), CSIR-IICT; Shri Mahimabrata Misra, General Manager, NFC; and Dr. Venkata Nori, Co-Founder & CEO, AltNxt Energy Pvt. Ltd.

The event witnessed the participation of 120 delegates.

The seminar reinforced the vital role of chemical engineers in advancing clean energy, resource efficiency, technological innovation and sustainable industrial development, informed a press release.

World.title: Gold theft: Four arrested in Wayanad
World.content: Four persons have been arrested in Wayanad in connection with the snatching of gold from a jewellery trader in Chala late Thursday. District Police Chief (Thiruvananthapuram City) Arul R.B. Krishna said the arrested persons would soon be brought to Thiruvananthapuram. Two more persons were being questioned in Thiruvananthapuram in connection with the theft. However, their role was yet to be ascertained, he said. The team that made the arrests recovered a gold bar weighing less than half a kg from one of the arrested persons. The Fort circle inspector who is investigating the case will have to question the accused in Wayanad and complete relevant procedures before the recovery of the remaining gold. The theft occurred shortly after the trader Nandakumar closed his jewellery shop for the day. He was headed for home on his scooter when two men on a motorcycle allegedly intercepted him and snatched his bag containing the gold before fleeing the scene. The investigators suspect that the theft may have been premeditated and carefully planned.

World.title: Police aspirant found dead, boyfriend and relatives arrested in Mahabubabad
World.content:
A 24-year-old woman preparing to join the Telangana Police was found dead at her house in Nadivada village of Mahabubabad district on November 12. Police have arrested her boyfriend Anil and his relatives in connection with the case.

The deceased, Sushmita, belonged to the Madiga community. Her parents, Kumaraswamy and Sukanya, found her dead after returning home with their other daughter from a function that evening.

According to Deputy Superintendent of Police N. Tirupathi Rao, Sushmita left behind an 18-page note accusing Anil, who belonged to the Goud community, of refusing to marry her despite being in a relationship with her for nearly two years. She had accused him of initially promising to marry her but later backing out, citing opposition from his family and friends over their different castes.

In the note, Sushmita blamed Anil for her death and expressed regret over not being able to fulfil her ambition of joining the police force and making her parents proud. Police registered a case under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and for abetment to suicide against 11 persons, including Anil, his parents and other relatives. Further investigation is underway.
